"""Stage 5 (WP5): Module 8 assessment kit — KPI 3.1 hallucination quiz, KPI 3.2 confidence survey, three-tool lab, AI-use disclosure.
Drafted by Copilot; requires human review (ethical framework, item validity, AI-tool access at CUHK, privacy wording).

KPI 3.1 (proposal): “80% correct on a ten-question hallucination quiz”. The wording is ambiguous, so both readings are reported:
  (a) mean score ≥ 80%, and (b) ≥ 80% of completers score ≥ 8/10. Each item also records a 1–5 confidence rating (calibration).
KPI 3.2: “70% of users report increased confidence”. Measured two ways, both reported:
  (a) post-minus-pre change on a 6-item confidence scale (same items, Module 8 start and end): % with a positive change;
  (b) a post-only direct item (“Compared with before Module 8 …”): % answering “somewhat” or “much more confident”.
Quiz item: (id, domain, h_code, statement, options, key, why, topic)."""

QUIZ = [
 ('HQ1', 'Fabricated source', 'H5', 'AI: “According to a 2023 CUHK Registry report (doi:10.1016/j.cuhk.2023.0412), 38% of undergraduates use AI weekly.” You cannot find the DOI.',
  ['Accept: a DOI is given', 'Accept but add “(AI)” to the citation', 'Do not use it until you have opened the source yourself', 'Ask the AI to confirm the DOI is real'], 2,
  'A citation you cannot open is unverified. Asking the same tool is not a check (H5).', '9.3'),
 ('HQ2', 'Arithmetic', 'H3', 'AI: “Of 240 respondents, 66 chose option C, which is 32.5%.”',
  ['Accept', 'Refuse: 66/240 = 27.5%', 'Refuse: percentages need a confidence interval', 'Accept: rounding differences are normal'], 1,
  'Recompute: 66/240 = 0.275. The slip is arithmetic, not rounding (H3).', '13.1'),
 ('HQ3', 'Wrong test', 'H2', 'AI ran an independent two-sample t-test on the same 40 students’ scores before and after a workshop and reports p = 0.21.',
  ['Accept: p is above 0.05', 'Refuse: the data are paired; a paired test is needed', 'Refuse: use a chi-square test', 'Accept: the samples are large enough'], 1,
  'The design is paired. Ignoring the pairing gives the wrong standard error (H2).', '8.7'),
 ('HQ4', 'Violated assumption', 'H2', 'AI: “Linear regression shows income rises by HK$410 per year of age (p < 0.001).” The residual plot is a strong U-shape.',
  ['Accept: p is very small', 'Refuse: the linear form is wrong; the slope summary misleads', 'Accept: residual plots are optional', 'Refuse: n is too small'], 1,
  'A clear pattern in the residuals means the model form is wrong. A small p-value does not repair it (H2).', '10.5'),
 ('HQ5', 'Causal over-claim', 'H4', 'AI, on observational records: “Students who attend more tutorials score higher, so attending tutorials raises scores by 3 marks per session.”',
  ['Accept: r is strong', 'Refuse the causal wording: report an association, with possible confounders', 'Refuse: correlations cannot be computed on marks', 'Accept if p < 0.05'], 1,
  'Observational data support association only. Motivation could drive both variables (H4).', '11.3'),
 ('HQ6', 'p-value meaning', 'H4', 'AI: “p = 0.03, so there is a 97% probability the new method works.”',
  ['Accept', 'Refuse: a p-value is not the probability that a hypothesis is true', 'Refuse: it should say 3%', 'Accept: this is the Bayesian reading'], 1,
  'A p-value is computed assuming H0; it is not P(H1 | data) (H4).', '8.2'),
 ('HQ7', 'Biased data', 'H4', 'AI: “An online poll of 5,000 followers of a fitness page shows Hong Kong adults exercise 6 hours a week.”',
  ['Accept: n is large', 'Refuse: self-selected followers do not represent HK adults', 'Accept with a footnote on n', 'Refuse: 5,000 is too small'], 1,
  'Voluntary response from an interested group. A large n does not remove selection bias (H4).', '2.5'),
 ('HQ8', 'Privacy', 'H6', 'To speed up marking, you plan to paste a spreadsheet of student names, IDs and grades into a free public chatbot.',

r"""FlippedStat v9.0 — content of the master revision (brief d3eeb280…: "FlippedStat v8.0 master revision brief").
Read by tools/assemble_v90.py. Everything here is data; the assembler applies and checks it.

FIX      (target, old, new)       target = 'L:<lesson>' | 'C:<topic>' | 'A:<lesson>' (FSA data) | 'FIG:<fig id>'
OPEN     {lesson: bridge}         anonymous situational opening ("Imagine you…") for the named lessons
NEW      list of added subtopics  {after, no, title, min, kind, html}
SPLIT    {lesson: (reading parts, practice parts)} and WEEK_ADD  {week: minutes} — shelf time made visible
JAM      {lesson: [(stage, piece)]} jamovi passages moved after an R-first subtopic (RFIRST)
"""
K = None  # keys of the bundled data are inserted by the assembler from build/rev90_keys.json

def ai(prompt, model, check, bad=None, fix=None):
    """The three-part AI skill block required by the brief."""
    h = '<div class="fsr-ai">'
    if bad:
        h += f'<p><b>A prompt that fails.</b> <code>{bad}</code></p><p>{fix}</p>'
    h += (f'<div class="fsr-ai3"><div><b>1 · Prompt</b><p>{prompt}</p></div>'
          f'<div><b>2 · Model, named before the AI runs</b><p>{model}</p></div>'
          f'<div><b>3 · Independent cross-check</b><p>{check}</p></div></div>'
          '<p class="fsr-rule">Agreement between two AI tools is not the check. Record both numbers: the AI’s and yours.</p></div>')
    return h

def rcall(call, line, excel, note=''):
    return (f'<div class="fsr-r"><div><b>R call</b><pre><code>{call}</code></pre></div>'
            f'<div><b>The line of output that answers the question</b><p>{line}</p></div>'
            f'<div><b>Excel command that should match</b><p><code>{excel}</code></p></div></div>{note}')

add('5.3.1', '5.3.0-forecast', 'What a 70% forecast means', 20, 'lesson',
 '<p>Imagine you hear a 70% forecast for rain tomorrow and must say what that probability means.</p><p>Tomorrow happens once, so the 70% cannot be a long-run frequency of tomorrows. It is a statement about a <b>forecasting procedure</b>: on the many days for which this forecaster says 70%, it should rain on about 70% of them. That property is called <b>calibration</b>, and it can be checked from records.</p><p>A worked check: of 200 past days with a 70% forecast, rain fell on 131 (65.5%). A binomial standard error of \\(\\sqrt{0.7\\times0.3/200}=0.032\\) puts 65.5% about 1.4 SE below 70% — no clear evidence of miscalibration.</p><p>The dice example that follows answers a different question — a probability you can compute from symmetry.</p>' +
 rcall('binom.test(131, 200, p = 0.7)$p.value   # about 0.17', 'The p-value line: no clear evidence that the 70% days are miscalibrated.', '=BINOM.DIST(131,200,0.7,TRUE)*2 (two-sided, approximate)'))
add('5.8.4', '5.8.4-ai', 'AI skill: ask for the 1,000-person table', 20, 'ai',
 ai('“A screening test has sensitivity 0.90 and specificity 0.90; prevalence is 1%. Build the table for 1,000 people: diseased/not diseased by positive/negative, with every cell count. Then report P(disease | positive). Show the arithmetic.”',
    'The model is a 2×2 table of 1,000 people with fixed prevalence, sensitivity and specificity. The question it supports is the positive predictive value, not “is the test 90% accurate?”.',
    'By hand: 10 diseased → 9 true positives; 990 healthy → 99 false positives; PPV = 9/108 = 0.083. R: <code>0.9*0.01/(0.9*0.01+0.1*0.99)</code> = 0.0833.',
    bad='Is this test 90% accurate?', fix='That question invites a yes. Ask instead for the table, and read the answer off its positive column.'))

The exam asks for this test now; Topic 9.7 returns to it in depth.</p><div class="fsaeq">\[t=\frac{r\sqrt{n-2}}{\sqrt{1-r^2}},\qquad df=n-2\]</div><p>Substitute: \(t=0.45\sqrt{18}/\sqrt{1-0.2025}=1.909/0.893=2.14\), df = 18, two-sided p = 0.046.</p>' +
 rcall('cor.test(x, y)   # prints t, df and p-value', 'The line <code>t = 2.1379, df = 18, p-value = 0.0465</code> (for r = 0.45, n = 20).', '=T.DIST.2T(2.138,18) → 0.046'))
add('9.7.4', '9.7.4-admitted', 'Case 1: only the admitted students', 15, 'case',
 '<p>Imagine you only observe the admitted students. In the full class, study hours and grade correlate at r = 0.62. Among A-grade students only, r = 0.15. The selection rule is on the <i>outcome</i> (grade), so the range of y is cut short and the correlation shrinks. This does not show that study is unimportant.</p>')
add('9.7.4', '9.7.4-top20', 'Case 2: keep the top 20% of x', 10, 'case',
 '<p>Imagine you keep the top 20% of x from a simulated population with r = 0.60. The selection rule is on the <i>predictor</i>, and the correlation falls to r = 0.33. Different rule, different numbers — the two cases are not one example.</p>')

 '<p>Imagine a classmate reruns your cross-validation and gets different fold errors. Without a named split, neither of you can check the other.</p><table class="tbl"><tr><th>Fold</th><th>1</th><th>2</th><th>3</th><th>4</th><th>5</th><th>Mean</th></tr><tr><td>quiz ~ hours, RMSE</td><td>9.64</td><td>7.25</td><td>6.68</td><td>6.63</td><td>6.40</td><td>7.32</td></tr><tr><td>Mean-only baseline</td><td>9.82</td><td>8.41</td><td>6.99</td><td>6.55</td><td>6.41</td><td>7.64</td></tr></table><p class="fsacap">Python: <code>KFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=1)</code> on revision_quiz.csv (n = 120). R uses a different generator; record your own seed and folds.</p>' +
 rcall('set.seed(1); fold &lt;- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = 120))\nsapply(1:5, function(k) { f &lt;- lm(quiz_score ~ revision_hours, subset = fold != k, data = d)\n  sqrt(mean((d$quiz_score[fold == k] - predict(f, d[fold == k, ]))^2)) })',
       'Five RMSEs and their mean, to be compared with the mean-only baseline on the same folds.', 'No single Excel command; recompute one fold with =SLOPE(), =INTERCEPT() and =SQRT(SUMXMY2()/24)'))
add('12.2.3', '12.2.3-ai', 'AI skill: forbid leakage, demand a baseline', 20, 'ai',
 '<p>Imagine an AI saying “98% accurate” when 2% of students drop out: predicting “nobody drops out” is also 98% accurate.</p>' +
 ai('“Predict dropout from the attached file. Do not use columns recorded after the outcome (list them). Report accuracy alongside the majority-class baseline and the recall for dropouts.”',
    'Outcome dropout; unit one student; group split by student; predictors fixed before fitting; leakage columns named and excluded.',
    'Compute the baseline yourself: <code>max(prop.table(table(d$dropout)))</code> in R or <code>=MAX(COUNTIF(C:C,0),COUNTIF(C:C,1))/COUNT(C:C)</code> in Excel.'))

========== FILE: ws/content/tiers.py ==========

"""FlippedStat subtopic tiers (F = Fundamental, I = Intermediate, X = Extension) and block-tier rules.
Nothing is removed by tiering. Subtopic tiers are drafted by Copilot and require academic approval.
Sources: content/e5_content.py (E5, stage 3a) and content/tiers_core.py (Weeks 1–14, E1–E4, C1–C4; stages 3b–3e)."""
import sys, json; sys.path.insert(0, 'content')
from e5_content import TIERS as E5
import tiers_core as TC

def build(FS):
    sub, topic = dict(E5), dict(TC.TOPIC)
    for u in FS['units']:
        for t in u['topics']:
            st = TC.CORE.get(t['no'])
            if st is None: continue
            if st.endswith('*'): st = st[0] * len(t['subs'])
            assert len(st) == len(t['subs']), (t['no'], st)
            for s_, c in zip(t['subs'], st): sub[s_['no']] = c
    for u in FS['units']:
        for t in u['topics']:
            if not t['subs'] and t['no'] not in topic and u['id'] != 'E5': raise SystemExit('companion topic without tier ' + t['no'])
            if t['subs'] and not all(s_['no'] in sub for s_ in t['subs']): raise SystemExit('untiered subtopic in ' + t['no'])
    return sub, topic

BLOCKS = [
  ['article.lesson .v5card.board', 'I', 'equation blackboard'],
  ['.fsa .fsast.k-why', 'I', '“Why it works” stage'],
  ['.fsa .fsast.k-use', 'I', '“Use it” stage'],
  ['.fsa .fsast.k-practice', 'I', '“Practise” stage'],
  ['.fsa .fsast.k-deeper', 'X', '“Go deeper” stage'],
  ['.fsa .fsast.opt', 'X', 'optional stage'],
  ['.fsa .fsast.k-pyroute', 'X', 'Think Stats Python route'],
  ['.fsa .fsa-item.lv-x', 'X', 'Challenge item'],
]
WHY = TC.WHY

## 1. What FlippedStat is

FlippedStat is a self-paced, interactive statistics-learning platform developed at the Chinese University of Hong Kong for the TDLEG 2025–28 project. It teaches statistics and how to use Copilot, Qwen, and Grok **validly, ethically, transparently, and reproducibly**, with explicit human verification of AI output.

It is an **optional self-study campaign**, not a compulsory credit-bearing course. Keep explanatory depth; move overflow into supplementary slides or handouts rather than cutting text. “Certificate”, “endorsement”, or “distinction” labels on the site are progress labels unless CUHK formally approves otherwise.

Synergise with the department’s eLearn StatLM modules at [https://elearn.sta.cuhk.edu.hk/statlm/](https://elearn.sta.cuhk.edu.hk/statlm/): cross-link, align style, avoid duplication.

### Core instructional philosophy

Each topic should normally follow this progression:

1. Question first: learners commit to an initial answer.
2. Plain-language explanation: intuition before formalism.
3. Formal statement or model.
4. Worked number: a transparent numerical example.
5. Interactive visual or task.
6. AI moment: a prompt or AI-generated claim that may contain a weakness.
7. Human verification (see C.R.O.S.S. below).
8. Interpretation: what is and is not supported.
9. Practice or check.
10. Time / readings ledger.

### Human-verification mindset

AI agreement is not proof. Copilot, Qwen, Grok, or another model may agree because they share training patterns or make the same mistake. Students verify with the **C.R.O.S.S.** checklist: Count, Recompute, Other tools, Statistical principles, Sources and scope. Practice is “AI calculates, student verifies.” Code is taught through AI prompting rather than syntax recitation; reference solutions exist as optional support. Welch’s *t*-test is the default two-sample procedure. The four-fifths / selection-rate ratio is lower rate divided by higher rate.

### Owner preferences

- Accuracy first; answer first; no generic praise.
- Traditional Chinese and natural Hong Kong wording when writing Chinese; standard written Chinese for formal institutional work.
- English is the platform language unless instructed otherwise.
- Prefer official and primary sources. Report conflicts instead of silently choosing one.
- Never fabricate data, sources, citations, quotations, test results, policies, or Hong Kong / CUHK claims.
- Preserve intellectual depth. Do not oversimplify into incorrectness. Keep difficult but worthwhile material as extensions rather than deleting it.
- Prefer animation, illustration, motion graphics, and screen recording of the interactive site over AI-generated live-action people.
- After every substantive stage, keep a versioned standalone and a change log. Never overwrite the only copy of a prior stable release.

## 4. Rebuild discipline

- Edit source, then assemble a **new** `-dev` standalone. Do not hand-edit the 20 MB HTML if the same change can be made in source.
- Overlay only changed FSA lessons. Do **not** run a full `tools/build_absorb.py` if OISD/BOOK/FSfull parts are missing.
- Do **not** re-run `rev90_data.py` or rewrite `build/rev90_files.json` unless you intend a keyed-data migration and have recomputed every affected key.
- Keep official extract bytes stable unless you are adding a documented new series (snapshot + codebook + attribution).
- Log every increment in `logs/v10.N-dev_change_log.md` and run the matching checker to a full pass.
- If a change would alter a placement / pre-post / QA-ledger key, stop and flag it for human review. Open QA rows QA-0536, 0537, 0543, 0544, 0546, 0547, 0548 still need textbook data and a real R check; do not fill them with invented numbers.
- Label synthetic teaching tables as FlippedStat calculations, not official statistics.
- Worked numbers on official extracts are FlippedStat calculations unless the source publishes that exact statistic.

## 8. Quality gates (unchanged in spirit)

Before integrating a change, check:

- **Content:** coherent lesson flow; no detached textbook dumps; HK or labelled-synthetic context where claimed; no cut text.  
- **Statistical:** target quantity, unit of analysis, sampling process, measurement, missingness, bias, effect size vs significance, multiple comparisons, census vs sample, and honest iid assumptions.  
- **AI-responsibility:** verification is independent of multi-model agreement; no personal data in public prompts; C.R.O.S.S. visible where AI is used.  
- **Assessment:** no silent key changes; no invented textbook numbers in open QA rows.  
- **Accessibility:** do not regress keyboard, contrast, 320 px reflow, or captions.  
- **Rights:** paraphrase; honest source labels; no claim of legal clearance; no official-statistics invention.  
- **Release:** new version name; previous hashes unchanged; checker n/n; change log written.

========== FILE: ws/exports/analyse_completion.py ==========

"""FlippedStat KPI 2.1 (unique enrolments) and KPI 2.2 (70% complete >= 80% of at least one module).
Inputs (CSV; Moodle exports mapped to these names — see stage1/moodle/analytics_data_dictionary.csv):
  enrolments.csv : pid, role (student|staff|test), enrolled_at (ISO date)
  completion.csv : pid, module, activity_id, required (0/1), completed (0/1)
Rules (KPI protocol §4):
  - Unique enrolment = distinct pid with role == student (staff/test accounts excluded), enrolled by the cut-off date.
  - Started = completed >= 1 required activity in any module.  Primary KPI 2.2 denominator = started learners.
  - Module complete = completed required activities / required activities >= 0.80 (FSM threshold).
  - Secondary denominator = all enrolled students (reported, not the KPI).
Usage: python analyse_completion.py enrolments.csv completion.csv [cutoff YYYY-MM-DD]"""
import sys, pandas as pd, numpy as np
from scipy import stats
en = pd.read_csv(sys.argv[1]); co = pd.read_csv(sys.argv[2]); cut = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else None
import os; sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))); import consent_filter
_en_all = en
en = consent_filter.apply(en, sys.argv[1], 'completion'); co = co[co.pid.isin(set(en.pid))]
if en is not _en_all:
    _a = _en_all[_en_all.role.str.lower() == 'student']
    if cut: _a = _a[pd.to_datetime(_a.enrolled_at) <= pd.Timestamp(cut)]
    print(f'[administrative aggregate, all students incl. non-consenting: {_a.pid.nunique()} unique enrolments — whether KPI 2.1 uses this count is for H11/ORKTS]')
st = en[en.role.str.lower() == 'student'].copy()
if cut: st = st[pd.to_datetime(st.enrolled_at) <= pd.Timestamp(cut)]
ids = set(st.pid); n_enr = len(ids)
co = co[co.pid.isin(ids) & (co.required == 1)]
mod = co.groupby(['pid', 'module']).completed.agg(['sum', 'count']).reset_index(); mod['share'] = mod['sum'] / mod['count']
started = set(mod[mod['sum'] >= 1].pid); best = mod.groupby('pid').share.max()
done = set(best[best >= 0.8].index)
def ci(k, n): return stats.binomtest(k, n).proportion_ci() if n else (np.nan, np.nan)
k, n = len(done & started), len(started); lo, hi = ci(k, n)
print('=== KPI 2.1 · unique student enrolments ===')
print(f'{n_enr} unique students' + (f' enrolled by {cut}' if cut else '') + f'; target 500: {"MET" if n_enr >= 500 else "not met"}')
print('\n=== KPI 2.2 · completion ===')
print(f'started learners: {n}  (of {n_enr} enrolled; {n_enr - n} enrolled but never started)')
print(f'completed >= 80% of at least one module: {k}/{n} = {k / n:.1%} (95% CI {lo:.1%}–{hi:.1%}); target 70%: {"MET" if n and k / n >= .7 else "not met"}' if n else 'no started learners')
print(f'secondary (all enrolled as denominator): {len(done)}/{n_enr} = {len(done) / n_enr:.1%}' if n_enr else '')
per = mod.groupby('module').apply(lambda g: pd.Series(dict(started=int((g['sum'] >= 1).sum()), completed=int((g.share >= .8).sum()), median_share=round(g.share.median(), 2))), include_groups=False)
per['completion_rate'] = (per.completed / per.started).round(3); print('\nper module:'); print(per.to_string())
per.to_csv('completion_by_module.csv')

========== END FILE: ws/exports/analyse_completion.py ==========


========== FILE: ws/exports/analyse_m8.py ==========

"""FlippedStat Module 8 KPI analysis (TDLEG KPIs 5.1 and 5.2).
Input CSV (site export or mapped Moodle export): pid, instrument, form, timestamp, item, response, correct, confidence
  instrument = hallucination_quiz | confidence_survey; form = pre | post (quiz rows use post).
Rules: latest attempt per learner × instrument × form. KPI 5.2 uses matched learners (both surveys).
Usage: python analyse_m8.py responses.csv"""
import sys, numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
d = pd.read_csv(sys.argv[1])
import os; sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))); import consent_filter
d = consent_filter.apply(d, sys.argv[1], 'Module 8')
d = d[d.timestamp == d.groupby(['pid', 'instrument', 'form']).timestamp.transform('max')]
q = d[d.instrument == 'hallucination_quiz']
print('=== KPI 5.1 · hallucination quiz ===')
if len(q):
    sc = q.groupby('pid').correct.sum(); n = len(sc)
    lo, hi = stats.binomtest(int((sc >= 8).sum()), n).proportion_ci() if n else (np.nan, np.nan)
    print(f'completers {n}; mean {sc.mean():.2f}/10 ({10 * sc.mean():.0f}%); median {sc.median():.0f}')
    print(f'(a) mean score ≥ 80%: {"MET" if sc.mean() >= 8 else "not met"}')
    print(f'(b) scoring ≥ 8/10: {(sc >= 8).mean():.1%} (95% CI {lo:.1%}–{hi:.1%}); target ≥ 80%: {"MET" if (sc >= 8).mean() >= .8 else "not met"}')
    it = q.groupby('item').correct.mean().sort_values(); print('item difficulty (proportion correct, hardest first):'); print(it.round(2).to_string())
    c = q.dropna(subset=['confidence']); c = c[c.confidence != '']
    if len(c):
        cal = c.astype({'confidence': float}).groupby('confidence').correct.agg(['count', 'mean']); print('calibration (confidence → proportion correct):'); print(cal.round(2).to_string())
        print(f'over-confident errors (confidence ≥ 4, wrong): {((c.confidence.astype(float) >= 4) & (c.correct == 0)).sum()} of {len(c)} responses')
s = d[d.instrument == 'confidence_survey'].copy(); s['response'] = pd.to_numeric(s.response, errors='coerce')
print('\n=== KPI 5.2 · confidence ===')
scale = s[s.item.str.match(r'^C\d$')]
w = scale.groupby(['pid', 'form']).response.mean().unstack()
if {'pre', 'post'} <= set(w.columns):
    m = w.dropna(); ch = m.post - m.pre
    print(f'matched {len(m)} (before {w.pre.notna().sum()}, after {w.post.notna().sum() if "post" in w else 0})')
    print(f'(a) % with a positive change in the 6-item scale mean: {(ch > 0).mean():.1%}; target ≥ 70%: {"MET" if (ch > 0).mean() >= .7 else "not met"}')
    if len(m) > 1:
        t = stats.ttest_rel(m.post, m.pre); print(f'    mean change {ch.mean():+.2f} on 1–5 (paired t = {t.statistic:.2f}, p = {t.pvalue:.4f}); unchanged {(ch == 0).mean():.1%}; decreased {(ch < 0).mean():.1%}')
    for it in sorted(scale.item.unique()):
        x = scale[scale.item == it].pivot_table(index='pid', columns='form', values='response').dropna()
        if {'pre', 'post'} <= set(x.columns): print(f'    {it}: before {x.pre.mean():.2f} → after {x.post.mean():.2f}')
dd = s[s.item == 'D1'].response.dropna()
if len(dd): print(f'(b) direct item D1, “somewhat/much more confident”: {(dd >= 4).mean():.1%} of {len(dd)}; target ≥ 70%: {"MET" if (dd >= 4).mean() >= .7 else "not met"}')
print('\nNote: report (a) and (b) for each KPI; self-reported confidence is not competence — read KPI 5.2 alongside the KPI 5.1 calibration table.')

========== END FILE: ws/exports/analyse_m8.py ==========


========== FILE: ws/exports/analyse_prepost.R ==========

# FlippedStat pre/post analysis in R — same rules and outputs as analyse_prepost.py.
# NOTE: mirrors analyse_prepost.py. v9.9 (S1.2): logic verified by a line-by-line Python emulation of R defaults
# (stage1/qa/s12_emulate_R.py; identical results on the synthetic fixture); edge-case guard added. Still to be executed once in real R.
# Usage: Rscript analyse_prepost.R responses.csv [out_prefix]
args <- commandArgs(TRUE); src <- args[1]; pre <- if (length(args) > 1) args[2] else "prepost"
d <- read.csv(src, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d <- d[d$timestamp == ave(d$timestamp, d$pid, d$module, d$form, FUN = max), ]
sc <- aggregate(correct ~ module + pid + form, d, mean)
an <- aggregate(correct ~ module + pid + form, d[d$anchor == 1, ], mean); names(an)[4] <- "anchor"
sc <- merge(sc, an)
rows <- lapply(split(sc, sc$module), function(g) {
  w <- reshape(g, idvar = "pid", timevar = "form", direction = "wide", drop = "module"); w <- na.omit(w)
  n <- nrow(w); started <- length(unique(g$pid[g$form == "pre"]))
  a <- 100 * w$correct.pre; b <- 100 * w$correct.post; dd <- b - a
  if (n < 2 || sd(dd) == 0) {  # v9.9 guard (S1.2): t.test() stops on n < 2 or constant differences; mirror the Python script
    return(data.frame(module = g$module[1], n_pre = started, n_matched = n, attrition_pct = if (started) round(100 * (1 - n / started), 1) else NA,
             pre_mean = NA, post_mean = NA, abs_gain = if (n) round(mean(dd), 1) else NA, ci_low = NA, ci_high = NA, rel_gain_pct = NA, norm_gain = NA,
             t = NA, p_t = NA, p_wilcoxon = NA, d_z = NA, anchor_gain = NA, KPI_rel_gain_20 = NA, KPI_p_lt_05 = NA))
  }
  tt <- t.test(b, a, paired = TRUE); wil <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(b, a, paired = TRUE))
  data.frame(module = g$module[1], n_pre = started, n_matched = n, attrition_pct = round(100 * (1 - n / started), 1),
             pre_mean = round(mean(a), 1), post_mean = round(mean(b), 1), abs_gain = round(mean(dd), 1),
             ci_low = round(tt$conf.int[1], 1), ci_high = round(tt$conf.int[2], 1),
             rel_gain_pct = round(100 * mean(dd) / mean(a), 1), norm_gain = round((mean(b) - mean(a)) / (100 - mean(a)), 2),
             t = round(unname(tt$statistic), 2), p_t = round(tt$p.value, 4), p_wilcoxon = round(wil$p.value, 4),
             d_z = round(mean(dd) / sd(dd), 2), anchor_gain = round(100 * mean(w$anchor.post - w$anchor.pre), 1),
             KPI_rel_gain_20 = mean(dd) / mean(a) >= 0.2, KPI_p_lt_05 = tt$p.value < 0.05)
})
res <- do.call(rbind, rows); write.csv(res, paste0(pre, "_modules_R.csv"), row.names = FALSE); print(res)

========== END FILE: ws/exports/analyse_prepost.R ==========


========== FILE: ws/exports/analyse_prepost.py ==========

"""FlippedStat pre/post analysis (TDLEG KPI 2.3 and Deliverable 2 evaluation).
Input: long CSV with one row per learner × item response:
    pid, module, form (pre|post), timestamp, item, lo, level, anchor (0/1), chosen, correct (0/1)
  - the website's “Export responses” button writes exactly this format;
  - from Moodle, export the quiz Responses report and map columns to the same names (one row per question).
Rules: latest complete attempt per learner × module × form; learners analysed only if they have BOTH forms (matched).
Reports, per module: n matched, attrition, pre/post mean (%), absolute gain, relative gain (KPI: ≥ 20%),
normalised gain, paired t with 95% CI, Wilcoxon signed-rank, paired effect size d_z, anchor-only gain (guards against
form-difficulty differences), and item statistics (difficulty p and corrected point-biserial).
Usage: python analyse_prepost.py responses.csv [out_prefix]"""
import sys, numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
src = sys.argv[1]; pre = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 'prepost'
d = pd.read_csv(src)
import os; sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))); import consent_filter
d = consent_filter.apply(d, src, 'pre/post')
need = {'pid', 'module', 'form', 'timestamp', 'item', 'lo', 'anchor', 'correct'}
miss = need - set(d.columns); assert not miss, f'missing columns: {miss}'
last = d.groupby(['pid', 'module', 'form'])['timestamp'].transform('max'); d = d[d.timestamp == last]
sc = d.groupby(['module', 'pid', 'form']).agg(score=('correct', 'mean'), anchor=('correct', lambda s: s[d.loc[s.index, 'anchor'] == 1].mean())).reset_index()
rows = []
for m, g in sc.groupby('module'):
    w = g.pivot(index='pid', columns='form', values=['score', 'anchor']).dropna()
    started = g[g.form == 'pre'].pid.nunique(); n = len(w)
    r = dict(module=m, n_pre=started, n_post=g[g.form == 'post'].pid.nunique(), n_matched=n, attrition_pct=round(100 * (1 - n / started), 1) if started else np.nan)
    if n >= 2:
        a, b = 100 * w[('score', 'pre')].values, 100 * w[('score', 'post')].values; dd = b - a
        t = stats.ttest_rel(b, a); ci = stats.t.interval(.95, n - 1, loc=dd.mean(), scale=stats.sem(dd)) if dd.std() > 0 else (dd.mean(), dd.mean())
        wil = stats.wilcoxon(b, a) if np.any(dd != 0) else None
        r.update(pre_mean=round(a.mean(), 1), post_mean=round(b.mean(), 1), abs_gain=round(dd.mean(), 1), ci_low=round(ci[0], 1), ci_high=round(ci[1], 1),
                 rel_gain_pct=round(100 * dd.mean() / a.mean(), 1) if a.mean() else np.nan,
                 norm_gain=round((b.mean() - a.mean()) / (100 - a.mean()), 2) if a.mean() < 100 else np.nan,
                 t=round(t.statistic, 2), p_t=round(t.pvalue, 4), p_wilcoxon=round(wil.pvalue, 4) if wil else np.nan,
                 d_z=round(dd.mean() / dd.std(ddof=1), 2) if dd.std(ddof=1) > 0 else np.nan,
                 anchor_gain=round(100 * (w[('anchor', 'post')] - w[('anchor', 'pre')]).mean(), 1),
                 KPI_rel_gain_20=bool(a.mean() and dd.mean() / a.mean() >= .2), KPI_p_lt_05=bool(t.pvalue < .05))
    rows.append(r)
res = pd.DataFrame(rows); res.to_csv(pre + '_modules.csv', index=False)
it = []
for (m, f), g in d.groupby(['module', 'form']):
    tot = g.groupby('pid').correct.sum()
    for iid, gi in g.groupby('item'):
        x = gi.set_index('pid').correct; rest = tot.loc[x.index] - x
        rpb = stats.pearsonr(x, rest)[0] if x.std() > 0 and rest.std() > 0 else np.nan
        it.append(dict(module=m, form=f, item=iid, n=len(x), difficulty_p=round(x.mean(), 2), point_biserial=round(rpb, 2),
                       flag='review' if (x.mean() > .95 or x.mean() < .2 or (rpb == rpb and rpb < .15)) else ''))
pd.DataFrame(it).to_csv(pre + '_items.csv', index=False)
pd.set_option('display.width', 200); print(res.to_string(index=False))
print(f'\nItem statistics → {pre}_items.csv ({sum(1 for x in it if x["flag"])} items flagged for review: p > .95, p < .20 or r_pb < .15).')
print('Interpretation: report relative gain (KPI ≥ 20%) and the paired test separately; a significant result is not the same as a 20% gain.')

========== END FILE: ws/exports/analyse_prepost.py ==========


========== FILE: ws/exports/consent_filter.py ==========

"""Research-consent and withdrawal filter for FlippedStat evaluation scripts (Copilot, 2026-11-18, Stage 10).

Implements stage10/FlippedStat_Pilot_Consent_Pack_DRAFT.md §2/§4/§5 (draft; H11 open).

Looks for two files in the same folder as the main input CSV (or in $FS_CONSENT_DIR):
  consent.csv          pid, research_consent (yes|no), consent_version, consent_at (ISO), age18 (yes|no)
  withdrawn_codes.csv  pid, processed_at, option (a|b)
Rule: latest consent row per pid; keep pid if research_consent == yes AND age18 == yes,
      and pid is not listed in withdrawn_codes.csv with option b (remove data).
If consent.csv is absent the data pass through unchanged and a warning is written to stderr:
results are then NOT eligible for research reporting (fine for synthetic tests).
"""
import os, sys
import pandas as pd


def _dir(src):
    return os.environ.get("FS_CONSENT_DIR") or os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(src))


def eligible_pids(src):
    d = _dir(src); cp = os.path.join(d, "consent.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(cp):
        return None
    c = pd.read_csv(cp, dtype=str)
    need = {"pid", "research_consent", "consent_at", "age18"}
    if not need <= set(c.columns):
        raise SystemExit(f"consent.csv missing columns: {sorted(need - set(c.columns))}")
    c = c.sort_values("consent_at").groupby("pid").tail(1)
    ok = set(c[(c.research_consent.str.lower() == "yes") & (c.age18.str.lower() == "yes")].pid)
    wp = os.path.join(d, "withdrawn_codes.csv")
    n_w = 0
    if os.path.exists(wp):
        w = pd.read_csv(wp, dtype=str)
        rm = set(w[w.get("option", pd.Series(["b"] * len(w))).str.lower() == "b"].pid)
        n_w = len(ok & rm); ok -= rm
    sys.stderr.write(f"[consent_filter] {d}: {len(c)} consent records; {len(ok)} eligible for research use; {n_w} removed by withdrawal\n")
    return ok


def apply(df, src, label=""):
    ok = eligible_pids(src)
    if ok is None:
        sys.stderr.write(f"[consent_filter] WARNING: no consent.csv beside {os.path.basename(src)} — {label} output is NOT eligible for research reporting\n")
        return df
    before = df.pid.nunique()
    out = df[df.pid.astype(str).isin(ok)]
    print(f"[research-consent filter applied: {out.pid.nunique()} of {before} learners kept]")
    return out

========== END FILE: ws/exports/consent_filter.py ==========


========== FILE: ws/exports/run_kpis.py ==========

"""One-command TDLEG KPI dashboard. Usage: python run_kpis.py evidence_dir [cutoff YYYY-MM-DD]
evidence_dir may contain (missing files -> KPI reported as 'no evidence yet'):
  module_deployment.csv  uptime.csv  enrolments.csv  completion.csv  prepost_responses.csv
  certificate_log.csv  clear_attendance.csv  course_adoption.csv  m8_responses.csv
Templates: stage1/kpi/templates/*_TEMPLATE.csv. Definitions: FlippedStat KPI and Evaluation Protocol v1.0 (§4)."""
import sys, os, subprocess, pandas as pd, io, contextlib, datetime
E = sys.argv[1]; cut = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None; here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
f = lambda n: os.path.join(E, n); has = lambda n: os.path.exists(f(n))
R = []
def add(k, target, value, met, src): R.append(dict(KPI=k, target=target, result=value, status=('MET' if met else 'not met') if met is not None else 'no evidence yet', evidence=src))
if has('module_deployment.csv'):
    d = pd.read_csv(f('module_deployment.csv')); live = d[(d[['essential_topics_live', 'preform_live', 'postform_live', 'completion_rule_live']] == 'Y').all(axis=1)]
    core = set(live.module) >= set(range(1, 9)); add('1.1', 'Modules 1–8 live (6–9 allowed)', f'{len(live)} modules fully live', len(live) >= 6 and core, 'module_deployment.csv')
else: add('1.1', 'Modules 1–8 live', '—', None, '')
if has('uptime.csv'):
    u = pd.read_csv(f('uptime.csv')); eff = u.minutes_in_month - u.announced_maintenance_minutes; up = 1 - u.minutes_down.sum() / eff.sum()
    add('1.2', '≥ 99% uptime with SSO', f'{up:.3%} over {len(u)} months; SSO failures {int((u.sso_test_passed != "Y").sum())}', up >= .99 and (u.sso_test_passed == 'Y').all(), 'uptime.csv')
else: add('1.2', '≥ 99% uptime with SSO', '—', None, '')
def run(script, *a):
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(here, script), *a], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=E); return r.stdout + r.stderr
if has('enrolments.csv') and has('completion.csv'):
    out = run('analyse_completion.py', 'enrolments.csv', 'completion.csv', *([cut] if cut else []))
    l1 = [x for x in out.splitlines() if 'unique students' in x][0]; l2 = [x for x in out.splitlines() if 'at least one module' in x]
    add('2.1', '500 unique students', l1.split(';')[0], 'MET' in l1, 'enrolments.csv')
    add('2.2', '≥ 70% of started learners complete ≥ 80% of a module', l2[0].split(': ', 1)[1].split('; target')[0] if l2 else '—', bool(l2) and 'MET' in l2[0], 'completion.csv')
else: add('2.1', '500 unique students', '—', None, ''); add('2.2', '≥ 70% complete ≥ 80% of a module', '—', None, '')
if has('prepost_responses.csv'):
    run('analyse_prepost.py', 'prepost_responses.csv', 'prepost'); p = pd.read_csv(f('prepost_modules.csv')).dropna(subset=['rel_gain_pct'])
    w = (p.rel_gain_pct * p.n_matched).sum() / p.n_matched.sum()
    add('2.3', '≥ 20% relative pre/post gain (matched)', f'pooled {w:.1f}% over {int(p.n_matched.sum())} matched learner-modules; modules meeting 20%: {int((p.rel_gain_pct >= 20).sum())}/{len(p)}', w >= 20, 'prepost_responses.csv')
else: add('2.3', '≥ 20% relative gain', '—', None, '')
if has('certificate_log.csv'):
    c = pd.read_csv(f('certificate_log.csv')); elig = c.completed_at.notna() & c.survey_submitted_at.notna(); iss = c.certificate_id.notna()
    add('3.1', 'Certificates auto-issued to all eligible', f'{int((elig & iss).sum())}/{int(elig.sum())} eligible issued; {int((iss & ~elig).sum())} issued without eligibility', bool((elig <= iss).all() and not (iss & ~elig).any()), 'certificate_log.csv')
else: add('3.1', 'Certificates auto-issued', '—', None, '')
if has('clear_attendance.csv'):
    a = pd.read_csv(f('clear_attendance.csv')); n = a.staff_id.nunique(); add('4.1', 'One CLEAR session, ≥ 20 staff', f'{n} distinct staff', n >= 20, 'clear_attendance.csv')
else: add('4.1', 'One CLEAR session, ≥ 20 staff', '—', None, '')
if has('course_adoption.csv'):
    a = pd.read_csv(f('course_adoption.csv')); a = a[a.evidence_file.notna() & ~a.course_code.str.upper().str.startswith(('STAT', 'RMSC'))]
    n = a.course_code.nunique(); add('4.2', '3 non-Stats courses adopt/recommend', f'{n} courses with written evidence', n >= 3, 'course_adoption.csv')
else: add('4.2', '3 non-Stats courses', '—', None, '')
if has('m8_responses.csv'):
    out = run('analyse_m8.py', 'm8_responses.csv')
    b = [x for x in out.splitlines() if x.startswith('(b) scoring')]; c = [x for x in out.splitlines() if x.startswith('(a) % with a positive')]
    add('5.1', '≥ 80% of completers score ≥ 8/10', b[0].split(': ', 1)[1].split('; target')[0] if b else '—', bool(b) and 'MET' in b[0], 'm8_responses.csv')
    add('5.2', '≥ 70% positive confidence change (6 items)', c[0].split(': ', 1)[1].split('; target')[0] if c else '—', bool(c) and 'MET' in c[0], 'm8_responses.csv')
else: add('5.1', '≥ 80% score ≥ 8/10', '—', None, ''); add('5.2', '≥ 70% confidence gain', '—', None, '')
df = pd.DataFrame(R); df.to_csv(os.path.join(E, 'kpi_dashboard.csv'), index=False)
md = f'# FlippedStat KPI dashboard ({datetime.date.today()})\n\n' + df.to_markdown(index=False) + '\n'
open(os.path.join(E, 'kpi_dashboard.md'), 'w').write(md); print(md)

========== END FILE: ws/exports/run_kpis.py ==========

# FlippedStat — Hong Kong data localisation inventory, wave 2 (18 Nov 2026)

Times below are Asia/Hong_Kong. This wave continues the 18 Nov 2026 source-and-extract review. Wave 1 is recorded in `logs/HK_DATA_LOCALISATION_INVENTORY_2026-11-18.md`. The machine-readable companion for this wave (all 209 inventory rows, with the six edited official topics updated) is `logs/HK_DATA_LOCALISATION_INVENTORY_2026-11-18-wave2.csv`.

Standing instruction (Mike Kan, t27u / t30u): when reviewing each page and each sub-topic, try to replace US-textbook-centred contexts and datasets with licence-clean Hong Kong public data. `hkdatasets` microdata remains uncleared and is not shipped.

Official modules remain Modules 1–8 (153 topics). Module 9 was not treated as approved and was not edited.

## What this wave reviewed

The remaining official Modules 1–8 topics that were still primarily textbook/overseas, deferred, or mixed were reviewed against the already-fetched official extracts (C&SD tables 110-02001, 130-06806, 510-60001 and the 18-row teaching profile). No new official series was fetched. Official *region* and Hong Kong mid-year land population totals already present in `hk_district_population_110-02001.csv` (`geo_level == "region_total"`) were used for population rates, instead of summing the 18 rounded district figures.

Topics changed this wave: **1.3, 3.1, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6**. Wave-1 topics 2.1, 2.2, 4.1, 4.2, 4.4 and E5.2 were left as in v10.4-dev.

Existing synthetic Hong Kong examples (Harbourside, survey300, sleep_column, MTR/bus, and similar) and their keys were not changed. Named historical case studies were not silently relocated. Placement stems, cut scores, QA-ledger open rows, and keyed Navarro / jamovi files were not rewritten.

## Licence (same sources as wave 1; no new series)

Terms were already read from the sources on 18 Nov 2026:

- [C&SD Intellectual Property Rights Notice](https://www.censtatd.gov.hk/en/page_31.html): specified statistical information (tables, datasets, reports and related statistical content, excluding maps, photographs, graphics, drawings, logos, audio and video) may be reused with source acknowledgement, acknowledgement of Government intellectual-property ownership, and modifications clearly indicated.
- [DATA.GOV.HK Terms of Use](https://data.gov.hk/en/terms-and-conditions): reuse with source identification and attribution; data “AS IS”; use is not government endorsement.

No department legal sign-off is claimed. No official C&SD statistic was invented. New worked numbers in this wave are labelled FlippedStat calculations on official figures.

The 18-row profile codebook was extended with wave-2 keys; the official CSV extracts are byte-identical to wave 1.

## Worked numbers added this wave (FlippedStat calculations, not official C&SD statistics)

Official 2025 mid-year land population *region totals* from table 110-02001 (use these, not a sum of the 18 rounded district figures): Hong Kong Island **1,162.4** thousand; Kowloon **2,242.7**; New Territories **4,092.7**; Hong Kong **7,497.8**. The 18 published district figures sum to 7,497.9 thousand (0.1 thousand above the official total). The C&SD table notes that figures may not add up to the totals due to rounding.

FlippedStat shares of the official Hong Kong total, rounded to one decimal place: Hong Kong Island **15.5%**; Kowloon **29.9%**; New Territories **54.6%**. By contrast, the 18 districts split **4 / 5 / 9** (22.2% / 27.8% / 50.0%).

Derived gained/lost flag (already in the profile) by region: Hong Kong Island 0 gained / 4 lost; Kowloon 3 / 2; New Territories 7 / 2.

Five-number summary of the 18 official 2025 district median monthly household incomes, using the same exclusive-halves quartile method as wave 1 (for even n the halves do not overlap): min **HK$24,900** (Kwun Tong); Q1 **HK$26,200**; median **HK$31,000**; Q3 **HK$34,200**; max **HK$45,000** (Central and Western); IQR **HK$8,000**. Tukey fences 14,200 and 46,200; **no** district is a Tukey outlier.

Mean of those 18 district medians: **HK$31,844**; sample SD (divisor n−1, matching R `sd()` and jamovi): **HK$6,121**. Neither is an official C&SD statistic, and the mean of district medians is not the official Hong Kong median (**HK$30,000** in 2025, table 130-06806).

z-scores using that sample SD: Central and Western income **+2.15**; Kwun Tong income **−1.13**; Kwun Tong density **+2.07**; Islands density **−1.00**. Empirical coverage: **11 of 18** incomes within one sample SD of the mean, **17 of 18** within two (Central and Western lies just beyond 2).

A median of district medians is not the official Hong Kong median. The 18 rows are area aggregates, not households.

## Topics changed this wave

### 1.3 Variables and measurement — replaced

The primary classification example is now the official 18-district profile: `region_en` and `district_en` are categorical and nominal; `district_code` is a label, not a number; mid-year land population is numerical and discrete in origin; official district median income is numerical on a ratio scale, but is an area median, not a household’s income. `population_gained` is labelled as a FlippedStat-derived flag. OpenIntro’s US-county typings and Figure 1.7 remain a labelled book illustration (including `median_edu`, because this extract has no official ordinal education variable). The OpenIntro class-records and migraine worked examples are kept and labelled. A short official continuous/discrete note was added in 1.3.2.

### 3.1 Tables, rates and percentages — replaced

The student-facing frequency table counts the 18 official districts by region (4 / 5 / 9). Population rates use official 2025 region totals, not a sum of rounded district figures. The contrast (Hong Kong Island 22.2% of districts but 15.5% of official mid-year land population; New Territories 50% of districts but 54.6% of population) is the teaching point. The contingency table is region × the derived gained/lost flag. Row percentages answer “within each region, what share of districts gained?”; column percentages answer “of the districts that gained, where were they?”. OpenIntro loans and Night Garden tables, and the spam “condition on the explanatory variable” example, remain labelled book illustrations. Their book self-checks were kept.

### 3.3 Measures of centre — supplemented

Existing MTR, AFL and loan examples and their keys were kept. A labelled official-data parallel was added: the unweighted mean of the 18 official 2025 district median incomes is HK$31,844 and the median of those medians is HK$31,000, neither of which is the official all-household median of HK$30,000. 3.3.2 notes the same mild right-skew signature (mean above the median of medians) beside the AFL 35.30 vs 30.50 walk-through.

### 3.4 Position and the boxplot — replaced

The primary five-number / box-plot example is the 18 official 2025 district median incomes (IQR HK$8,000; no Tukey outliers). The method is the same exclusive-halves rule as Topic 4.1, and the lesson states that software percentile algorithms may differ slightly at n = 18. OpenIntro’s loan50 box plot (which does have outliers) and AFL software figures remain labelled illustrations. 3.4.4 notes that splitting the 18 incomes by `region_en` gives three short boxes (n = 4, 5, 9); regional quartiles were not quoted. 3.4.5 (finding typo rows in AFL) was left as a labelled textbook illustration of data cleaning.

### 3.5 Measures of spread — supplemented

Existing MTR, AFL and loan spread examples were kept. A labelled official-data parallel was added: range HK$20,100, IQR HK$8,000, sample SD HK$6,121; 11 of 18 incomes (about 61%) within one sample SD of the mean, 17 of 18 within two. The 68/95 rule is taught as rough here (small n, mild right skew).

### 3.6 Standardisation and shape — replaced

The primary z-score comparison uses official income and density on the 18 districts (z = +2.15, −1.13, +2.07, −1.00) so that HK$ and persons per sq. km can be compared only after standardising. SAT/ACT and possum checks remain labelled book illustrations. Skewness of the official incomes is described qualitatively only; the AFL 0.780 figure remains the software walk-through, because jamovi’s skewness convention was not treated as interchangeable with the lesson formula at n = 18.

# FlippedStat — Hong Kong data localisation inventory, wave 3 (18 Nov 2026)

Times below are Asia/Hong_Kong. This wave continues the 18 Nov 2026 source-and-extract review. Wave 1 is in `logs/HK_DATA_LOCALISATION_INVENTORY_2026-11-18.md`; wave 2 is in `logs/HK_DATA_LOCALISATION_INVENTORY_2026-11-18-wave2.md`. The machine-readable companion for this wave (all 209 inventory rows, with the three edited official topics updated) is `logs/HK_DATA_LOCALISATION_INVENTORY_2026-11-18-wave3.csv`.

Standing instruction (Mike Kan, t27u / t30u): when reviewing each page and each sub-topic, try to replace US-textbook-centred contexts and datasets with licence-clean Hong Kong public data. `hkdatasets` microdata remains uncleared and is not shipped.

Official modules remain Modules 1–8 (153 topics). Module 9 was not treated as approved and was not edited.

## What this wave reviewed

Wave 2 reused the 18-district profile and did not fetch a new official series. Topics 4.3, 6.3 and 6.5 had been deferred because that profile is a poor demonstration (18 populations span less than one order of magnitude; 18 aggregates are a poor rare-event or normal-curve demo). This wave fetched additional official open data, verified terms, and used only series that actually teach those points.

Topics changed this wave: **4.3, 6.3, 6.5**. Wave-1 and wave-2 topics were left as in v10.5-dev. Existing synthetic Hong Kong examples and their keys were not changed. Named historical case studies were not silently relocated. Placement stems, cut scores, QA-ledger open rows, and keyed Navarro / jamovi files were not rewritten.

A C&SD income-group table (130-06604) was inspected as a skew candidate and not shipped: it is a binned official frequency table, not a list of observations that students can log or square-root. E5.11 remains a keyed Harbourside forecast lab; official monthly series were not mixed into those keys (optional official CPI practice remains at E5.2).

## New official series (retrieved 18 Nov 2026, about 04:03 HKT)

Raw snapshots, with retrieval metadata, are under `sources/hk_extracts_raw/`. Teaching extracts and codebooks are under `content/data/hk_extracts/`.

A separate, stricter Intellectual Property Rights Notice applies to materials on the Hong Kong Observatory *website*. These extracts are taken from official open-data endpoints listed on DATA.GOV.HK, not copied from website prose, maps or graphics. Department legal sign-off is not claimed. No official HKO or C&SD statistic was invented.

The official token **Trace** in the rainfall file is preserved. The source file itself defines it as rainfall less than 0.05 mm. It is not recoded as 0.

Wave-1 official CSV bytes (tables 110-02001, 130-06806, 510-60001 and the 18-row profile) were left unchanged.

## Worked numbers added this wave (FlippedStat calculations, not official HKO or C&SD statistics)

**Daily rainfall, measurable wet days (published amount > 0), 2016–2025 at the Hong Kong Observatory.** Of 3,653 days: 1,544 have a published total of 0.0 mm, 632 are official Trace, and 1,477 have a published positive amount. Among those 1,477: minimum 0.1 mm; maximum 425.0 mm (8 September 2023); mean 16.73 mm; median 4.3 mm; sample SD 33.93 mm; Pearson skew 5.28; span 3.63 orders of magnitude. After log₁₀: mean 0.58, median 0.63, Pearson skew −0.14. After a square root: mean 2.99, median 2.07, Pearson skew 1.81. Trace days are excluded from the log (log of 0 is undefined; Trace is not a published millimetre amount).

**June–August daily mean temperature, 2016–2025 at the Hong Kong Observatory** (n = 920): minimum 24.1 °C (4 June 2024); maximum 32.2 °C (27 July 2023); mean 29.23 °C; median 29.50 °C; sample SD (n−1) 1.35 °C; Pearson skew −0.75. Empirical coverage: 633 of 920 (68.8%) within one sample SD of the mean, 875 of 920 (95.1%) within two, 918 of 920 (99.8%) within three. This is a course illustration of a reasonably mound-shaped official measurement, **not** a claim that the official series is exactly normal. The full-year series (n = 3,653; mean 24.27 °C; sample SD 5.01 °C; only 2,174 of 3,653, or 59.5%, within one sample SD) is a poor normal-curve demonstration because of the seasonal cycle.

**June–August days with at least one official cloud-to-ground lightning count, 2016–2025** (30 months; a FlippedStat derivation from official daily totals): mean 17.17 days; median 17; sample variance 18.35; sample SD 4.28; variance/mean 1.07; minimum 8 (July 2022); maximum 26 (August 2018). A Poisson rate λ = 17.17 is a starting description of these summer *day-counts*. Official daily *stroke* totals are not used for that model (2,815 of 3,653 days are 0; the largest official daily total in the window is 14,358 on 6 June 2020; storms cluster).

**Official annual live births** from the yearly series of the same C&SD table: 60,856 (2016) and 31,053 (2025). Among the 120 official monthly totals in 2016–2025: minimum 2,275 (November 2022); maximum 5,519 (November 2016). These published counts have a clear rate, but a single constant Poisson rate does not fit this decade; they are used as a caution, not as the Poisson worked example.

Skewness is the bias-adjusted Pearson moment coefficient using the sample SD (divisor n−1). It is a FlippedStat calculation.

Wave-1 and wave-2 keys are unchanged (10 vs 8; HK$30,350 vs 33,800; IQRs 5,600 vs 11,650; r = −0.38; region totals/shares; five-number summary; z-scores; mean/median of medians).

## Topics changed this wave

### 4.3 Transformations — replaced

The student-facing log/sqrt example is the official 2016–2025 daily rainfall extract at the Hong Kong Observatory. Measurable wet-day amounts are strongly right-skewed; a base-10 log is nearly symmetric (Pearson skew −0.14). Official Trace values are kept as Trace. OpenIntro’s 3,142 US-county population histograms remain a labelled book illustration. The Likert recoding walk-through in 4.3.1 was not changed.

### 6.3 Poisson distribution and rare events — replaced

The student-facing count is the number of June, July and August days, 2016–2025, with at least one official cloud-to-ground lightning record (mean 17.17, sample variance 18.35). Daily stroke totals are described but not used as a constant-rate Poisson example. Official monthly live births (table 115-01012A) are a labelled caution that a published count can have a changing rate (official annual totals 60,856 in 2016 and 31,053 in 2025). OpenIntro’s New York AMI figure remains a labelled book illustration. Book exercises were not rewritten.

### 6.5 The normal distribution — replaced

The student-facing official illustration is the 920 June–August 2016–2025 official daily mean temperatures at the Hong Kong Observatory (mean 29.23 °C, sample SD 1.35 °C; 68.8 / 95.1 / 99.8% within 1 / 2 / 3 sample SDs). The lesson states that this is a course illustration and does **not** claim that the official series is exactly normal. The full-year series is shown only as a contrast (seasonal cycle). SAT scores and US adult heights remain labelled book illustrations; keyed SAT/height checks in 6.5.2 were not rewritten.

# FlippedStat — Hong Kong data localisation inventory, wave 4 (parallels) (18 Nov 2026)

Times below are Asia/Hong_Kong. This is a short parallels note, not a new data fetch. Wave 1 is in `logs/HK_DATA_LOCALISATION_INVENTORY_2026-11-18.md`; wave 2 in `...-wave2.md`; wave 3 in `...-wave3.md`. The machine-readable companion (all 209 inventory rows, with the four supplemented official topics updated) is `logs/HK_DATA_LOCALISATION_INVENTORY_2026-11-18-wave4.csv`.

Standing instruction (Mike Kan, t27u / t30u): when reviewing each page and each sub-topic, try to replace US-textbook-centred contexts with licence-clean Hong Kong public data. This wave adds labelled parallels only. `hkdatasets` microdata remains uncleared and is not shipped.

Official modules remain Modules 1–8 (153 topics). Module 9 was not treated as approved and was not edited.

## What this wave reviewed

The 33 deferred official topics and the 5 named case studies (C4.1, C4.2, C4.7, C4.8, C4.9) from the wave-3 inventory were re-read against official extracts *already in the tree*. Quality over volume: a parallel was added only where an existing official extract cleanly illustrates the teaching point, clearly separate from keyed textbook or Navarro examples.

No new official table was fetched. Weather and birth series already used in wave 3 were not reused as iid samples for confidence intervals, tests, or the central limit theorem, because they are time-ordered and serially dependent. Named historical cases were not relocated or dropped.

Topics supplemented this wave: **9.7, 10.3, 10.6, 11.4**. Wave-1, wave-2 and wave-3 teaching text and keys were left as in v10.6-dev.

## Worked numbers added this wave (FlippedStat calculations, not official C&SD statistics)

All four boxes use the existing teaching file `hk_district_profile_2016_2025.csv` (C&SD tables 110-02001 and 130-06806).

- Pearson r = **−0.38** between the 18 official 2025 district median monthly household incomes and official 2025 densities — already a wave-1 key on Topics 4.1–4.2; reused, not recomputed as a new official figure.
- The corresponding R² = r² is about **0.14**: a straight line accounts for about 14% of the variation in these 18 official district median incomes.
- On the simple line of official 2025 median income on official 2025 density: average hat-value (K+1)/n = 2/18 ≈ 0.11; Kwun Tong (official density 59,400 persons per sq. km) has hat-value **0.31** (above the 2× guide, a little under the 3× guide); Islands (official density 1,090) has hat-value 0.11; Central and Western has the largest ordinary residual and hat-value 0.06. Cook’s distances: Kwun Tong **0.04**; largest of the 18 is Central and Western **0.15**. Both are well below the page’s rule that Dᵢ > 1 is large.
- Official 2025 density is defined from mid-year land population and land area. A regression of official log-density on log(population) and log(area) for the 18 districts has R² = **1.000** to three decimal places; official density and population ÷ area differ by under 0.2%. Putting all three columns in one linear model asks the official definition twice.

Wave-1, wave-2 and wave-3 keys are unchanged.

## Topics supplemented this wave

### 9.7 Correlation and its limits — supplemented

A labelled official-data illustration was added to lesson 9.7.3. It reuses Pearson r = −0.38 from Topics 4.1–4.2 to show the limits of r: n = 18 is small; the association is ecological (district aggregates, not households); a moderate linear association is not a law for every district; r does not describe a curve. OpenIntro scatterplots, the Spearman walk-through, and the Guided Practice 8.3 check were not changed.

### 10.3 Residuals and R-squared — supplemented

A labelled official-data illustration was added to lesson 10.3.4. With r = −0.38, R² is about 0.14: the line accounts for about 14% of the variation in the 18 official district median incomes; most of the variation is residual. The keyed sleep/grumpiness spreadsheet (R² = 0.8161), the Elmhurst aid figure (R = −0.499, R² = 0.25), and the Guided Practice 8.7 check (r = −0.97) were not changed.

### 10.6 Outliers, leverage and influence — supplemented

A labelled official-data illustration was added to lesson 10.6.1, after the parenthood Cook’s-distance figure. Kwun Tong is high leverage by the page’s 2× guide (hat-value 0.31) but is not highly influential (Cook’s D = 0.04). Central and Western has the largest residual and the largest Cook’s D (0.15), still well below Dᵢ > 1, and is not high-leverage on density. High leverage is not the same as high influence. The parenthood summary and book residual plots were not changed.

### 11.4 Multicollinearity — supplemented

A labelled official-data illustration was added to lesson 11.4.3. Official 2025 density is defined from mid-year land population and land area. On the log scale that definition is almost exact (R² = 1.000 to three decimal places; leftover is published-figure rounding). Putting all three columns into one linear model asks the official definition twice. The parenthood correlation matrix and VIF figures were not changed.

## Still deferred after this wave

| Topic or file | Why still deferred |
|---|---|
| 1.4, 1.6, 8.9 | Keyed Navarro / LSJ files (`booksales.csv`, `broca.csv`, `chico.csv`, `parenthood`). The teaching object is a verification or integrity workflow on those files. Replacement needs a coordinated recompute and QA-ledger update. |
| 5.6, 5.7 | Conditional probability and independence need a clean two-way table of people or trials. The 18 district aggregates do not cleanly illustrate P(A\|B) versus P(B\|A), or independence of events. |
| 6.6, 6.7 | Simulation / LLN and the rare-event copilot lab are about Monte Carlo behaviour and lab keys. Official series were not mixed into those keys. The official lightning example already sits on Topic 6.3. |
| 7.2, 7.3, 7.6, 7.7, 7.8, 7.9, 7.10 | Sampling distributions, the CLT, confidence intervals, differences and sample size assume draws that can honestly be treated as random and (for the usual intervals) independent. Official daily weather and monthly births are time-ordered and serially dependent; the 18 districts are a census of areas, not a random sample of people. A “finite list, ignore date order” box would risk teaching the wrong independence story. |
| 8.3, 8.4, 8.5, 8.6, 8.8 | Power, t-tests, chi-square, ANOVA and multiple comparisons have the same sampling-design problem, plus keyed book exercises. Gained-versus-lost district groups are observational and already used descriptively in Topics 2.1–2.2. |
| 9.2 | The teaching object is Simpson’s paradox via the historical Berkeley admissions tables (and the age-gap audit). No official extract already in the tree is a clean three-way reversal table. |
| 10.1, 10.2, 10.4 | Keyed Navarro / OpenIntro regression numbers (parenthood, possums, unemployment). The official scatter is already used for correlation, R² and leverage on 9.7 / 10.3 / 10.6; a further slope box would repeat the same 18 points and would introduce a new slope that is not a wave-1 key. Slope inference would also treat 18 census districts as a random sample. |
| 11.1, 11.2 | Multiple regression and indicators. n = 18 with a three-level region factor is a thin fit; 11.2’s teaching object includes Mario Kart. Definitional collinearity is already illustrated on 11.4. |
| E1.12 | Rank-based tests. The hook is a keyed reaction-time example. Official 10-versus-8 district income groups are observational area medians, not a clean rank-test demonstration, and would require a new p-value. |
| E5.11 | Keyed Harbourside forecast lab. Optional official CPI practice remains at E5.2. Official monthly series were not mixed into those keys. |
| C4.5 | Two-proportion special topics with a Mario Kart / book context; no clean official two-proportion extract in the tree. |
| 12.6 | Bias in data and models (Chicago / OpenIntro). Official district or weather extracts do not cleanly illustrate algorithmic or data-collection bias. |
| Named case studies C4.1, C4.2, C4.7, C4.8, C4.9 | Stents, malaria vaccine, Mario Kart auctions, résumé callbacks, and possums / college aid / elections. A parallel HK case would be an addition, not a drop-in replacement. No official extract already in the tree is a clean match for those named studies. |
| Keyed Navarro / LSJ files (`clinicaltrial.csv`, `chico.csv`, `broca.csv`, `ancova.csv`, `ASQ.csv`, `parenthood.csv`, `booksales.csv`) | Still too risky without a coordinated recompute and QA-ledger update. |

# FlippedStat — Hong Kong data localisation inventory, wave 5 (18 Nov 2026)

Times below are Asia/Hong_Kong. Wave 1 is in `logs/HK_DATA_LOCALISATION_INVENTORY_2026-11-18.md`; wave 2 in `...-wave2.md`; wave 3 in `...-wave3.md`; wave 4 in `...-wave4.md`. The machine-readable companion (all 209 inventory rows, with the 34 previously deferred official Modules 1–8 topics updated) is `logs/HK_DATA_LOCALISATION_INVENTORY_2026-11-18-wave5.csv`.

Standing instruction (Mike Kan, t32u, 18 Nov 2026): leave copyright issues to a later stage and adapt the contents first. Formal rights clearance (H7, Barocas/fairmlbook, ModernDive ShareAlike, hkdatasets package-licence inconsistency) remains deferred and is **not claimed as done**. This wave does not invent licences or department legal approval.

Official modules remain Modules 1–8 (153 topics). Module 9 was not treated as approved and was not edited.

## What this wave reviewed

All 29 official topics still deferred after wave 4, and the 5 named case studies (C4.1, C4.2, C4.7, C4.8, C4.9), were adapted now. Quality over volume, but this is a substantial pass: a labelled official-data or synthetic-HK parallel was added on every one of those official topics, while keyed textbook answers were left in place.

No new official table was fetched. Official calculations reuse extracts already in `content/data/hk_extracts/` (C&SD tables 110-02001 and 130-06806). Official daily weather and monthly birth *series* were not treated as iid random samples. The 18 districts were not treated as a random sample of people. Where a mean, t-test, ANOVA, rank test, or Simpson reversal needed individual-level or three-way teaching data that those official extracts cannot honestly supply, a labelled FlippedStat synthetic teaching table was used instead.

Named historical cases were kept as labelled citations/illustrations. A paraphrased parallel was added; the named study was not silently deleted. Keyed Navarro / LSJ files were not replaced. Placement / pre-post keys and open QA-ledger rows were not rewritten. Wave-1 to wave-4 official-extract keys were left unchanged. hkdatasets microdata was not shipped. Personal identifiers and casualty microdata were not shipped. `stage8/` was not edited.

## Worked numbers added this wave (FlippedStat calculations, not official C&SD statistics)

**Official 2025 mid-year land population, with a FlippedStat gained/lost flag** (18 published district figures sum to 7,497.9 thousand; official Hong Kong total 7,497.8 thousand; New Territories district figures sum to 4,092.8 against an official regional total of 4,092.7):

- P(lives in a gained-population district) = 4,831.0 / 7,497.9 = **64.4%**.
- P(gained | Hong Kong Island) = **0%**; P(gained | Kowloon) = 1,535.3 / 2,242.7 = **68.5%**; P(gained | New Territories) = 3,295.7 / 4,092.8 = **80.5%**.
- P(Kowloon | gained) = 1,535.3 / 4,831.0 = **31.8%** (not 68.5%).
- Under independence, expected official 2025 population in gained-population districts on Hong Kong Island would be about **749 thousand**; the observed figure is **0**. That comparison is a description of official aggregates, not a chi-square test of a random sample.

**Official New Territories share** 4,092.7 / 7,497.8 = **54.6%** (already a wave-2 teaching share), used as a known population proportion:

- For n = 400, SE = √(p(1 − p)/n) ≈ **0.0249**; a typical 95% Wald margin of error is about **4.9** percentage points; np ≈ 218 and n(1 − p) ≈ 182.
- Planning n for a 95% margin of 3 percentage points, using 54.6% as a planning value: **1,059** (or 1,068 at the conservative p = 0.5).
- Planning power ≈ **0.83** for a two-sided α = 0.05 test of H₀: p = 0.50 with n = 1,000, if the true p were the official 54.6%. The official table itself is not tested.
- Official Islands share 198.4 / 7,497.8 ≈ **2.65%**; P(at least one Islands resident in 50 independent draws) ≈ **74%**. The keyed 6.7 lab benchmark **0.0802** is unchanged.

**Descriptive official income-on-density line** (18 official 2025 pairs; r = −0.38 and R² ≈ 0.14 already on Topics 4.1–4.2 and 10.3):

- Least-squares line: median income (HK$) ≈ **34,283 − 0.121 × density**, or about HK$121 lower district median income per additional 1,000 persons per sq. km. Census summary of these official pairs, not a household slope and not a sampling estimate. A formula-SE is not reported as a test result (Topic 10.4).
- Descriptive multiple regression with region indicators (Hong Kong Island reference): median income ≈ **43,380 − 0.230 × density − 5,127 × Kowloon − 10,982 × New Territories**, R² about **0.59**. n = 18 with four parameters is a thin fit; coefficient p-values are not reported as sampling tests. Unadjusted means of official 2025 district medians: HK$39,425 (Hong Kong Island, n = 4), HK$27,420 (Kowloon, n = 5), HK$30,933 (New Territories, n = 9). Those means of medians are not official regional medians (the official Hong Kong median in 2025 is HK$30,000).

**Labelled synthetic teaching tables** (not official CUHK, Hospital Authority, or C&SD data):

- Hostel-floor midterm quiz scores — quiet: 78, 74, 81, 69, 75, 77 (mean 75.67, sample SD 4.08); mixed: 70, 68, 73, 65, 71, 67 (mean 69.00, SD 2.90); social: 60, 64, 58, 66, 61, 63 (mean 62.00, SD 2.90); n = 6 each. Quiet-floor 95% t interval about **71.4 to 80.0**. Welch quiet vs social: difference 13.67, 95% interval about **9.0 to 18.3**, t ≈ 6.69, df ≈ 9.0, p ≈ 0.00009. One-sample quiet vs 70: t = 3.40, df = 5, p ≈ 0.019. ANOVA: F ≈ **25.12** on 2 and 15 df, p ≈ 0.000016, η² ≈ 0.77. Tukey HSD: all three pairs significant at 95% family-wise. Mann–Whitney U = 36, p ≈ 0.002; Kruskal–Wallis H ≈ 13.56, df = 2, p ≈ 0.0011.
- Simpson clinic table: Clinic B has the higher recovery rate in each need group (80% vs 70% lower-need; 30% vs 20% higher-need) but the lower pooled rate (42.5% vs 62.9%), because it sees more higher-need patients. Berkeley 1973 remains the named historical illustration.
- Exam-support 2×2: 12/80 vs 24/80 missed a deadline; z ≈ −2.27, p ≈ 0.023 (Fisher exact p ≈ 0.036). The stent trial, including 45/224, is kept.
- Second-hand textbook scatter (8 listings): price ≈ **192.38 − 15.39 × (years since publication)**, r = −0.983, R² ≈ 0.97. Mario Kart remains the named case study.

Wave-1, wave-2, wave-3 and wave-4 keys are unchanged.

# FlippedStat — Hong Kong data localisation inventory (18 Nov 2026)

Standing instruction (Mike Kan, 18 Nov 2026): when reviewing each page and each sub-topic, try to replace US-textbook-centred contexts and datasets with the R package [hkdatasets](https://github.com/Hong-Kong-Districts-Info/hkdatasets) or Hong Kong public APIs / open data.

This inventory covers official Modules 1–8 first (153 topics). Module 9 / electives appear only as a short appendix. A machine-readable companion is `logs/HK_DATA_LOCALISATION_INVENTORY_2026-11-18.csv`.

Times below are Asia/Hong_Kong. Official figures were retrieved from C&SD APIs on 18 Nov 2026, about 02:41.

## How the review was done

Source pages reviewed, not filenames only:

- Official topic lists in `content/modules93.py` (Modules 1–8 reportable; Module 9 optional).
- Rewritten lesson bodies in `content/absorb_*.py` and `content/e5_content.py` (subtopic keys such as 4.1.1, E5.2.1).
- Later additions and R-first cards in `content/rev90.py`, `content/rfirst94.py`, `content/codeprompt100.py`.
- Placement items in `content/placement99.py` (constructs and stems only; cut scores not touched).
- Bundled synthetic files in `tools/rev90_data.py`.
- Topic titles from `stage8/slides/topics/manifest.json`.

Already-Hong Kong *synthetic* examples (Harbourside demand/temperature, harbour water, CUHK-style `survey300` / `satisfaction300` / `wellbeing300` / `sleep_column`, Sha Tin / MTR items, the MTR vs bus commute comparison, and similar) were **kept**. They were not silently replaced, and their keyed worked numbers were not changed.

A first useful wave of replacements was implemented where the mapping was clean, the licence was read from the source, the teaching point was preserved, and any new worked numbers were recomputed in Python. Other US or textbook examples were deferred with a reason, or kept as clearly labelled designated-textbook illustrations.

Topics 1.1 and 13.2 were reviewed for context but **not edited**, to avoid racing a sibling v10.3-dev polish of those pages.

## Licence findings (not legal advice; no department sign-off recorded)

### hkdatasets

Reviewed from the GitHub master tree and CRAN DESCRIPTION on 18 Nov 2026.

- README lists `hkdc`, `hkstreetnames20`, `hkdistrict_summary`, and (via `download_data()` from v1.0.0) `hk_accidents`, `hk_casualties`, `hk_vehicles`. An additional in-package file, `hkagepop19` (2019 age-by-district population; source named as C&SD product FA100096), is not in the README excerpt but is in the package.
- The README carries an **MIT** badge. The package **DESCRIPTION states Licence: GPL-3**, and also states: “All of the data in this package is available in the public domain.” No licence file was returned by the GitHub licence API. This discrepancy is recorded; it is not resolved here.
- Underlying sources named by the package (districtcouncils.gov.hk, dce2019.hk01.com, Lands Department, Transport Department FOI microdata) may have their own terms. Those terms were **not** treated as cleared by the package’s public-domain sentence.
- `hkdc` includes names, office addresses, telephone numbers, emails and social-media URLs. It is not shipped. Traffic-casualty microdata are not shipped (ethical caution; do not identify individuals; do not sensationalise deaths). Street names are deferred until Lands Department terms are read from the source.
- Students are not required to `install.packages("hkdatasets")` inside Moodle or WebR. An optional desktop-R snippet is documented in the extracts folder. Curated CSVs are the supported path.

### C&SD and DATA.GOV.HK (used this pass)

Terms were read from the sources on 18 Nov 2026:

- [C&SD Intellectual Property Rights Notice](https://www.censtatd.gov.hk/en/page_31.html): specified statistical information (tables, datasets, reports and related statistical content, **excluding** maps, photographs, graphics, drawings, logos, audio and video) may be downloaded, printed, adapted, distributed, reproduced and hyperlinked to, free, for commercial and non-commercial use, if the C&SD website is acknowledged as the source, the Government is acknowledged as the intellectual property owner, and modifications are clearly indicated.
- [DATA.GOV.HK Terms of Use](https://data.gov.hk/en/terms-and-conditions): browsing, download, distribution, reproduction, hyperlinking and printing, commercial or non-commercial, free, with source identification, acknowledgement of Government / relevant-organisation IP ownership, and attribution to the Government, the relevant organisations and DATA.GOV.HK. Data are provided “AS IS”. Use is not government endorsement.

This pass therefore prefers official C&SD web-table APIs listed on data.gov.hk over unverified package microdata.

Official extracts shipped (each with a codebook):

| Teaching file | Official table | What was modified |
|---|---|---|
| `hk_district_population_110-02001.csv` | 110-02001, years 2016 and 2025 only | Subset of years; figures copied |
| `hk_district_household_130-06806.csv` | 130-06806, years 2016 and 2025, series `ADHS` and `MED_DH_INC` only | Subset; two further API income series omitted because published English labels were not verified |
| `hk_district_profile_2016_2025.csv` | Join of the two tables, 18 districts | Derived columns (`land_pop_change_000`, `population_gained`) labelled as FlippedStat calculations |
| `hk_cpi_composite_monthly_510-60001.csv` | 510-60001, Composite CPI monthly, Jan 2015–Sep 2026 | Subset of series and dates; figures copied |
| `hk_district_lookup.csv` | District codes and English names as in those C&SD tables; region names matching 110-02001 region totals | Teaching lookup, not a statistical table |

Worked numbers computed on the 18-row profile (not official C&SD statistics; method in the profile codebook):

- 10 districts gained mid-year land population between 2016 and 2025; 8 lost (none unchanged).
- Median of 2025 district median monthly household incomes: **HK$30,350** (gained group) vs **HK$33,800** (lost group).
- IQR of those district medians (median of each half): **HK$5,600** vs **HK$11,650**.
- Pearson r of 2025 median income vs 2025 density, n = 18: **−0.38**.
- Hong Kong-wide official totals in the source tables (context only): mid-year land population 7,335.4 thousand (2016) and 7,497.8 thousand (2025); official median monthly household income HK$25,200 (2016) and HK$30,000 (2025).

A median of district medians is not the official Hong Kong median. The 18 rows are area aggregates, not households.

## Topics changed this pass

### 2.1 Data rectangles and encoding

`hk_district_profile_2016_2025.csv` is now the file students import first. Navarro’s `booksales.csv` and its jamovi figure remain as a designated-textbook illustration (CC BY-SA 4.0). The four import questions (header, decimal, quote, separator, encoding) are unchanged. Big5 guidance for older Hong Kong files is kept.

### 2.2 Importing and checking

The primary filter example is `region_en == "New Territories"` on the 18-row official-extract file (9 rows remain). `nightgarden.csv` is retained as a labelled textbook illustration. The keyed toy-data count “n = 10 utterances” is still stated for that illustration and was not altered. `sleep_column.csv` is kept.

### 4.1 Comparing groups

The primary worked example is the official 18-district table: compare 2025 median monthly household incomes for districts that gained vs lost mid-year land population from 2016 to 2025. The centre goes the **other way** from OpenIntro’s US-county illustration (lost-population districts have the higher median of district medians). That contrast is taught as an observational warning, not as a causal finding. OpenIntro US-county figures and book dollar figures remain in a labelled illustration box and are not mixed with the Hong Kong numbers. The existing synthetic MTR vs bus comparison in the revision layer is kept. `clinicaltrial.csv` in 4.1.3 is **deferred** (mean mood gain 0.88; reused in ANOVA weeks).

### 4.2 Two numerical variables

Primary student scatter: 2025 official median income vs density (r = −0.38). OpenIntro’s US income–poverty scatter is a labelled book illustration. No official district poverty-rate series was verified, so that pair was not relocated. `parenthood.csv` is deferred (keyed regression weeks).

### 4.4 Visual encoding and chart choice

C&SD maps are not reproduced. Students read a ranked official table of 18 district incomes and densities. OpenIntro US-county maps remain labelled illustrations. The self-check now asks what stands out in the Hong Kong table (Central and Western / Wan Chai highest medians; Kwun Tong / Sham Shui Po lowest). The Australian AFL filter-and-bar example in 4.4.2 is deferred.

### E5.2 What makes a time series different (Module 7)

Optional official Composite CPI monthly series added for date-indexing practice. Synthetic Harbourside keys are unchanged. Think Stats U.S. EIA electricity is labelled a designated-textbook illustration. Other E5 topics still mention US electricity or nuclear generation as book illustrations; those keyed Harbourside steps were not moved.

## Placement and assessment

- Placement test (`content/placement99.py`): 20 items reviewed. Stems are already Hong Kong or construct-generic. **No item was rewritten.** Correct option indices and cut-score constants were not changed. Item review is not claimed to be done (H3 remains a human decision).

- `#codeprompt` examples already use `sleep_column.csv` (synthetic HK-style). No US textbook file was the primary prompt file there.

## FSINT / WebR / site assembly

New CSVs and codebooks live in `content/data/hk_extracts/` and are also written to `build/hk_files.json` by `python tools/hk_local_data.py`. To mount them like existing rev90 files (FSR download buttons and WebR):

```
python tools/hk_local_data.py --merge-rev90
```

That command **appends** keys and will refuse to overwrite existing rev90 keys. `tools/rev90_data.py` itself was not changed except for a pointer comment.

No new standalone HTML was assembled in this pass. `build/FlippedStat_v10.3-dev_standalone.html` was already present (sibling work) and was **not** overwritten. Frozen standalones listed in the brief were not modified. A later v10.4-dev assemble should start from v10.3-dev (read-only), rebuild absorbed lesson data from the edited `absorb_*.py` / `e5_content.py` / `rev90.py` sources, merge the HK files, and run checks.

## Student-facing licence text

A “Data sources in the lessons” section was appended to the existing licence HTML in `content/rev90.py` (`LICENCE`). The original textbook-licence paragraphs were not rewritten. Official extracts, synthetic FlippedStat files, and designated-textbook illustrations are distinguished. Government endorsement is explicitly disclaimed.
