========== FILE: ws/stage1/moodle/package/privacy_retention_DRAFT.md ==========

# Privacy and data retention — DRAFT (requires CUHK confirmation, decision H11)
This is a working draft prepared by Copilot to structure the discussion; it is not legal advice and has not been checked against CUHK policy.
- Purpose: course delivery and evaluation of the TDLEG project (KPIs and research evaluation).
- Data collected in Moodle: login, enrolment, activity completion, quiz responses, survey responses, certificate issue.
- Analysis files: pseudonymised (salted hash of the login). The salt and the re-identification key are held by the Principal Supervisor only.
- No student data are entered into public AI tools at any stage of the evaluation.
- Retention: raw exports on CUHK storage for the project period plus the period set by the department; pseudonymised analysis files retained for reporting; deletion recorded.
- Before the first cohort: personal information collection statement on the course page; check with ORKTS whether ethics review is required for publication of results.

========== END FILE: ws/stage1/moodle/package/privacy_retention_DRAFT.md ==========


========== FILE: ws/stage1/moodle/package/uptime_monitoring_spec.md ==========

# Uptime and SSO monitoring specification (KPI 1.2)
- Probe: an external HTTPS check every 5 minutes on (1) the Moodle course URL and (2) the hosted FlippedStat site URL. Down = no HTTP 200 within 30 s for two consecutive probes.
- SSO: a scripted or manual CUHK login test on the first working day of each month; record pass/fail in `uptime.csv`.
- Monthly figure = 1 − minutes_down ÷ (minutes in month − announced maintenance). Target ≥ 99% (≤ about 7 h 18 min unplanned downtime in a 30-day month).
- Announced maintenance must be posted on the course page at least 48 h ahead to be excluded.
- Note: the offline standalone file is a backup route for learners; it does not count towards uptime.

========== END FILE: ws/stage1/moodle/package/uptime_monitoring_spec.md ==========

# FlippedStat v9.9 — R confirmation harness for the statistical QA ledger (Stage 1, S1.2)
# Run:  Rscript run_in_R.R  [data_dir]
# Part A needs only base R (+ stats). Part B needs the textbook data files in data_dir
# (chico.csv, broca.csv, ancova.csv, the scale/EFA/CFA item files used in E4.5.2, E4.6.3, C3.5) and packages psych, car, lavaan.
# Record each PASS/CHECK line in the ledger column "Decision" with your initials and date.
args <- commandArgs(TRUE); dd <- if (length(args)) args[1] else "data"
ok <- function(id, label, got, exp, tol) { pass <- abs(got - exp) <= tol
  cat(sprintf("%-8s %-34s R=%-12.6g printed=%-12.6g %s\n", id, label, got, exp, if (pass) "PASS" else "** FAIL **")); invisible(pass) }
cat("== Part A: self-contained checks ==\n")
clin.trial <- data.frame(
  drug = factor(rep(c("placebo","anxifree","joyzepam","placebo","anxifree","joyzepam"), each = 3), levels = c("placebo","anxifree","joyzepam")),
  therapy = factor(rep(c("no.therapy","CBT"), each = 9), levels = c("no.therapy","CBT")),
  mood.gain = c(.5,.3,.1, .6,.4,.2, 1.4,1.7,1.3, .6,.9,.3, 1.1,.8,1.2, 1.8,1.3,1.4))
a <- summary(aov(mood.gain ~ drug + therapy, data = clin.trial))[[1]]
ok("QA-0533","drug F",a[1,"F value"],26.15,.005); ok("QA-0533","therapy F",a[2,"F value"],7.08,.005)
b <- summary(aov(mood.gain ~ drug * therapy, data = clin.trial))[[1]]
ok("QA-0534","drug F",b[1,"F value"],31.71,.005); ok("QA-0534","drug:therapy p",b[3,"Pr(>F)"],0.125,5e-4)
ms <- b[4,"Mean Sq"]; ok("QA-0535","SE = sqrt(MSE/3)",sqrt(ms/3),0.135,5e-4)
print(contr.treatment(3)); print(contr.sum(3)); print(contr.helmert(3))
r <- sapply(list(contr.treatment, contr.sum, contr.helmert), function(f) { ct2 <- clin.trial; contrasts(ct2$drug) <- f(3); deviance(lm(mood.gain ~ drug + therapy, ct2)) })
ok("QA-0532","RSS range across codings",diff(range(r)),0,1e-10)
ok("QA-0545","nested F",anova(lm(mood.gain ~ therapy, clin.trial), lm(mood.gain ~ drug + therapy, clin.trial))$F[2],26.149,5e-4)
ok("QA-0540","K-W chi-squared",kruskal.test(mood.gain ~ drug, data = clin.trial)$statistic,12.076,5e-4)
aw <- data.frame(scores = c(6.4,10.7,11.9,7.3,10,14.5,10.4,12.9,11.7,13), group = rep(c("A","B"), each = 5))
w <- wilcox.test(scores ~ group, data = aw); ok("QA-0538","W",w$statistic,3,0); ok("QA-0538","p",w$p.value,.05556,5e-6)
v <- wilcox.test(c(6,29,11,31,17,2,31,21,8,21), c(30,43,21,24,23,40,29,56,38,16), paired = TRUE); ok("QA-0539","V",v$statistic,7,0); ok("QA-0539","p",v$p.value,.03711,5e-6)
ok("QA-0541","Fisher p",fisher.test(matrix(c(0,10,3,3),2))$p.value,.03571,5e-6)
ok("QA-0542","McNemar chi2",mcnemar.test(matrix(c(65,5,25,5),2))$statistic,12.033,5e-4)
cat("\n== QA-0549: analyse_prepost.R on the synthetic fixture (compare with stage1/qa/_py_modules.csv) ==\n")
if (file.exists("SYNTHETIC_responses_fixture.csv")) system("Rscript analyse_prepost.R SYNTHETIC_responses_fixture.csv fixture") else cat("copy logs/SYNTHETIC_responses_fixture.csv and exports/analyse_prepost.R (canonical copy) here first\n")
cat("\n== Part B: data-dependent checks (data_dir =", dd, ") ==\n")
f <- function(x) file.path(dd, x)
if (file.exists(f("chico.csv"))) { chico <- read.csv(f("chico.csv")); t <- t.test(chico$grade_test2, chico$grade_test1, paired = TRUE)
  ok("QA-0536","t",t$statistic,6.48,.005); ok("QA-0536","df",t$parameter,19,0); ok("QA-0536","mean difference",t$estimate,1.4,.05) } else cat("QA-0536 SKIP: chico.csv missing\n")
if (file.exists(f("broca.csv"))) { broca <- read.csv(f("broca.csv"))
  long <- reshape(broca, direction = "long", varying = c("speech","conceptual","syntax"), v.names = "score", timevar = "task", idvar = "id")
  print(summary(aov(score ~ factor(task) + Error(factor(id)/factor(task)), data = long))); print(friedman.test(as.matrix(broca[, c("speech","conceptual","syntax")])))
  cat("QA-0537 CHECK: compare the Within-stratum factor(task) row and Friedman chi-squared with lesson E1.6.1\n") } else cat("QA-0537 SKIP: broca.csv missing\n")

========== FILE: ws/stage1/qa/s12_emulate_R.py ==========

"""Emulate exports/analyse_prepost.R line by line with R's default semantics, and compare to exports/analyse_prepost.py.
R defaults that matter: wilcox.test(paired=TRUE) uses the exact distribution only if n < 50 AND no ties/zeros,
otherwise the normal approximation WITH continuity correction (correct = TRUE); zeros are dropped."""
import sys,subprocess,numpy as np,pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
src=sys.argv[1]
d=pd.read_csv(src); d=d[d.timestamp==d.groupby(['pid','module','form']).timestamp.transform('max')]
sc=d.groupby(['module','pid','form']).correct.mean().rename('correct').reset_index()
an=d[d.anchor==1].groupby(['module','pid','form']).correct.mean().rename('anchor').reset_index()
sc=sc.merge(an)
def r_wilcox(b,a):
    dd=b-a; dd=dd[dd!=0]; n=len(dd); r=stats.rankdata(abs(dd)); V=r[dd>0].sum()
    ties=len(np.unique(abs(dd)))<n
    if n<50 and not ties: return stats.wilcoxon(dd,method='exact').pvalue, 'exact'
    _,cnt=np.unique(r,return_counts=True); mu=n*(n+1)/4; sig=np.sqrt(n*(n+1)*(2*n+1)/24-(cnt**3-cnt).sum()/48)
    z=(V-mu-np.sign(V-mu)*0.5)/sig; return 2*min(stats.norm.cdf(z),stats.norm.sf(z)),'normal+cc'
rows=[];errs=[]
for m,g in sc.groupby('module'):
    w=g.pivot(index='pid',columns='form',values=['correct','anchor']).dropna(); n=len(w); started=g[g.form=='pre'].pid.nunique()
    a=100*w[('correct','pre')].values; b=100*w[('correct','post')].values; dd=b-a
    if n<2 or dd.std()==0: errs.append(f'module {m}: t.test would stop with an error (n={n}, constant differences)'); continue
    t=stats.ttest_rel(b,a); ci=stats.t.interval(.95,n-1,loc=dd.mean(),scale=stats.sem(dd)); pw,meth=r_wilcox(b,a)
    rows.append(dict(module=m,n_matched=n,abs_gain=round(dd.mean(),1),ci_low=round(ci[0],1),ci_high=round(ci[1],1),rel_gain_pct=round(100*dd.mean()/a.mean(),1),
        t=round(t.statistic,2),p_t=round(t.pvalue,4),p_wilcoxon_R=round(pw,4),wilcox_method_R=meth,d_z=round(dd.mean()/dd.std(ddof=1),2)))
Rr=pd.DataFrame(rows)
subprocess.run([sys.executable,'exports/analyse_prepost.py',src,'stage1/qa/_py'],capture_output=True,check=True)
P=pd.read_csv('stage1/qa/_py_modules.csv')
c=Rr.merge(P,on='module',suffixes=('_R','_py'))
out=[]
for col in ['n_matched','abs_gain','ci_low','ci_high','rel_gain_pct','t','p_t','d_z']:
    diff=(c[col+'_R']-c[col+'_py']).abs().max(); out.append((col,diff))
pdiff=(c.p_wilcoxon_R-c.p_wilcoxon).abs()
print('max |R - Python| per statistic:'); [print(f'  {k:14s} {v:.6g}') for k,v in out]
print(f'  p_wilcoxon     {pdiff.max():.6g}  (R method used: {c.wilcox_method_R.value_counts().to_dict()})')
print('R-script failure modes on this input:',errs or 'none')
c[['module','p_wilcoxon_R','p_wilcoxon','wilcox_method_R']].to_csv('stage1/qa/s12_wilcoxon_R_vs_py.csv',index=False)

========== END FILE: ws/stage1/qa/s12_emulate_R.py ==========

========== FILE: ws/stage1/qa/s12_verify.py ==========

"""S1.2 independent reproduction of R-first expected outputs (QA-0532..0548) in Python, mirroring R defaults.
clin.trial is reconstructed from the values printed in Learning Statistics with R/jamovi (Navarro & Foxcroft);
the reconstruction is accepted only if it reproduces every printed statistic below."""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, json
from scipy import stats
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from statsmodels.stats.anova import anova_lm
R=[]
def chk(qa,label,got,exp,tol):
    ok=abs(got-exp)<=tol; R.append(dict(qa=qa,check=label,python=round(float(got),6),printed=exp,tol=tol,ok=bool(ok))); return ok
mg={('placebo','no.therapy'):[.5,.3,.1],('anxifree','no.therapy'):[.6,.4,.2],('joyzepam','no.therapy'):[1.4,1.7,1.3],
    ('placebo','CBT'):[.6,.9,.3],('anxifree','CBT'):[1.1,.8,1.2],('joyzepam','CBT'):[1.8,1.3,1.4]}
ct=pd.DataFrame([dict(drug=d,therapy=t,mood_gain=v) for (d,t),vs in mg.items() for v in vs])
ct['drug']=pd.Categorical(ct.drug,['placebo','anxifree','joyzepam']); ct['therapy']=pd.Categorical(ct.therapy,['no.therapy','CBT'])
# QA-0533 additive ANOVA (R aov = sequential type I)
a=anova_lm(smf.ols('mood_gain ~ drug + therapy',ct).fit(),typ=1)
chk('QA-0533','drug SS',a.loc['drug','sum_sq'],3.453,5e-4); chk('QA-0533','drug F',a.loc['drug','F'],26.15,5e-3); chk('QA-0533','drug p',a.loc['drug','PR(>F)'],1.9e-5,5e-7)
chk('QA-0533','therapy SS',a.loc['therapy','sum_sq'],0.467,5e-4); chk('QA-0533','therapy F',a.loc['therapy','F'],7.08,5e-3); chk('QA-0533','therapy p',a.loc['therapy','PR(>F)'],0.019,5e-4)
chk('QA-0533','residual df',a.loc['Residual','df'],14,0)
# QA-0534 interaction model
b=anova_lm(smf.ols('mood_gain ~ drug * therapy',ct).fit(),typ=1)
chk('QA-0534','drug F',b.loc['drug','F'],31.71,5e-3); chk('QA-0534','drug p',b.loc['drug','PR(>F)'],1.6e-5,5e-7)
chk('QA-0534','therapy F',b.loc['therapy','F'],8.58,5e-3); chk('QA-0534','therapy p',b.loc['therapy','PR(>F)'],0.013,5e-4)
chk('QA-0534','drug:therapy F',b.loc['drug:therapy','F'],2.49,5e-3); chk('QA-0534','drug:therapy p',b.loc['drug:therapy','PR(>F)'],0.125,5e-4)
# QA-0535 emmeans: cell means and SE = sqrt(MSE/3)
mse=b.loc['Residual','sum_sq']/b.loc['Residual','df']
chk('QA-0535','placebo/no.therapy mean',ct.query("drug=='placebo' and therapy=='no.therapy'").mood_gain.mean(),0.30,5e-3)
chk('QA-0535','residual MS',mse,0.0544,5e-5); chk('QA-0535','SE',np.sqrt(mse/3),0.135,5e-4)
# QA-0532 contrast codings: matrices and invariance of the ANOVA table
treat=np.array([[0,0],[1,0],[0,1]]); summ=np.array([[1,0],[0,1],[-1,-1]]); helm=np.array([[-1,-1],[1,-1],[0,2]])
fits={}
for nm,C in [('treatment',treat),('sum',summ),('helmert',helm)]:
    X=np.column_stack([np.ones(len(ct)),C[ct.drug.cat.codes.values],(ct.therapy=='CBT').astype(float)])
    beta,res,*_=np.linalg.lstsq(X,ct.mood_gain.values,rcond=None); fits[nm]=(beta,((ct.mood_gain.values-X@beta)**2).sum())
chk('QA-0532','RSS identical across codings (max diff)',max(abs(f[1]-fits['treatment'][1]) for f in fits.values()),0,1e-12)
chk('QA-0532','coefficients differ (treatment vs sum, max |diff|)',float(abs(fits['treatment'][0][1:3]-fits['sum'][0][1:3]).max())>0.01,1,0)
chk('QA-0532','each matrix 3 x 2',all(m.shape==(3,2) for m in (treat,summ,helm)),1,0)
# QA-0545 model comparison F
r0=smf.ols('mood_gain ~ therapy',ct).fit(); r1=smf.ols('mood_gain ~ drug + therapy',ct).fit()
F=((r0.ssr-r1.ssr)/2)/(r1.ssr/14); chk('QA-0545','nested-model F(2,14)',F,26.149,5e-4)
# QA-0540 Kruskal-Wallis
kw=stats.kruskal(*[g.mood_gain for _,g in ct.groupby('drug',observed=True)])
chk('QA-0540','K-W chi-squared',kw.statistic,12.076,5e-4); chk('QA-0540','K-W p',kw.pvalue,0.002386,5e-7)
# QA-0538 Mann-Whitney (R: exact, W = U of group A)
A=[6.4,10.7,11.9,7.3,10]; B=[14.5,10.4,12.9,11.7,13]; mw=stats.mannwhitneyu(A,B,method='exact')
chk('QA-0538','W',mw.statistic,3,0); chk('QA-0538','p',mw.pvalue,0.05556,5e-6)
# QA-0539 signed rank (R: V = sum of positive ranks of after-before, exact)
bef=np.array([30,43,21,24,23,40,29,56,38,16]); aft=np.array([6,29,11,31,17,2,31,21,8,21]); dd=aft-bef
rk=stats.rankdata(abs(dd)); V=rk[dd>0].sum(); w=stats.wilcoxon(aft,bef,method='exact')
chk('QA-0539','V',V,7,0); chk('QA-0539','p',w.pvalue,0.03711,5e-6)
# QA-0541 Fisher exact
chk('QA-0541','Fisher p',stats.fisher_exact([[0,3],[10,3]]).pvalue,0.03571,5e-6)
# QA-0542 McNemar with continuity correction
x=(abs(25-5)-1)**2/(25+5); chk('QA-0542','McNemar chi2',x,12.033,5e-4); chk('QA-0542','McNemar p',stats.chi2.sf(x,1),0.0005226,5e-8)
df=pd.DataFrame(R); df.to_csv('stage1/qa/s12_rfirst_python.csv',index=False)
print(df.to_string(index=False)); print('\nALL OK' if df.ok.all() else '\nFAILURES: '+str((~df.ok).sum()))

# FlippedStat teaching extracts — Hong Kong official data

**Retrieval date.** 2026-11-18 (Asia/Hong_Kong)
**These files are official/public extracts, or a labelled join of such extracts.** They are not synthetic FlippedStat survey files, and they are not designated-textbook illustration files.

Source: Census and Statistics Department, Hong Kong SAR Government (C&SD website / data.gov.hk). Intellectual property in the official statistics belongs to the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. This is not a government publication and does not imply endorsement by the Government or C&SD.

## Licence, as stated by the sources (not legal advice)

**C&SD Intellectual Property Rights Notice** (https://www.censtatd.gov.hk/en/page_31.html), as read on 18 Nov 2026: unless otherwise specified, visitors may download, print, adapt, distribute, reproduce and hyperlink to specified statistical information (tables, datasets, reports and related statistical content, excluding maps, photographs, graphics, drawings, logos, audio and video) free of charge for commercial and non-commercial purposes, provided that (i) acknowledgement is given to the C&SD website as the source, (ii) the Government is acknowledged as the intellectual property rights owner, and (iii) any modifications are clearly indicated.

**DATA.GOV.HK Terms of Use** (https://data.gov.hk/en/terms-and-conditions), as read on 18 Nov 2026: data may be browsed, downloaded, distributed, reproduced, hyperlinked to, and printed for commercial and non-commercial purposes free of charge, provided the user complies with the Terms, clearly identifies the source, acknowledges the Government and relevant organisations’ ownership of intellectual property in the data, and gives proper attribution to the Government, the relevant organisations and DATA.GOV.HK. Individual dataset pages may carry additional terms. The data are provided “AS IS”. Use of the portal is not a statement of government approval or endorsement.

Department legal sign-off of this packaging has **not** been recorded. This note is a source register entry, not a legal opinion.

## Files in this folder

| File | Kind | Official table |
|---|---|---|
| hk_district_lookup.csv | teaching lookup from official names/codes | — |
| hk_district_population_110-02001.csv | official extract (subset) | C&SD 110-02001 |
| hk_district_household_130-06806.csv | official extract (subset) | C&SD 130-06806 |
| hk_district_profile_2016_2025.csv | teaching join; derived columns labelled | both tables above |
| hk_cpi_composite_monthly_510-60001.csv | official extract (subset) | C&SD 510-60001 |

Each CSV has a matching `*_codebook.md`.

## What this pass does not ship

- The R package **hkdatasets** (CRAN; https://github.com/Hong-Kong-Districts-Info/hkdatasets) was reviewed. Its DESCRIPTION states Licence **GPL-3** and that “All of the data in this package is available in the public domain.” The GitHub README carries an **MIT** badge, which does not match the DESCRIPTION. Underlying sources (districtcouncils.gov.hk, dce2019.hk01.com, Lands Department, Transport Department FOI microdata) may have their own terms. This pass therefore prefers C&SD / data.gov.hk tables whose reuse conditions were read from the source.
- `hkdc` (2019 District Councillors) is not shipped: it contains names, office addresses, phone numbers, emails and social-media URLs. Aggregate election teaching use is deferred pending a human licence review of the HK01 and district-council sources.
- `hk_accidents` / `hk_casualties` / `hk_vehicles` microdata are not shipped (size, ethical caution, FOI provenance). Official TD annual accident *publications* listed on data.gov.hk remain a possible later extract if a licence-clean aggregated table is confirmed.
- `hkstreetnames20` (source: landsd.gov.hk) is deferred until Lands Department reuse terms are verified from the source.
- `hkagepop19` is a 2019 age-by-district series in the package described as estimates based on calculated census percentages. Official C&SD tables were used instead.

## Optional desktop R (not the Moodle / WebR path)

WebR and some Moodle CSP setups may block `install.packages("hkdatasets")`. Students should use the CSV extracts mounted in this course. On a local desktop R, the package can be tried as an optional extra:

```r
# Optional, desktop R only — not required for FlippedStat exercises.
# Package licence: see the CRAN DESCRIPTION (GPL-3 as of the copy reviewed
# on 18 Nov 2026). Underlying data sources have their own terms.
install.packages("hkdatasets")
library(hkdatasets)
head(hkdistrict_summary)
```

## Reconstruction

Snapshots of the API records used here are stored under `sources/hk_extracts_raw/`. Regenerate the student files with:

```
python tools/hk_local_data.py --merge-rev90
```

No new official series was added in wave 2. ========== FILE: ws/stage1/rights/aipolicy.html ==========

<section class="wrap prose fsp"><h1>AI-use rules for FlippedStat</h1>
<p class="lead">Which rules apply when you use AI tools on this site, and where the official text is.</p>
<div class="statusnote" role="note"><b>Draft for approval (v9.9).</b> The controlling text is the University’s, not this page. This summary was checked against the public CUHK and ITSC pages on 17 November 2026 and must be confirmed by the project supervisors before student use.</div>
<h2>1. The University guidelines control</h2>
<p>CUHK’s <i>Guidelines on the Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools in Teaching, Learning and Assessments</i> set the rules. The student guide states that its second version (May 2025) supersedes the first version of March 2023. The guidelines describe four approaches a course can take to AI use, and say that improper or unauthorised use is academic dishonesty. <b>In any credit-bearing course, follow the approach stated in that course’s outline.</b> FlippedStat cannot give you permission to use AI in another course’s assessment.</p>
<ul><li><a href="https://www.res.cuhk.edu.hk/wp-content/uploads/undergraduate-students/A-guide-for-students_use-of-AI-tools.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Use of AI Tools in Teaching, Learning and Assessments — A Guide for Students (PDF)</a> ↗</li>
<li><a href="https://clear.cuhk.edu.hk/web/technology-empowered-teaching/generative-ai-in-education/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">CLEAR: Generative AI in Education</a> ↗ (links to the staff guidelines, CUHK login)</li>
<li>For research work (capstones, theses), the University’s guidelines on the responsible use of AI for research also apply.</li></ul>
<h2>2. Rules for FlippedStat activities (project rules — pending approval)</h2>
<table class="tbl"><tr><th scope="col">Activity</th><th scope="col">AI use</th></tr>
<tr><td>Placement test, pre- and post-assessments, Module 8 hallucination quiz</td><td><b>No AI.</b> These measure what you can do on your own.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Copilot labs, audit labs, AI moments</td><td><b>AI expected</b>, then every number is checked by you (C.R.O.S.S.) and recorded in your verification log.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Practice and checks in lessons</td><td>Try first without AI; use AI to explain, not to answer.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Anything you hand in for a course</td><td>Your course’s approach applies; add an AI-use statement (see the <a href="#m8kit">Module 8 kit</a>).</td></tr></table>
<h2>3. Which tool, and which data</h2>
<ul><li><b>Default tool: Microsoft Copilot Chat signed in with your CUHK account.</b> ITSC states that this service is free to students and staff, and that chat data are covered by enterprise data protection and are not used to train the model. ITSC still advises you not to enter personal or private information. <a href="https://www.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/all-it/email-messaging-and-collaboration/microsoft-copilot-for-the-web/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ITSC: Microsoft Copilot Chat</a> ↗</li>
<li><b>Qwen and Grok</b> (used in the three-tool comparison lab) are public services outside CUHK’s enterprise agreement. Use them <b>only with the synthetic datasets on this site</b> or other public, non-personal data.</li>
<li><b>Never</b> paste names, student or staff numbers, HKID numbers, contact details, health or financial information into any AI tool. De-identify first and keep any key separately. See ITSC’s <a href="https://www.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/all-it/information-security/data-privacy-and-protection/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Data Privacy and Protection</a> ↗ page and the University’s personal-data policy.</li></ul>
<h2>4. Telling others how you used AI</h2>
<p>Record the tool and date, what it did, and how you checked it. The AI-use statement template is in the <a href="#m8kit">Module 8 kit</a>.</p>
<p class="muted">Links are online-only. Policy wording changes: check the official pages before relying on this summary. Topics <a href="#t/1.4">1.4</a> and <a href="#t/8.9">8.9</a> link here.</p></section>

========== END FILE: ws/stage1/rights/aipolicy.html ==========


========== FILE: ws/stage1/rights/build_rights.py ==========

"""S1.7 rights register: every cited/embedded work (live FS.books + FS.rightsOf) and a component-level licence map."""
import json, collections
from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.styles import Font,PatternFill,Alignment,Border,Side
from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter
d=json.load(open('stage1/live_v99.json')); B=d['books']
A='Arial'; H=Font(name=A,bold=True,color='FFFFFF'); HF=PatternFill('solid',fgColor='1F4E79'); N=Font(name=A,size=10); Y=PatternFill('solid',fgColor='FFF2CC')
thin=Side(style='thin',color='BFBFBF'); BR=Border(top=thin,bottom=thin,left=thin,right=thin)
def fmt(ws,widths):
    for c in ws[1]: c.font=H; c.fill=HF; c.alignment=Alignment(wrap_text=True)
    for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2):
        for c in row: c.font=N; c.alignment=Alignment(wrap_text=True,vertical='top'); c.border=BR
    for i,w in enumerate(widths,1): ws.column_dimensions[get_column_letter(i)].width=w
    ws.freeze_panes='A2'
wb=Workbook(); ws=wb.active; ws.title='README'
for r in ['FlippedStat rights register (v9.9, Stage 1 S1.7)','Register = every work in the site’s reading register (FS.books) with the permitted-use decision the site applies (FS.rightsOf).',
 'Components = what licence applies to each part of the site; the proposal promises open access under Creative Commons, so each part must carry the correct licence.',
 'Open questions = decisions that need the project team or CUHK (yellow cells). This is not legal advice.']: ws.append([r])
ws['A1'].font=Font(name=A,bold=True,size=13); ws.column_dimensions['A'].width=120
rg=wb.create_sheet('Register'); rg.append(['Code','Work','Licence / access (as recorded)','Verification grade','Permitted use on the site','Use class','Cite-only','URL'])
for k,b in sorted(B.items()):
    r=b.get('rights') or {}; rg.append([k,b['title'],b['licence'],b['grade'],r.get('text',''),r.get('use',''),'Yes' if r.get('citeOnly') else 'No',b['url']])
last=rg.max_row; fmt(rg,[10,50,26,24,44,11,9,36])
sm=wb.create_sheet('Summary'); sm.append(['Use class','Works'])
for u in sorted({x[5].value for x in rg.iter_rows(min_row=2)}):
    r=sm.max_row+1; sm.append([u,f'=COUNTIF(Register!$F$2:$F${last},A{r})'])
r=sm.max_row+1; sm.append(['Cite-only works',f'=COUNTIF(Register!$G$2:$G${last},"Yes")']); sm.append(['Total works',f'=COUNTA(Register!$A$2:$A${last})'])
fmt(sm,[30,12])
cp=wb.create_sheet('Components'); cp.append(['Component','Contains','Licence that applies','Basis','Action'])
for r in [['Original FlippedStat lessons, widgets, datasets','Project-authored text, code and synthetic data','CC BY-SA 4.0 (site default)','Site licence page; combined with BY-SA textbooks','Confirm department is willing to release under CC (H7b)'],
 ['OpenIntro Statistics adaptation','Textbook-track passages and embedded edition','CC BY-SA 4.0 (adaptation of CC BY-SA 3.0)','Licence confirmed on openintro.org 15 Nov 2026 (site record)','Keep attribution and change notice'],
 ['Learning Statistics with jamovi adaptation','Passages and embedded edition','CC BY-SA 4.0','DOI 10.11647/OBP.0333 (site record)','Keep attribution'],
 ['Think Stats 3e adaptation (Elective E5, Python-route stages)','Adapted text; code excerpts','CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; code MIT','Site licence page','H7: confirm the use is non-commercial; NC parts must not be bundled into any fee-charging Phase 2 workshop'],
 ['Cite-only works','Section pointers only','All rights reserved / not cleared','Rights register','Never reproduce; link or cite only'],
 ['Images generated with Copilot','Illustrations','Site credit line “Visuals … generated with Microsoft Copilot”','Site footer','Keep the credit'],
 ['Moodle question banks and placement test','Items, keys, feedback','CC BY-SA 4.0 if released; keys should NOT be published openly while used for KPI evidence','S1.6 package','Decide release timing (after the evaluation period)']]: cp.append(r)
fmt(cp,[34,30,30,34,44])
oq=wb.create_sheet('Open questions'); oq.append(['ID','Question','Copilot recommendation','Decision','By','Date'])
for r in [['H7','Is FlippedStat’s use of Think Stats (CC BY-NC-SA) non-commercial, including any Phase 2 cost-recovery workshops?','Yes for the free platform; exclude NC material from fee-charging workshops'],
 ['H7b','Will the department release original FlippedStat content under CC BY-SA 4.0 as the proposal promises?','Yes, with assessment keys held back until the evaluation ends'],
 ['H7c','HELM (licence not checked) and AIP (notice forbids paraphrase): keep as cite-only?','Keep cite-only; do not paraphrase AIP']]: oq.append(r+['','',''])
fmt(oq,[7,60,50,18,14,12])
for row in oq.iter_rows(min_row=2,min_col=4,max_col=6):
    for c in row: c.fill=Y
out='stage1/rights/FlippedStat_Rights_Register_v1.0.xlsx'; wb.save(out); print(out, last-1, 'works')

========== END FILE: ws/stage1/rights/build_rights.py ==========

| Measure | v9.8 | v9.9 |
|---|---|---|
| Routes visited (all topics, units, modules, 18 assessment forms, kit and special pages) | 304 | 304 |
| JavaScript errors | 0 | 0 |
| Routes ok in v9.8 but failing in v9.9 | — | 0 |
| Short pages by design (10: post-forms and the after-survey show “take the pre-form first”) | 10 | 10 |

New in v9.9: `#placement` and `#aipolicy`. In v9.8 these routes did not exist and rendered an empty page (15 characters); in v9.9 they render 4,596 and 2,854 characters with no errors.
C4.11 showed 5,417 vs 4,714 characters in the timed pass; a direct re-render gives 4,711 in both versions, so the difference was lazy-loading timing, not lost content.
Placement/policy/item-bank functional suite: see placement_test_result.json.

========== FILE: ws/stage1/tests/regression99.py ==========

"""S1.8 full regression pass. Usage: python stage1/tests/regression99.py build/X.html label
Visits every topic, unit, module, assessment form, kit page and special page; records JS errors and empty pages."""
import sys,asyncio,pathlib,json
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
async def main(src,label):
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        b=await p.chromium.launch(executable_path='/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1228/chrome-linux64/chrome')
        pg=await b.new_page(viewport={'width':1280,'height':900}); errs=[]; pg.set_default_timeout(20000)
        pg.on('pageerror',lambda e: errs.append(str(e))); pg.on('console',lambda m: errs.append(m.text) if m.type=='error' else None)
        await pg.goto(pathlib.Path(src).resolve().as_uri(),timeout=180000); await pg.wait_for_timeout(3500)
        tops=await pg.evaluate("FS.units.flatMap(u=>u.topics.map(t=>'t/'+t.no))"); units=await pg.evaluate("FS.units.map(u=>'u/'+u.id)")
        special=['home','map','modules','pathways','tiers','assess','m8kit','m8kit/quiz','m8kit/survey/pre','m8kit/survey/post','m8kit/lab','m8kit/disclose','status','licence','release','a11y','ledger','books','about','lib','placement','aipolicy']
        routes=special+[f'm/{i}' for i in range(1,10)]+[f'assess/{i}/{f}' for i in range(1,10) for f in ('pre','post')]+units+tops
        out=[];bad=0
        for r in routes:
            n0=len(errs)
            async def visit():
                await pg.evaluate(f"location.hash='#{r}'"); await pg.wait_for_timeout(450 if r.startswith('t/') else 700)
                return await pg.evaluate("document.querySelector('#main').innerText.length")
            try: c=await asyncio.wait_for(visit(),20)
            except Exception as ex: c=-1; errs.append('TIMEOUT/'+type(ex).__name__)
            e=errs[n0:]; print(r,c,'ERR' if e else '',flush=True)
            ok=not e and c>=200; bad+=not ok; out.append(dict(route=r,ok=ok,chars=c,errors='; '.join(e)[:200]))
        await b.close()
    json.dump(out,open(f'stage1/tests/regression_{label}.json','w'),indent=0)
    fails=[o for o in out if not o['ok']]; print(label,len(routes),'routes,',len(fails),'failing'); [print('  ',f) for f in fails[:15]]
asyncio.run(main(sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2]))

========== END FILE: ws/stage1/tests/regression99.py ==========

========== FILE: ws/stage1/tests/test_placement.py ==========

"""Headless test of the v9.9 placement test. Usage: python stage1/tests/test_placement.py build/FlippedStat_v9.9_standalone.html"""
import sys,os,asyncio,json
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
CH='/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1228/chrome-linux64/chrome'
async def main(src):
    res=[]; errs=[]
    def ok(name,cond,info=''): res.append((name,bool(cond),info))
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        b=await p.chromium.launch(executable_path=CH); pg=await b.new_page(viewport={'width':1280,'height':900})
        pg.set_default_navigation_timeout(180000); pg.set_default_timeout(60000); pg.on('pageerror',lambda e: errs.append(str(e)))
        await pg.goto('file://'+os.path.abspath(src)+'#placement'); await pg.wait_for_timeout(3500)
        n=await pg.locator('fieldset.fsp-q').count(); ok('20 questions rendered',n==20,n)
        ok('each question has 5 radios',await pg.locator('fieldset.fsp-q input[type=radio]').count()==100)
        ok('legend used for each question',await pg.locator('fieldset.fsp-q > legend').count()==20)
        await pg.click('#fsp-form button[type=submit]'); await pg.wait_for_timeout(200)
        msg=await pg.inner_text('#fsp-msg'); ok('incomplete submit blocked with message',"answer every question" in msg,msg)
        # answer: all correct in domains D,P,Q; wrong in I and R
        data=await pg.evaluate('window.FSP_DATA.items')
        for it in data:
            k=it['key'] if it['domain'] in 'QDP' else (it['key']+1)%4
            await pg.check(f'input[name="{it["id"]}"][value="{k}"]')
        await pg.click('#fsp-form button[type=submit]'); await pg.wait_for_timeout(500)
        ok('hash moves to result',(await pg.evaluate('location.hash'))=='#placement/result')
        txt=await pg.inner_text('#main')
        ok('total score 12/20',"Score 12 / 20" in txt)
        ok('pathway = Foundation',"Foundation Certificate route" in txt)
        ok('Inference = Start here',"Start here" in txt)
        ok('revision links for missed topics',await pg.locator('a[href="#t/8.2"]').count()>=1)
        ok('module links present',await pg.locator('#main a[href="#m/3"]').count()>=1)
        # persistence after reload
        await pg.reload(); await pg.wait_for_timeout(3000); ok('result persists after reload',"Your starting route" in await pg.inner_text('#main'))
        # retake
        await pg.click('#fsp-retake'); await pg.wait_for_timeout(500); ok('retake shows fresh form',await pg.locator('fieldset.fsp-q').count()==20)
        # topic 1.1 banner + nav link
        await pg.goto('file://'+os.path.abspath(src)+'#t/1.1'); await pg.wait_for_timeout(2500)
        ok('topic 1.1 banner',await pg.locator('.fsp-banner a[href="#placement"]').count()==1)
        ok('nav link',await pg.locator('a[href="#placement"]').count()>=2)
        await pg.goto('file://'+os.path.abspath(src)+'#status'); await pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        ok('status open item updated','Implemented in v9.9' in await pg.inner_text('#main'))
        await pg.goto('file://'+os.path.abspath(src)+'#aipolicy'); await pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        t=await pg.inner_text('#main'); ok('AI-use rules page renders','AI-use rules for FlippedStat' in t and 'May 2025' in t)
        for tp in ('1.4','8.9'):
            await pg.goto('file://'+os.path.abspath(src)+'#t/'+tp); await pg.wait_for_timeout(2500)
            ok(f'policy banner on topic {tp}',await pg.locator('.fsp-pol a[href="#aipolicy"]').count()==1)
        await pg.goto('file://'+os.path.abspath(src)+'#m8kit'); await pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        t=await pg.inner_text('#main'); ok('Module 8 kit uses KPI 5.x numbering','KPI 3.1' not in t)
        # S1.4: Module 3 pre-form shows revised items; completing it unlocks a 10-item post-form
        await pg.goto('file://'+os.path.abspath(src)+'#assess/3/pre'); await pg.wait_for_timeout(2500)
        t=await pg.inner_text('#main'); ok('M3 pre-form shows revised AI-claim item','sensitivity is 0.9' in t)
        for fs in await pg.locator('#main fieldset').all():
            r=fs.locator('input[type=radio]'); 
            if await r.count(): await r.first.check()
        btn=pg.locator('#main button[type=submit], #main button:has-text("Submit")').first
        if await btn.count(): await btn.click(); await pg.wait_for_timeout(800)
        await pg.goto('file://'+os.path.abspath(src)+'#assess/3/post'); await pg.wait_for_timeout(2500)
        n=await pg.locator('#main fieldset').count(); ok('M3 post-form unlocked with 10 questions',n==10,n)
        ok('M3 post-form shows revised AI-claim item','science major' in await pg.inner_text('#main'))
        # mobile reflow 320px
        m=await b.new_page(viewport={'width':320,'height':700}); m.set_default_navigation_timeout(180000); await m.goto('file://'+os.path.abspath(src)+'#placement'); await m.wait_for_timeout(3000)
        sw=await m.evaluate('document.documentElement.scrollWidth'); ok('no horizontal scroll at 320px',sw<=322,sw)
        await b.close()
    ok('no JavaScript errors',not errs,errs[:3])
    for r in res: print(('PASS ' if r[1] else 'FAIL ')+r[0],'' if r[1] else r[2])
    json.dump([dict(test=r[0],passed=r[1],info=str(r[2])) for r in res],open('stage1/tests/placement_test_result.json','w'),indent=1)
    print(f"{sum(r[1] for r in res)}/{len(res)} passed")
asyncio.run(main(sys.argv[1]))

# FlippedStat 43-step walkthrough instrument

**Draft instrument for human review — 18 November 2026 (Asia/Hong_Kong)**

This is a **draft test instrument**. It is **not** a completed audit, **not** a record that the walkthrough has been run, and **not** a WCAG 2.2 AA certification or accessibility sign-off. Result columns are blank on purpose. Leave them blank until a human tester actually performs the step.

Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Chinese University of Hong Kong. No CUHK crest is used, and nothing in this file implies institutional approval.

Human decisions **H1–H11** remain open. This instrument does not invent policy, approvals, pilot results, accessibility scores, or attendance figures.

---

## 1. What this is for

A human tester (a staff member first, and later a student or staff volunteer if the course team so decides) can follow these 43 numbered steps on the **current development tip**, record what they observe, and mark each step **pass**, **fail**, or **not testable**.

The proposal and stage plan call this the **43-step human walkthrough**. Automated WCAG 2.2 AA work (axe, contrast, keyboard-outline sampling, and 320 CSS-pixel reflow checks) was done in **v9.8**. Manual screen-reader testing is still open. This draft is the instrument for that human work; filling it in is a later human task.

### 1.1 File to test

| Build | Path | Role | SHA-256 | Size (bytes) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **v10.7-dev** | `build/FlippedStat_v10.7-dev_standalone.html` | Current **development tip** — use this unless the course team names another file | `eee89a12f31e167a95e9bb5521627ab14ad649131ad930b5544434b9e4b06632` | 20,422,264 |
| **v9.9** | `build/FlippedStat_v9.9_standalone.html` | Last **closed public** release (Stage 1 closed 17 November 2026). Do not treat it as the tip. Some v10 features below (WebR, `#assess` hub, official-extract download buttons, `#interactives`) are not on v9.9 | `ca3054be56c17c7a0f996c49a0eb3ddec86c8eaba869cf46e5f8a8ae0b542651` | 19,287,711 |

Open the HTML in a browser from a hosted URL or as a local file. Hash routes work once the file is open (for example `…/FlippedStat_v10.7-dev_standalone.html#m/2`).

**Moodle is not live.** There is no course shell, SSO, or hosted eLearn copy to test from this workspace. If a step would only apply on Moodle (for example a content-security policy blocking WebR), mark it **not testable** unless the course team has since provided a live host.

### 1.2 Protocol this instrument extends

Do not invent a conflicting protocol. Steps **1–25** are the v9.8 manual-test script, copied with the same step IDs, WCAG success criteria, areas, routes, actions, and pass criteria.

**Source file:** `content/a11y_manual.py` (module docstring: “Stage 7: manual accessibility test script (WCAG 2.2 AA) for human reviewers”). That list has **25** steps (`K1`–`K7`, `S1`–`S7`, `V1`–`V6`, `M1`–`M2`, `C1`–`C3`). The same rows were written into a “Manual test script” sheet by `tools/build_a11y98.py` when the v9.8 workbook was generated; this instrument cites the Python source, which is what remains in the tree.

Steps **26–43** are extensions so that the whole instrument has **43** numbered steps, matching the proposal/plan name. They cover items the original script did not name explicitly, or that were added after v9.8: 320 CSS-pixel reflow (already in the v9.8 *automated* checks and later `check107dev.py`, but not a manual step), a module-overview plus short-topic path, official Hong Kong data download buttons, WebR on- and off-network, placement and the `#assess` hub, interactives, captions/transcripts for scripted videos (test what actually exists), alt text on an official-data figure, the site “Larger text” control, and a closing keyboard path.

Pass criteria for steps 1–25 are not rewritten. Where a v9.8 route now sits on optional Module 9, or a later feature should be checked as well, a *tester note* is added under that step. The note does not change the original criterion.

### 1.3 How to record results

For each step use exactly one of:

- **Pass** — the expected observation held on the file you tested.
- **Fail** — it did not hold. Write what you saw in Notes.
- **Not testable** — you could not run the step honestly (no screen reader, no network for a network-only check, no film when the step is about captions on a film, Moodle not hosted, and so on). Say why.

Do not invent a score, a percentage, or a WCAG conformance claim from a partial run. A mix of pass, fail, and not-testable is a valid record.

Recommended kit (same tools as the v9.8 script, plus DevTools for the 320 px step):

- Browser: Edge or Chrome for most steps; Safari for the VoiceOver step.
- Assistive technology: NVDA (Windows) for `S1`–`S6`; VoiceOver (macOS and, if available, iPhone) for `S7`.
- A colour picker / DevTools, a text-spacing bookmarklet for `V3`, and a way to turn on the operating-system reduce-motion setting for `M1`.
- For steps 31–32: a network you can turn off, or a way to block `webr.r-wasm.org`.
- For step 38: access to the workspace folder `stage8/scripts/` (draft VTT files live there, not in the standalone HTML).

# FlippedStat CLEAR session outline

**Draft for human review — 18 November 2026 (Asia/Hong_Kong)**

This is a **session outline** a course team could take to the Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research (CLEAR) at CUHK. It is **not** a booking, **not** a scheduled session, and **not** a record that CLEAR has reviewed any material. No date is proposed as a confirmed booking, and no attendance figure is claimed.

Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Chinese University of Hong Kong. No CUHK crest is used. Nothing in this file implies institutional approval of FlippedStat, of this outline, or of any human decision **H1–H11**.

Do not invent CUHK policy text (**H8** remains open). Do not invent pilot results, accessibility scores, or voucher numbers.

---

## 1. Purpose and limits

The proposal tracks two related but different pieces of work:

| Item | What the proposal/crosswalk asks for | Status in this workspace (18 November 2026) |
|---|---|---|
| **Outcome 2** | CLEAR review of materials, with a submission and review record; a CLEAR deck is listed under Stage 10 | **Not started.** This outline is a draft agenda and materials list for the course team to edit. It is not a submission and not a review record. A finished briefing deck is still outstanding. |
| **Proposed KPI 4.1** | One CLEAR session with **20+** distinct staff on the attendance record (in person + online; organisers excluded), as specified in `stage1/crosswalk/build_crosswalk.py` and `stage1/kpi/build_protocol.js` | **A future evidence target, not a result.** No session has been booked or delivered from this work, and no attendance has been recorded. |

The project names **Dr WONG Kin Chi** as Co-Supervisor (Co-S). Involving the Co-S in any approach to CLEAR is a course-team step. This draft does not itself contact CLEAR, invite attendees, or send email.

Two different meetings may later be useful. Neither is scheduled by this file:

1. A **review conversation** with CLEAR (supports Outcome 2): a small meeting to show the materials and ask what a formal review would need.
2. A later **staff briefing or sharing session** (the event that could, if delivered and recorded, contribute evidence toward KPI 4.1). Attendance would be taken on the blank template in `stage1/kpi/templates/clear_attendance_TEMPLATE.csv`. That template includes an **example row** with a placeholder date; the example is not a booking.

The course team decides whether to hold one meeting or two, in what format, and when.

---

## 2. Suggested duration

These timings are suggestions for planning, not a confirmed programme.

| Format | Suggested duration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Review conversation with CLEAR (Outcome 2) | **60–75 minutes** | Agenda in Section 3. Shorten by dropping the live WebR attempt if the room has no reliable network. |
| Later staff briefing (possible KPI 4.1 event) | To be agreed with CLEAR and the department (a common working range is 45–90 minutes) | Do not treat this line as a booked length. If held, use the attendance template and exclude organisers from the KPI 4.1 count, as the protocol already states. |

A room, a hybrid link, and a booking route are human arrangements. They are not made here.

## 3. Suggested agenda (review conversation)

Adjust names, order, and timing when a real meeting is arranged.

| Minutes (indicative) | Item | What to show or say |
|---|---|---|

Completing a module, or seeing a certificate-style label on the site, does not confer academic credit. Human decisions H1–H11 are still open. This meeting, if it occurs, is a review discussion, not an approval ceremony. |
| 12–15 | The student site | Open the current **development tip**, `build/FlippedStat_v10.7-dev_standalone.html` (20,422,264 bytes, SHA-256 `eee89a12f31e167a95e9bb5521627ab14ad649131ad930b5544434b9e4b06632`, 18 November 2026). Say clearly that the last **closed public** release is **v9.9** (`build/FlippedStat_v9.9_standalone.html`, SHA-256 `ca3054be56c17c7a0f996c49a0eb3ddec86c8eaba869cf46e5f8a8ae0b542651`). **Moodle is not live** (no course shell, SSO, or official evaluation data). Which file is later hosted for students is a course-team / IT choice. Walk `#modules` → `#m/2` → `#t/2.1` (or another short official path). Point to `#pathways` and `#placement` only as implemented tools, with cut scores still awaiting **H3**. |
| 8 | One official-data example | Stay on Topic 2.1 or open Topic 4.1 / 4.4 / E5.2. Show a labelled official extract (for example C&SD Table 110-02001 or 130-06806; other extracts in `content/data/hk_extracts/` include CPI, live births, and Hong Kong Observatory series). Download the CSV from the page button. Stress the teaching rule: FlippedStat arithmetic on an official table is **not** an official C&SD or HKO statistic and does **not** imply government endorsement. Terms recorded in `stage1/rights/HK_DATA_SOURCES_2026-11-18.md` still require source acknowledgement, acknowledgement of Government intellectual property, and a clear indication of modifications. Department sign-off of the packaging has not been recorded. The R package `hkdatasets` is **not** shipped. |
| 10 | Module 8 lab | Open `#m8kit` and `#m8kit/lab`. The kit has a ten-question hallucination quiz, a confidence survey, a three-tool comparison lab on the **synthetic** file `tutorial_scores.csv`, and an AI-use statement template (`#m8kit/disclose`). Teach the site rule: **agreement is not proof**. Welch’s *t* is the course default two-sample *t* when that test is appropriate. Live Copilot / Qwen / Grok testing of the lab is still a human task (“Last checked by the project team: not yet” is the kit’s own wording). Do not paste personal data into a public tool. |

On the site, `#assess` and `#placement` are **formative practice** — answers stay in the browser or in the page, and are not official evaluation evidence. OpenShot projects in `stage8/openshot/` are **editable scaffolds, not finished films** (no rendered MP4 required to make this point). A short Beamer deck or a still sequence is not a finished video. |
| 5 | Accessibility status | Automated WCAG 2.2 AA checks (axe, contrast, keyboard-outline sampling, 320 px reflow) were run on **v9.8**. The **43-step human walkthrough** and manual screen-reader testing are **not done**. A draft instrument now sits at `stage10/FlippedStat_43_step_walkthrough_instrument_DRAFT.md`. That file is an instrument, not a completed audit, and not a certification. If a student hits an access barrier, treat it as an open issue. |
| 10 | Questions for CLEAR | See Section 4. Leave time for CLEAR colleagues to ask about students, adopting lecturers, and what a formal review would need. |
| 5 | Next steps (human decisions only) | Record actions the **course team** will take: whether to request a formal CLEAR review (Outcome 2), whether to plan a later staff session (KPI 4.1 target), who holds the attendance template, and which open H1–H11 items need to be decided before any public claim. Do not invent a date. |

If time is short, keep the site path, the official-data example, the Module 8 lab, and the questions, and point to the instructor guide draft for assessments and media status.

## 4. Questions for review

These are questions the course team may put to CLEAR. They are not questions that have already been asked, and they do not imply advice already received.

1. Is the “optional self-study, not a credit-bearing course” framing clear enough on the site and in the draft instructor guide for students and for lecturers who might later assign a module as pre-class work?
2. What would CLEAR need in order to **review the materials** formally (Outcome 2): a written submission, a recorded walkthrough, a student-facing checklist, or something else?
3. Given that automated accessibility checks exist from v9.8 but the 43-step walkthrough and screen-reader testing have **not** been run, what would CLEAR advise as the next human accessibility step? In particular, how should draft captions (`captions.vtt` for 32 unfilmed programme-map videos) be treated until films exist?
4. Is the labelling of official C&SD / DATA.GOV.HK / HKO extracts — teaching calculations, not official statistics, no government endorsement — adequate for a student audience?
5. In-browser `#placement` and `#assess` scores are formative only; official evaluation is planned on a Moodle course that is not yet live. Does that split need clearer student wording?
6. Module 8 asks students to compare tools, including public services, on **synthetic** data, and human decision **H8** (controlling AI-use policy text) is still open. The site page `#aipolicy` is a draft insertion point only. Without inventing policy, what should the team point students to in the meantime (the team should themselves check the current CUHK student guide on AI tools, CLEAR’s own generative-AI pages, and ITSC pages, rather than relying on a paraphrase in this outline)?
7. If the department later holds a staff briefing aimed at proposed KPI 4.1 (20+ distinct staff, organisers excluded), what format and evidence would CLEAR consider appropriate? This is a planning question, not a claim that such a briefing is scheduled.
8. Adoption in a named non-Statistics course is a later human step (proposed KPI 4.2). Is there advice on what “ready to show a colleague” should mean while H1–H11 remain open?

### 5.3 What not to bring as if it were finished or approved

- Finished films, or Beamer PDFs that have not actually been compiled in the copy you are showing.

## 2. What FlippedStat is

FlippedStat is an **optional self-study campaign** and a self-paced learning resource. It is **not a credit-bearing course**. Completing a module, or seeing a “certificate / endorsement / distinction” label on the student site, does not confer academic credit and does not exempt a student from any other CUHK course.

The materials are prepared for instructors in the Department of Statistics and Data Science, and for later adopters in other departments. Adoption or formal recommendation in a named non-Statistics course is a later human step (proposal KPI 4.2). No such confirmations are documented in this repository.

### 2.1 Official reportable units

The working map in `content/modules93.py`, the proposal crosswalk, and later Stage 8 artefacts treat **Modules 1–8** as the official reportable units: **153 official topics** (17 + 17 + 18 + 22 + 23 + 25 + 13 + 18) plus eight module overviews. That freeze is the Copilot recommendation for human decision **H1**. The decision cells for H1 are still blank. Until the course team records H1, do not treat the eight-module list as a signed academic approval, and do not report Module 9 as an official KPI 1.1 unit.

**Module 9** (*Advanced Modelling: Categorical, Predictive and Multivariate*, 56 topics) is an optional extension allowed by the proposal’s 6–9 module range. It is **not** in Appendix III, is **not** an official reportable unit, and is **not** approved. Pre/post items, an optional OpenShot folder, and a Moodle XML file exist for it. Do not treat a Module 9 quiz as part of the official pilot unless H1 is decided that way.

The student site also contains supporting material outside Modules 1–9 (companion clinics and a depth shelf). The crosswalk describes the whole site as 24 units / 231 topics, including those companions. Supporting pages are not counted as official reportable units.

English is the platform language of the current materials. Native-speaker review of existing Chinese Modules 1–6, and Chinese Modules 7–8, are listed as later work in the gap check; they are not delivered in this draft.

### 2.2 Official module map

Titles below are the FlippedStat v9.9 / current-map titles from `content/modules93.py`. The proposal Appendix III title, where it differs, is noted in parentheses. Essential topic IDs are those listed on the official map. Learning-outcome wording is abbreviated from the same file; this table is not a new set of outcomes.

Module 8 is required for every learner on the placement design: it is not “placed out.” Full outcome lists, checks, and topic inventories are on the module pages (`#m/1` … `#m/8`) and in `content/modules93.py`.

Design-hour estimates for modules are recorded in the proposal crosswalk. The crosswalk README states that those figures are **design estimates, not measured study time**. This guide does not redefine hours and does not reprint them as an official workload.

### 2.3 Pathways

Three named pathways are defined in `content/modules93.py` and shown on `#pathways`:

| Pathway | Who it is for (wording on the map) | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Essential Statistical Literacy | Any CUHK student who needs the core ideas and safe AI habits, e.g. as pre-class work | The Fundamental-tier subtopics of Modules 1–5 and 8 (other subtopics stay available) |
| Foundation Certificate route | Students who want a complete grounding for coursework or a research project | All topics of Modules 1–5 and 8 (Modules 6–7 optional) |
| Intermediate extensions | Students in courses that use experiments, surveys, classification or multivariate data | Modules 6, 7 and 9: Module 6 after Module 4; Modules 7 and 9 after Module 5 |

The extension pathway includes Module 9. That does not make Module 9 an official reportable unit while H1 is open. If you point students at Module 9, say clearly that it is optional and unapproved.

Subtopic tiers (Fundamental / Intermediate / eXtended) are implemented on topic pages. The Essential pathway uses the Fundamental-tier subtopics of the modules listed above, not a different set of module numbers.

### 2.4 Completion on the site versus official completion

The site completion rule, matching the proposal’s KPI 2.2 threshold, is: a module is complete when at least **80%** of its topics are marked done. On the standalone HTML file, progress is saved **in that browser only**.

The official record for TDLEG reporting is intended to come from the CUHK Moodle deployment (Work Package 7 / Stage 9). That deployment still needs a course shell, SSO, hosting, and live analytics. It has not been carried out from this workspace.

In Moodle, the drafted rule (see `completion_certificate_rules.md`) is that a module is complete when at least 80% of activities marked `required_for_completion = Y` in `course_structure.csv` are complete, and that pre- and post-assessments count when **submitted** (any score). Those rules, and the certificate condition, await human confirmation (including **H6** for certificate wording and signatory).

### 3.3 Practice scores are formative; official evaluation is Moodle

Answers for the in-browser placement test, `#assess` practice forms, and site quizzes are in the page or stay in the browser. Treat every in-browser score as **formative practice**. Do **not** use site scores as official assessment evidence, as psychometric evidence, or as TDLEG evaluation data.

The official evaluation record is the Moodle course (when it exists): imported question banks, completion tracking, the Module 8 instruments, and any certificate log. That course shell, SSO, and live analytics are not in place in this workspace.

### 3.4 Interactives (v10.2-dev layer, still on the tip)

Six widgets live on `#interactives`:

1. Missing codes moving a mean (`sleep_column.csv`; keyed 2.53 h on *n* = 105 versus 7.61 h on *n* = 100) — Topic 2.2
2. Sampling distribution / central-limit-theorem builder — Topics 7.2–7.3
3. Confidence-interval coverage — Topic 7.6
4. Correlation versus a lurking third variable (`satisfaction300.csv`) — Topic 9.7
5. p-value “what it is not” simulation — Topics 8.1–8.2
6. Optional bootstrap of a mean, tiny *n* versus *n* = 100 — Topics 7.5–7.6

Interaction *patterns* were adapted from *ModernDive* 2e; the widgets were reimplemented in the FlippedStat style with course synthetic data. Book prose, exercises, and ModernDive datasets were not copied. This layer is a labelled **CC BY-NC-SA 4.0** supplement (see Section 4.4).

### 3.5 WebR and coding

R and Python are the mainstream statistical coding tools in the materials. Students are not expected to memorise syntax. The taught skill is to write a prompt that names the data, the method, and the required output; run the code an AI tool returns; and verify the result.

WebR runs selected R cells in the browser. Known limit, documented since v10.1-dev: a Moodle / eLearn content-security policy **may block** `webr.r-wasm.org`. If that happens, students can still use desktop R, or Excel / hand recomputation, as the verification step. A local `md_r_server.py` bridge was deliberately not ported.

`#codeprompt` is an extension. It does not add a module, change hours, or change completion rules.

## 4. Teaching approach

### 4.1 AI writes, the student verifies (C.R.O.S.S.)

The core habit is taught on Topic 1.9 (*Prompt contract, C.R.O.S.S. and the log*) and reused in later labs and in Module 8.

The **prompt contract** (Topic 1.9) has five clauses, condensed from the topic page: (1) data check; (2) show code; (3) separate results, interpretation and assumptions; (4) limits; (5) handover checks. The contract does not make the AI correct; it makes errors easier to see.

**C.R.O.S.S.** is the verification checklist the student applies to a number or claim:

1. **C**ount
2. **R**ecompute
3. **O**ther tool
4. **S**tatistical principles
5. **S**ources and scope

Students keep a verification log (template on Topic 1.9; disclosure template in the Module 8 kit). Agreement among Copilot, Qwen and Grok is **not** proof — including when they return the same code (Topic 13.2 and the Module 8 comparison lab).

Failure modes used in Module 8 teaching (H-codes in the kit, not the same IDs as human decisions H1–H11) include: misreads or invents data; wrong method or violated assumption; calculation slip; over-reach in interpretation; fabricated or unsupported source; unsafe or unverified practice.

### 4.2 Default two-sample *t*: Welch’s *t*

Welch’s *t*-test is the default two-sample *t* in this course (and in R). Students should prompt for it by name, then verify. A worked pattern is on `#codeprompt` and is flagged from Topic 8.4. A paired design still needs a paired test; the Module 8 quiz includes that distinction. Do not treat a pooled two-sample *t* as the course default.

### 4.3 Three layers of teaching data — keep them labelled and separate

Teaching examples on the current tip fall into three labelled layers. Do not mix official figures with synthetic answer keys, or treat a FlippedStat calculation on an official table as a Census and Statistics Department publication.

**1. Official / public extracts** (C&SD, DATA.GOV.HK, Hong Kong Observatory), stored under `content/data/hk_extracts/` with codebooks, and mounted for download and WebR on the site from v10.4-dev onwards. Source register: `stage1/rights/HK_DATA_SOURCES_2026-11-18.md`. Series in the tree include:

- C&SD Table 110-02001 — land area, land population and density by District Council district (2016 and 2025 extract)
- C&SD Table 130-06806 — average household size and median monthly household income by district (2016 and 2025 extract)
- a labelled teaching join of those two tables
- C&SD Table 510-60001 — Composite CPI monthly extract, January 2015–September 2026
- C&SD Table 115-01012A — monthly live births, totals only (wave 3)
- HKO daily rainfall, daily mean temperature, and daily cloud-to-ground lightning counts at / over Hong Kong (2016–2025 teaching extracts), plus a derived June–August lightning-days table

On v10.7-dev, labelled official-data teaching text appears on Topics 1.3, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 6.3, 6.5, 9.7, 10.3, 10.6, 11.4 and E5.2. Calculations on official figures are FlippedStat teaching calculations, not official C&SD or HKO statistics. The materials state that this is not a government publication and does not imply government endorsement.

Some official Modules 1–8 topics and named case studies (including C4.1, C4.2, C4.7–C4.9) remain on textbook or other examples for documented reasons (keyed source files, no clean official two-way table, or official weather / births / 18 districts being a poor iid sample for CLT, confidence intervals, or tests). That pause is recorded in the localisation inventories under `logs/`. This guide does not start another localisation wave.

**2. Synthetic Hong Kong examples** already written for the course (for example Harbourside time-series files, `survey300.csv`, `satisfaction300.csv`, and other FlippedStat synthetic files). These stay labelled synthetic. They do not describe real students, stations, or services. Where they already serve the teaching point, they were kept.

**3. Labelled textbook illustrations** (for example OpenIntro figures, or keyed checks retained beside a new official-data illustration). Textbook material is paraphrased in slides and scripts, not copied. Some named files and case studies are still in use because their keys are locked or no clean official substitute was accepted.

The R package **hkdatasets** was reviewed and is **not shipped**. Its DESCRIPTION and GitHub licence badges disagree, and several tables raise personal-data or underlying-licence questions. An optional desktop-R pointer appears in the sources note; it is not required for exercises. Students should use the CSV extracts mounted in the course.

### 4.4 Rights — point to the register; several decisions are still human

Point instructors and later adopters to:

- `stage1/rights/FlippedStat_Rights_Register_v1.0.xlsx` (93 works registered at Stage 1 close)
- `stage1/rights/HK_DATA_SOURCES_2026-11-18.md`
- the site page `#licence`

This guide is not legal advice and does not record department legal sign-off.

Human rights decisions that remain open (do not treat the following as cleared):

- **H7** — Think Stats 3e (CC BY-NC-SA) use in a university resource; confirm non-commercial status with the department. Module 7 is built on Chapter 12 of Think Stats 3e, adapted in that module, with synthetic Harbourside data. Optional Think Stats Python-route stages remain where they already sit in v9.9; that licence question is not extended by `#codeprompt`.
- **H7b** — whether the department will release original FlippedStat content under CC BY-SA 4.0 as the proposal promises (assessment keys held back until the evaluation ends is the documented recommendation, not a recorded decision).
- **H7c** — HELM (licence not checked in the register workflow) and AIP (notice forbids paraphrase): keep as cite-only? The documented recommendation is to keep them cite-only and not paraphrase AIP.
- *ModernDive* 2e (Chester Ismay, Albert Y. Kim and Arturo Valdivia, <https://moderndive.com>), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: the `#interactives` widget layer is itself offered under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and must stay labelled as a supplement. NonCommercial and ShareAlike are stricter than some other FlippedStat materials. Do not silently merge that layer into materials intended for a more permissive licence without a separate rights decision.
- Barocas / fairmlbook and legal textbook copies are listed in the 18 November 2026 gap check as still needing human approval.

C&SD and DATA.GOV.HK terms, as read on 18 November 2026 and quoted in the sources note, require source acknowledgement, acknowledgement of Government intellectual property, and a clear indication of modifications. Individual dataset pages may carry additional terms. Department sign-off of the packaging has not been recorded.

### 4.5 AI-use wording in class

Do **not** invent or “tidy up” CUHK AI-policy text.

The site page `#aipolicy` is a **draft for approval (v9.9)**. It states that the controlling text is the University’s, not that page; that the summary was checked against public CUHK and ITSC pages on 17 November 2026; and that project supervisors must confirm it before student use. Topics 1.4 and 8.9 point here. Human decision **H8** (controlling AI-use policy text) is still open.

Public links already cited on that draft page, for instructors to open and check themselves, include the CUHK student guide on the use of AI tools, the CLEAR generative-AI pages, and the ITSC pages on Microsoft Copilot Chat and data privacy. Policy wording changes: check the official pages before relying on the site summary.

For any **credit-bearing** host course, the approach stated in *that* course’s outline applies. FlippedStat cannot give permission to use AI in another course’s assessment. When you assign FlippedStat activities inside your own course, say so in your outline; do not copy this draft as if it were confirmed departmental policy.

Draft project rules on `#aipolicy` (pending H8) distinguish: no AI on placement, pre/post assessments, and the Module 8 hallucination quiz; AI expected, then checked with C.R.O.S.S., on Copilot labs, audit labs and AI moments; practice items — try first without AI, then use AI to explain, not to answer. The default tool named on the draft page is Microsoft Copilot Chat signed in with a CUHK account. Qwen and Grok, used in the three-tool lab, are public services outside CUHK’s enterprise agreement; the draft page says to use them only with the synthetic datasets on the site or other public, non-personal data. Live Copilot / Qwen / Grok testing of the Module 8 lab is still a human task.

### 5.2 How to import (Moodle XML)

Follow `DEPLOYMENT_README.md`. In brief:

1. Request a CUHK Moodle course shell with SSO, self-enrolment and completion tracking enabled. This is an IT / Stage 9 step, not something this draft can do.
2. Host the agreed standalone HTML on departmental web space and test that `#m/1` and `#t/1.1` open. The deployment note names v9.9; if the course team instead hosts v10.7-dev, record that choice.
3. In the course: **Question bank → Import → Moodle XML**.
4. Import `FlippedStat_placement_test.xml` first, then `FlippedStat_module1_prepost.xml` through `FlippedStat_module8_prepost.xml`.
5. `FlippedStat_module9_prepost.xml` is in the zip because the bank was built for nine modules. Do not treat a Module 9 quiz as part of the official pilot unless H1 is decided that way.
6. Build quizzes as in the deployment note: pre-form = Anchors + Pre-form; post-form = Anchors + Post-form; one attempt each; review after close.
7. Keep item IDs (`PL-Q1`, `M1-K1`, …) unchanged if you want the analysis scripts to match.
8. For Module 8, also import the hallucination quiz and confidence survey from the instruments spreadsheet named in the deployment note.
9. Create sections 0–10 and activities as listed in `course_structure.csv`. Required (`Y`) rows for Modules 1–8 are the pre-assessment, the essential topic links, the post-assessment, and, in Module 8, the hallucination quiz and confidence survey. Section 10 holds the final survey and the certificate activity.

`DEPLOYMENT_README.md` states that human approvals needed before step 3 (bank import for official use) are: item review (S1.4 pack), cut scores (H3), certificate wording (H6), and the privacy statement (H11). A sandbox import for the course team to inspect the banks is still useful; do not treat sandbox scores as official pilot evidence.

### 5.3 Placement (built; cut scores await H3)

The test has 20 items, four in each of five domains:

| Code | Domain | Maps towards |
|---|---|---|
| Q | Quantitative readiness | Background mathematics the course assumes (Lesson 1.1). Not itself a module |
| D | Data, design and description | Modules 1–2 |
| P | Probability and variation | Module 3 |
| I | Inference | Modules 4 and 6 |
| R | Relationships and prediction | Modules 5, 7 and 9 |

Module 8 is required for every learner and is not placed.

Draft routing rules ship in `content/placement99.py` and are labelled draft on the site. The Copilot recommendation recorded for **H3** is: advisory (not compulsory); ≥ 3/4 per domain = ready; 2/4 = core route; ≤ 1/4 = start here. **Do not treat those cuts, or advisory-versus-compulsory status, as approved.** Until H3 is recorded, tell students that routing is advisory. Nothing on the site is an exemption decision.

### 5.4 Certificates and vouchers — quote the draft rules, do not rewrite them

Recommended wording and issue rules are in `stage1/moodle/package/completion_certificate_rules.md`. That file is itself a draft for approval (decision **H6**). The site’s “certificate / endorsement / distinction” labels remain progress labels only.

Quoted from that file, not rewritten:

> Wording (recommended): “Certificate of Completion — FlippedStat module *N*: *title*. Issued by the Department of Statistics and Data Science, CUHK. This certificate records completion of a self-paced learning resource; it carries no academic credit.” Include a verification code.

The same file drafts the issue condition as: (any module complete) **and** final survey submitted; automatic issue and e-mail; one certificate per learner per module completed; plugin *Custom certificate* (`mod_customcert`) or *Workplace certificates* (`tool_certificate`), whichever CUHK Moodle provides.

HK$50 vouchers for the first 50 completers are a proposal deliverable. Only an eligibility rule specification exists. Procurement and distribution have **not** started. If a budget contingency applies, the cap recorded in that file is 30. This guide is not a voucher scheme and does not change those numbers.

### 5.5 Privacy, ethics, and KPI measurement

`privacy_retention_DRAFT.md` is a working draft for **H11**. It is not legal advice and has not been checked against CUHK policy. Before the first cohort, the draft calls for a personal information collection statement and a check with ORKTS on whether ethics review is required for publication of results.

KPI operational definitions (relative gain for KPI 2.3; hallucination-quiz rule for 5.1; confidence-gain rule for 5.2; and others in the crosswalk) are **proposed, not approved** (**H2**, **H4**, **H5**). No KPI in the 18 November 2026 gap check is marked achieved. Several can be measured only after Moodle is live. This guide does not invent enrolment numbers or results.

## 6. Slides and videos

These materials are English drafts and scaffolds. They are not a claim of finished production, WCAG sign-off, or institutional approval. Do not add a CUHK crest or any lockup that would imply approval of a draft.

### 6.1 Beamer slides — `stage8/slides/`

Platform is Beamer (LaTeX), not PowerPoint or Google Slides. There are two products:

| Product | Where | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| Module-length decks | `M1_Statistical_Thinking.tex` … `M8_Responsible_Ethical_AI.tex` | One long source per official module, with a section per official topic |
| Short per-topic decks | `topics/M1/` … `topics/M8/` | One standalone short deck per official topic, plus one short overview deck per module (161 official `.tex` files: 153 topics + 8 overviews). Inventory: `topics/manifest.csv` |

Both reuse `theme/beamerthemeFlippedStat.sty`. Official reportable units are Modules 1–8. Optional Module 9 is not generated in the official slides folder.

Short topic decks are meant for self-study of one official topic (title frame, about four to eight teaching frames, and a closing check / next-step frame). Nine companion case topics in Module 6 (C4.1–C4.9) have thin extracted lesson fields; their short decks are honestly shorter and do not invent worked numbers — open the site page for the worked path.

**PDFs may be uncompiled.** A TeX engine was not available in the environment that wrote the sources (a previous TeX Live apt install failed on Debian mirror errors). The `.tex` sources are the deliverable to edit. Compile locally with the commands in `stage8/slides/README.md` (`compile_slides.sh` for module-length decks; `compile_topic_slides.sh` for short decks).

### 6.2 Programme-map scripts — `stage8/scripts/`

All **32** official programme-map videos (8 module overviews + 24 concept videos, Modules 1–8) have English drafts: `BEATS.md`, `NARRATION.md`, and `captions.vtt`. The map is `stage8/VIDEO_PROGRAMME_MAP.md` (and the companion CSV). Module 9 was not scripted.

Target length on the map: overviews 6–8 minutes; concept videos 4–7 minutes (rarely 8). Duration estimates in the script folders use 150 words/minute and will need a booth pass.

Formats allowed: motion graphics (including a digital blackboard), illustration, and site screencast. **No AI live-action people.** Palette: navy text, teal highlights, amber warnings, red errors, green verified numbers.

Some later scripts were drafted against v10.4-dev and may still carry a “v9.9 / v10.4-dev” end-card line. If you record site screencasts now, use the current agreed tip (v10.7-dev unless the course team says otherwise) and check the script against the page you will film. A short alignment note exists at `logs/stage8_scripts_v10.6_align_2026-11-18.md`; films were not re-exported.

### 6.3 OpenShot projects — `stage8/openshot/`

These are **editable OpenShot projects, not finished films**. There are no MP4 files in that folder, and nothing there was passed through ffmpeg. This environment is not used to render video.

- Official Modules 1–8: 169 projects (8 overviews + 153 official-topic projects + 8 scripted concept projects that are not themselves a whole official topic).
- Optional Module 9: 57 projects only under `projects/optional-M9/`, with `[OPTIONAL]` in the title.
- Each project is a 1920×1080, 30 fps, 16:9 still sequence, with a sidecar `.vtt` and a sibling `*_media/` folder. Keep those three together. Paths inside the `.osp` are relative.
- Scripted IDs have richer, beat-timed timelines. Other topic videos are honest scaffolds (title, teaching-point stills, end card). Scaffold stills do not invent keyed statistics.

When you edit a project, the matching short Beamer deck is the intended visual source for later still replacement. Overview `V-M1-OV` pairs with `stage8/slides/topics/M1/M1_overview.tex`, and official topic `V-T-1.1` with `topics/M1/T-1.1_*.tex`, and likewise for other modules.

Narration, human edit of stills, screencast footage, and export (OpenShot export / ffmpeg) are a later step. Do not treat a short-deck PDF, when compiled, or these still sequences as a finished video.
