#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""FlippedStat — curated Hong Kong official-extract teaching files (18 Nov 2026).

Builds licence-labelled CSV extracts from snapshots of Census and Statistics
Department (C&SD) web-table APIs, plus a small district lookup. Writes:

  content/data/hk_extracts/*          (student-facing extracts + codebooks)
  build/hk_files.json                 (filename -> text, for WebR / FSR mounts)

Optionally merges new files into build/rev90_files.json without changing
existing keys. Does not invent official figures. Derived columns are labelled.

usage:
  python tools/hk_local_data.py
  python tools/hk_local_data.py --merge-rev90
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse, csv, io, json, math, statistics
from pathlib import Path

# Sibling helper (this file is run as a script from the repo root or tools/).
import importlib.util as _ilu
_w3p = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "hk_local_data_wave3.py"
_w3s = _ilu.spec_from_file_location("hk_local_data_wave3", _w3p)
_w3m = _ilu.module_from_spec(_w3s)
_w3s.loader.exec_module(_w3m)
build_wave3 = _w3m.build_wave3
extended_licence_markdown = _w3m.extended_licence_markdown

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RAW = ROOT / "sources" / "hk_extracts_raw"
OUTDIR = ROOT / "content" / "data" / "hk_extracts"
BUILD = ROOT / "build"

# Standard region grouping, matching the region totals already published in
# C&SD table 110-02001 (Hong Kong Island / Kowloon / New Territories).
REGION = {
    "A": "Hong Kong Island",
    "B": "Hong Kong Island",
    "C": "Hong Kong Island",
    "D": "Hong Kong Island",
    "E": "Kowloon",
    "F": "Kowloon",
    "G": "Kowloon",
    "H": "Kowloon",
    "J": "Kowloon",
    "K": "New Territories",
    "L": "New Territories",
    "M": "New Territories",
    "N": "New Territories",
    "P": "New Territories",
    "Q": "New Territories",
    "R": "New Territories",
    "S": "New Territories",
    "T": "New Territories",
}

RETRIEVAL = "2026-11-18 (Asia/Hong_Kong)"
CSD_IP = "https://www.censtatd.gov.hk/en/page_31.html"
DATA_GOV_TERMS = "https://data.gov.hk/en/terms-and-conditions"
ATTRIBUTION = (
    "Source: Census and Statistics Department, Hong Kong SAR Government "
    "(C&SD website / data.gov.hk). Intellectual property in the official "
    "statistics belongs to the Government of the Hong Kong Special "
    "Administrative Region. This is not a government publication and does "
    "not imply endorsement by the Government or C&SD."
)


def tocsv(header, rows):
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(header)
    w.writerows(rows)
    return buf.getvalue()


def load_snap(name):
    return json.loads((RAW / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def fig(rows, year, code, sv):
    hits = [r for r in rows if r["period"] == str(year) and r["DC"] == code and r["sv"] == sv]
    if len(hits) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"expected 1 row for year={year} DC={code!r} sv={sv}; got {hits}")
    return hits[0]["figure"]


def quartile_median_of_half(vals):
    """Quartiles as the median of the lower/upper half (even n: halves do not overlap)."""
    s = sorted(vals)
    n = len(s)
    if n % 2 == 0:
        lower, upper = s[: n // 2], s[n // 2 :]
    else:
        lower, upper = s[: n // 2 + 1], s[n // 2 :]
    return statistics.median(lower), statistics.median(s), statistics.median(upper)


def pearson(x, y):
    n = len(x)
    mx, my = sum(x) / n, sum(y) / n
    num = sum((a - mx) * (b - my) for a, b in zip(x, y))
    den = math.sqrt(sum((a - mx) ** 2 for a in x) * sum((b - my) ** 2 for b in y))
    return num / den


def build():
    pop_snap = load_snap("csd_110-02001_2016_2025.json")
    inc_snap = load_snap("csd_130-06806_2016_2025.json")
    cpi_snap = load_snap("csd_510-60001_ccpi_monthly_2015_2026.json")
    pop, inc, cpi = pop_snap["dataSet"], inc_snap["dataSet"], cpi_snap["dataSet"]

    names = {r["DC"]: r["DCDesc"] for r in inc if r["DC"]}
    codes = sorted(names, key=lambda c: (REGION[c], names[c]))

    lookup_rows = [[c, names[c], REGION[c]] for c in codes]
    # Official region totals from table 110-02001
    for code, label in (("HK", "Hong Kong Island"), ("KLN", "Kowloon"), ("NT", "New Territories"), ("", "Hong Kong (all districts)")):
        pass

    # --- long extracts (official figures only; two years) ---
    pop_rows = []
    for year in (2016, 2025):
        for r in sorted(pop, key=lambda x: (x["period"], x["DC"], x["sv"])):
            if r["period"] != str(year):
                continue
            pop_rows.append([
                year,
                r["DC"] or "ALL",
                r["DCDesc"],
                "region_total" if r["DC"] in ("", "HK", "KLN", "NT") else "district",
                r["sv"],
                r["svDesc"],
                r["figure"],
            ])

    inc_rows = []
    for year in (2016, 2025):
        for r in sorted(inc, key=lambda x: (x["period"], x["DC"] or "ALL", x["sv"])):
            if r["period"] != str(year):
                continue
            inc_rows.append([
                year,
                r["DC"] or "ALL",
                r["DCDesc"],
                "total" if r["DC"] == "" else "district",
                r["sv"],
                "average_household_size" if r["sv"] == "ADHS" else "median_monthly_household_income_hkd",
                r["svDesc"],
                r["figure"],
            ])

    profile_rows = []
    gained_inc, lost_inc = [], []
    xs, ys = [], []
    district_rows = []
    for c in codes:
        p0 = fig(pop, 2016, c, "MYPOPN_LAND")
        p1 = fig(pop, 2025, c, "MYPOPN_LAND")
        area = fig(pop, 2025, c, "LA")
        dens = fig(pop, 2025, c, "POPN_D")
        inc0 = fig(inc, 2016, c, "MED_DH_INC")
        inc1 = fig(inc, 2025, c, "MED_DH_INC")
        sz1 = fig(inc, 2025, c, "ADHS")
        change = round(float(p1) - float(p0), 1)
        gained = "yes" if float(p1) > float(p0) else "no"
        rec = [
            c, names[c], REGION[c],
            p0, p1, change, gained,
            area, dens, inc0, inc1, sz1,
        ]
        profile_rows.append(rec)
        (gained_inc if gained == "yes" else lost_inc).append(int(inc1))
        xs.append(float(dens))
        ys.append(float(inc1))
        district_rows.append({"district_en": names[c], "region_en": REGION[c], "gained": gained, "inc2025": float(inc1), "dens2025": float(dens), "pop2025": float(p1)})

    # keys (FlippedStat calculations, not official C&SD statistics)
    q1g, medg, q3g = quartile_median_of_half(gained_inc)
    q1l, medl, q3l = quartile_median_of_half(lost_inc)
    r_inc_dens = round(pearson(xs, ys), 2)
    keys = {
        "n_districts": 18,
        "n_gained_2016_2025": len(gained_inc),
        "n_lost_or_unchanged_2016_2025": len(lost_inc),
        "median_of_district_median_incomes_2025_gained_hkd": medg,
        "median_of_district_median_incomes_2025_lost_hkd": medl,
        "q1_district_median_incomes_2025_gained_hkd": q1g,
        "q3_district_median_incomes_2025_gained_hkd": q3g,
        "iqr_district_median_incomes_2025_gained_hkd": q3g - q1g,
        "q1_district_median_incomes_2025_lost_hkd": q1l,
        "q3_district_median_incomes_2025_lost_hkd": q3l,
        "iqr_district_median_incomes_2025_lost_hkd": q3l - q1l,
        "pearson_r_2025_median_income_vs_density": r_inc_dens,
        "hk_land_pop_000_2016": fig(pop, 2016, "", "MYPOPN_LAND"),
        "hk_land_pop_000_2025": fig(pop, 2025, "", "MYPOPN_LAND"),
        "hk_median_monthly_hh_income_2016": fig(inc, 2016, "", "MED_DH_INC"),
        "hk_median_monthly_hh_income_2025": fig(inc, 2025, "", "MED_DH_INC"),
        "quartile_method": "median of the lower/upper half of the district values; for even n the two halves do not overlap",
        "official_region_land_pop_000_2016": {
            "Hong Kong Island": fig(pop, 2016, "HK", "MYPOPN_LAND"),
            "Kowloon": fig(pop, 2016, "KLN", "MYPOPN_LAND"),
            "New Territories": fig(pop, 2016, "NT", "MYPOPN_LAND"),
        },
        "official_region_land_pop_000_2025": {
            "Hong Kong Island": fig(pop, 2025, "HK", "MYPOPN_LAND"),
            "Kowloon": fig(pop, 2025, "KLN", "MYPOPN_LAND"),
            "New Territories": fig(pop, 2025, "NT", "MYPOPN_LAND"),
        },
    }

    # Wave-2 keys (still FlippedStat calculations on official figures, unless labelled official).
    inc18 = [d["inc2025"] for d in district_rows]
    dens18 = [d["dens2025"] for d in district_rows]
    q1_18, med_18, q3_18 = quartile_median_of_half(inc18)
    q1_d, med_d, q3_d = quartile_median_of_half(dens18)
    n18 = 18
    mean_inc = sum(inc18) / n18
    sd_inc_sample = (sum((x - mean_inc) ** 2 for x in inc18) / (n18 - 1)) ** 0.5
    mean_dens = sum(dens18) / n18
    sd_dens_sample = (sum((x - mean_dens) ** 2 for x in dens18) / (n18 - 1)) ** 0.5

    def zscore(x, mean, sd):
        return round((x - mean) / sd, 2)

    def named(district):
        hits = [d for d in district_rows if d["district_en"] == district]
        if len(hits) != 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"expected 1 district {district!r}")
        return hits[0]

    cw, kt, islands = named("Central and Western"), named("Kwun Tong"), named("Islands")
    tot25 = keys["hk_land_pop_000_2025"]
    reg25 = keys["official_region_land_pop_000_2025"]

    def share(part, total, nd=1):
        return round(100 * part / total, nd)

    # Contingency of the 18 districts (derived gained flag x official region name)
    from collections import Counter
    cells = Counter((d["region_en"], d["gained"]) for d in district_rows)
    region_n = Counter(d["region_en"] for d in district_rows)

    keys.update({
        "n_districts_by_region": {
            "Hong Kong Island": region_n["Hong Kong Island"],
            "Kowloon": region_n["Kowloon"],
            "New Territories": region_n["New Territories"],
        },
        "n_gained_by_region": {
            "Hong Kong Island": cells[("Hong Kong Island", "yes")],
            "Kowloon": cells[("Kowloon", "yes")],
            "New Territories": cells[("New Territories", "yes")],
        },
        "n_lost_by_region": {
            "Hong Kong Island": cells[("Hong Kong Island", "no")],
            "Kowloon": cells[("Kowloon", "no")],
            "New Territories": cells[("New Territories", "no")],
        },
        "official_hk_land_pop_000_2025_Hong_Kong_Island": reg25["Hong Kong Island"],
        "official_hk_land_pop_000_2025_Kowloon": reg25["Kowloon"],
        "official_hk_land_pop_000_2025_New_Territories": reg25["New Territories"],
        "flippedstat_share_pct_2025_official_region_pop_of_official_hk_total": {
            "Hong Kong Island": share(reg25["Hong Kong Island"], tot25),
            "Kowloon": share(reg25["Kowloon"], tot25),
            "New Territories": share(reg25["New Territories"], tot25),
        },
        "sum_of_18_published_district_land_pop_000_2025": round(sum(d["pop2025"] for d in district_rows), 1),
        "rounding_note_2025": "The 18 published district mid-year land populations sum to 7497.9 thousand, which is 0.1 thousand above the official Hong Kong total of 7497.8 thousand. Use official region and Hong Kong totals, not the district sum. The C&SD table notes that figures may not add up to the totals due to rounding.",
        "five_number_2025_district_median_incomes_hkd": {
            "min": min(inc18),
            "q1": q1_18,
            "median": med_18,
            "q3": q3_18,
            "max": max(inc18),
            "iqr": q3_18 - q1_18,
            "lower_fence": q1_18 - 1.5 * (q3_18 - q1_18),
            "upper_fence": q3_18 + 1.5 * (q3_18 - q1_18),
            "n_tukey_outliers": 0,
            "min_district": "Kwun Tong",
            "max_district": "Central and Western",
        },
        "mean_of_18_district_median_incomes_2025_hkd_rounded": round(mean_inc),
        "sample_sd_of_18_district_median_incomes_2025_hkd_rounded": round(sd_inc_sample),
        "sd_method": "sample standard deviation, divisor n-1, matching R sd() and jamovi; labelled as a FlippedStat calculation on the 18 official district medians",
        "z_2025_median_income_sample_sd": {
            "Central and Western": zscore(cw["inc2025"], mean_inc, sd_inc_sample),
            "Kwun Tong": zscore(kt["inc2025"], mean_inc, sd_inc_sample),
        },
        "mean_of_18_district_densities_2025_rounded": round(mean_dens),
        "sample_sd_of_18_district_densities_2025_rounded": round(sd_dens_sample),
        "z_2025_density_sample_sd": {
            "Kwun Tong": zscore(kt["dens2025"], mean_dens, sd_dens_sample),
            "Islands": zscore(islands["dens2025"], mean_dens, sd_dens_sample),
        },
        "n_of_18_incomes_within_1_sample_sd_of_mean": sum(1 for x in inc18 if abs(x - mean_inc) <= sd_inc_sample),
        "n_of_18_incomes_within_2_sample_sd_of_mean": sum(1 for x in inc18 if abs(x - mean_inc) <= 2 * sd_inc_sample),
        "wave2_topics_using_these_keys": ["1.3", "3.1", "3.3", "3.4", "3.5", "3.6"],
    })

    # CPI monthly composite
    idx = {(r["period"], r["svDesc"]): r["figure"] for r in cpi}
    periods = sorted({r["period"] for r in cpi})
    cpi_rows = []
    for p in periods:
        year, month = int(p[:4]), int(p[4:])
        cpi_rows.append([
            f"{year:04d}-{month:02d}",
            year,
            month,
            idx.get((p, "Index"), ""),
            idx.get((p, "Year-on-year % change"), ""),
        ])

    OUTDIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    files = {}

    files["hk_district_lookup.csv"] = tocsv(
        ["district_code", "district_en", "region_en"],
        lookup_rows,
    )
    files["hk_district_lookup_codebook.md"] = f"""# hk_district_lookup.csv — codebook

**Kind.** Teaching lookup table, not an official C&SD statistical table.
**Retrieval date.** {RETRIEVAL}

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| district_code | District Council district code as used in C&SD tables 110-02001 and 130-06806 (A–T, skipping I and O) |
| district_en | English district name as published in those C&SD tables |
| region_en | Region name matching the region totals already published in table 110-02001: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon, New Territories |

The 18-district / three-region classification is a public geographic fact also tabulated by C&SD. Codes and English names were taken from the 2016–2025 snapshot of those official tables (see `hk_district_population_110-02001.csv`).

{ATTRIBUTION}
C&SD Intellectual Property Rights Notice: {CSD_IP}
DATA.GOV.HK Terms of Use: {DATA_GOV_TERMS}
"""

    files["hk_district_population_110-02001.csv"] = tocsv(
        ["year", "district_code", "district_en", "geo_level", "series_code", "unit", "figure"],
        pop_rows,
    )
    files["hk_district_population_110-02001_codebook.md"] = f"""# hk_district_population_110-02001.csv — codebook

**Kind.** Official public extract (C&SD Table 110-02001), subsetted. Not synthetic.
**Official title.** Land area, land population and population density by District Council district
**Provider.** Census Planning Section (1), Census and Statistics Department, Hong Kong SAR Government
**API used.** https://www.censtatd.gov.hk/api/get.php?id=110-02001&lang=en&full_series=1
**Also listed at.** https://data.gov.hk/en-data/dataset/hk-censtatd-tablechart-110-02001
**Retrieval date.** {RETRIEVAL}

**Modification (must be stated).** This file is a subset: calendar years 2016 and 2025 only, all series and all geographic levels in the snapshot. Figures are copied from the official API and are not recalculated. Column names were added for teaching use.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| year | Mid-year of the official figure (2016 or 2025) |
| district_code | C&SD code; `ALL` = Hong Kong total; `HK` / `KLN` / `NT` = region totals |
| district_en | Official English name |
| geo_level | `district` or `region_total` |
| series_code | `LA` land area; `MYPOPN_LAND` mid-year land population; `POPN_D` population density |
| unit | As published: `(sq. km)`; `Number (‘000)`; `(Persons per sq. km)` |
| figure | Official figure. Population is in thousands of persons |

**Selected official notes (abridged; see the C&SD table for the full notes).**
- Geographical classification is by District Council district as defined by the Registration and Electoral Office applicable for that year. Boundaries of Wan Chai and Eastern adopted since 2016 differ from 2015 and earlier; figures for those two districts from 2016 onward are not strictly comparable with earlier years. This extract starts in 2016 for that reason.
- Land population figures are as at mid-year. Marine population and area for reservoirs are not included in calculating population density. Land area figures are those adopted for calculating population density.
- Figures may not add up to the totals due to rounding.

{ATTRIBUTION}
C&SD Intellectual Property Rights Notice: {CSD_IP}
DATA.GOV.HK Terms of Use: {DATA_GOV_TERMS}
"""

    files["hk_district_household_130-06806.csv"] = tocsv(
        ["year", "district_code", "district_en", "geo_level", "series_code", "series_en", "unit", "figure"],
        inc_rows,

## What this pass does not ship

- The R package **hkdatasets** (CRAN; https://github.com/Hong-Kong-Districts-Info/hkdatasets) was reviewed. Its DESCRIPTION states Licence **GPL-3** and that “All of the data in this package is available in the public domain.” The GitHub README carries an **MIT** badge, which does not match the DESCRIPTION. Underlying sources (districtcouncils.gov.hk, dce2019.hk01.com, Lands Department, Transport Department FOI microdata) may have their own terms. This pass therefore prefers C&SD / data.gov.hk tables whose reuse conditions were read from the source.
- `hkdc` (2019 District Councillors) is not shipped: it contains names, office addresses, phone numbers, emails and social-media URLs. Aggregate election teaching use is deferred pending a human licence review of the HK01 and district-council sources.
- `hk_accidents` / `hk_casualties` / `hk_vehicles` microdata are not shipped (size, ethical caution, FOI provenance). Official TD annual accident *publications* listed on data.gov.hk remain a possible later extract if a licence-clean aggregated table is confirmed.
- `hkstreetnames20` (source: landsd.gov.hk) is deferred until Lands Department reuse terms are verified from the source.
- `hkagepop19` is a 2019 age-by-district series in the package described as estimates based on calculated census percentages. Official C&SD tables were used instead.

## Optional desktop R (not the Moodle / WebR path)

WebR and some Moodle CSP setups may block `install.packages("hkdatasets")`. Students should use the CSV extracts mounted in this course. On a local desktop R, the package can be tried as an optional extra:

```r
# Optional, desktop R only — not required for FlippedStat exercises.
# Package licence: see the CRAN DESCRIPTION (GPL-3 as of the copy reviewed
# on 18 Nov 2026). Underlying data sources have their own terms.
install.packages("hkdatasets")
library(hkdatasets)
head(hkdistrict_summary)
```

## Reconstruction

Snapshots of the API records used here are stored under `sources/hk_extracts_raw/`. Regenerate the student files with:

```
python tools/hk_local_data.py --merge-rev90
```
"""

    # Wave 3: additional official series (HKO rainfall/temperature/lightning; C&SD 115-01012A).
    # Existing C&SD district/CPI file bytes above are not regenerated by the wave-3 helper.
    w3_files, w3_keys = build_wave3()
    overlap = set(files) & set(w3_files)
    if overlap:
        raise SystemExit(f"wave3 would overwrite existing extract names: {sorted(overlap)}")
    files.update(w3_files)
    keys.update(w3_keys)
    files["DATA_SOURCES_AND_LICENCE.md"] = extended_licence_markdown(
        files["DATA_SOURCES_AND_LICENCE.md"], w3_files
    )

    # write to disk
    for name, text in files.items():

        (OUTDIR / name).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")

    BUILD.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (BUILD / "hk_files.json").write_text(json.dumps(files, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    (BUILD / "hk_data_keys.json").write_text(json.dumps(keys, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print("wrote", len(files), "files to", OUTDIR)
    print("keys:", json.dumps(keys, indent=2))
    return files, keys


def merge_rev90(files, refresh_official=False):
    path = BUILD / "rev90_files.json"
    if not path.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"missing {path}; run tools/rev90_data.py first")
    current = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    overlap = set(current) & set(files)
    if overlap and not refresh_official:
        raise SystemExit(f"refusing to overwrite existing rev90 keys: {sorted(overlap)}")
    if refresh_official:
        updated = []
        added = []
        for name, text in files.items():
            if name in current:
                if current[name] != text:
                    current[name] = text
                    updated.append(name)
            else:
                current[name] = text
                added.append(name)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(current, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
        print("refreshed official keys in", path, "updated", updated, "added", added, "total keys", len(current))
        return
    current.update(files)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(current, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print("merged", len(files), "files into", path, "total keys", len(current))


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--merge-rev90", action="store_true", help="append new files to build/rev90_files.json")
    ap.add_argument("--refresh-official", action="store_true", help="update already-merged official extract keys (codebooks) without touching synthetic keys")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    files, _ = build()
    if args.merge_rev90 or args.refresh_official:
        merge_rev90(files, refresh_official=args.refresh_official)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def tocsv(header, rows):
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(header)
    w.writerows(rows)
    return buf.getvalue()


def pearson_skew(xs):
    n = len(xs)
    m = statistics.mean(xs)
    s = statistics.stdev(xs)
    return (n / ((n - 1) * (n - 2))) * sum(((x - m) / s) ** 3 for x in xs)


def load_hko_csv(name, numeric=float):
    path = RAW / name
    recs = []
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
    lines = text.splitlines()
    # Two title lines, then header, then rows until a footer legend line.
    header = None
    start = 0
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if "Year" in line and "Month" in line and "Day" in line:
            header = line
            start = i + 1
            break
    if header is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"no header in {name}")
    reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO("\n".join([header] + lines[start:])))
    for row in reader:
        yraw = (row.get("年/Year") or "").strip()
        if not yraw or not yraw[0].isdigit():
            continue
        y, m, d = int(row["年/Year"]), int(row["月/Month"]), int(row["日/Day"])
        raw = row["數值/Value"]
        c = (row.get("數據完整性/data Completeness") or "").strip()
        if raw == "Trace":
            recs.append((y, m, d, raw, None, c))
            continue
        try:
            recs.append((y, m, d, raw, numeric(raw), c))
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            recs.append((y, m, d, raw, None, c))
    return recs


def window(recs, y0=2016, y1=2025):
    return [r for r in recs if y0 <= r[0] <= y1]


def build_wave3():
    files = {}
    keys = {}

    # ---------- Rainfall ----------
    rain = window(load_hko_csv("hko_daily_rainfall_HKO_ALL.csv"))
    if len(rain) != 3653:
        raise SystemExit(f"expected 3653 rainfall days 2016-2025, got {len(rain)}")
    if any(r[5] != "C" for r in rain):
        raise SystemExit("unexpected non-C completeness in 2016-2025 rainfall extract")
    rain_rows = []
    for y, m, d, raw, val, c in rain:
        rain_rows.append([
            y, m, d, f"{y:04d}-{m:02d}-{d:02d}",
            raw,
            "" if val is None else val,
            "yes" if raw == "Trace" else "no",
            c,
        ])
    files["hk_hko_daily_rainfall_HKO_2016_2025.csv"] = tocsv(
        ["year", "month", "day", "date", "rainfall_published", "rainfall_mm", "is_trace", "completeness"],
        rain_rows,
    )
    wet = [r[4] for r in rain if r[4] is not None and r[4] > 0]
    n_trace = sum(1 for r in rain if r[3] == "Trace")
    n_zero = sum(1 for r in rain if r[4] == 0)
    n_wet = len(wet)
    log10w = [math.log10(v) for v in wet]
    sqrtw = [math.sqrt(v) for v in wet]
    max_rain = max(wet)
    max_dates = [f"{r[0]:04d}-{r[1]:02d}-{r[2]:02d}" for r in rain if r[4] == max_rain]
    keys.update({
        "rainfall_station": "Hong Kong Observatory (HKO)",
        "rainfall_years": "2016-2025",
        "rainfall_n_days": 3653,
        "rainfall_n_trace": n_trace,
        "rainfall_n_zero_mm": n_zero,
        "rainfall_n_measurable_wet": n_wet,
        "rainfall_wet_min_mm": min(wet),
        "rainfall_wet_max_mm": max_rain,
        "rainfall_wet_max_date": max_dates,
        "rainfall_wet_mean_mm": round(statistics.mean(wet), 2),
        "rainfall_wet_median_mm": statistics.median(wet),
        "rainfall_wet_sample_sd_mm": round(statistics.stdev(wet), 2),
        "rainfall_wet_pearson_skew": round(pearson_skew(wet), 2),
        "rainfall_log10_wet_mean": round(statistics.mean(log10w), 2),
        "rainfall_log10_wet_median": round(statistics.median(log10w), 2),
        "rainfall_log10_wet_pearson_skew": round(pearson_skew(log10w), 2),
        "rainfall_sqrt_wet_mean": round(statistics.mean(sqrtw), 2),
        "rainfall_sqrt_wet_median": round(statistics.median(sqrtw), 2),
        "rainfall_sqrt_wet_pearson_skew": round(pearson_skew(sqrtw), 2),
        "rainfall_wet_span_orders_of_magnitude": round(math.log10(max(wet) / min(wet)), 2),
        "trace_definition_from_source_file": "Trace means rainfall less than 0.05 mm",
        "skew_method": "bias-adjusted Pearson moment coefficient of skewness, using the sample SD (divisor n-1); FlippedStat calculation, not an official HKO or C&SD statistic",
    })

## FlippedStat calculations on the official 2016–2025 figures (not official HKO statistics)

Of 3,653 days: **1,544** have a published total of 0.0 mm, **632** are official Trace, and **1,477** have a published positive amount (“measurable wet days”). Among those 1,477 amounts: minimum **0.1** mm; maximum **425.0** mm on **8 September 2023**; mean **16.73** mm; median **4.3** mm; sample SD **33.93** mm; Pearson skew **5.28**. The 1,477 values span **3.63** orders of magnitude (425.0 / 0.1). After a base-10 log: mean **0.58**, median **0.63**, Pearson skew **−0.14**. After a square root: mean **2.99**, median **2.07**, Pearson skew **1.81**. These summaries exclude Trace days (log of zero is undefined; Trace is below 0.05 mm and is not a published millimetre amount).

Use this file to see why a log transformation can reveal structure in a strongly right-skewed official series. It is a course illustration, not a climatological analysis published by the Observatory.

    # ---------- Temperature ----------
    temp = window(load_hko_csv("hko_daily_mean_temp_HKO_ALL.csv"))

        raise SystemExit(f"expected 3653 temperature days, got {len(temp)}")

        raise SystemExit("missing or non-C temperature values in 2016-2025")

        temp_rows.append([

    )
    jja = [r[4] for r in temp if r[1] in (6, 7, 8)]

    jja_mu, jja_sd = statistics.mean(jja), statistics.stdev(jja)
    all_mu, all_sd = statistics.mean(all_t), statistics.stdev(all_t)

    def coverage(xs, mu, sd):
        return {k: sum(1 for x in xs if abs(x - mu) <= k * sd) for k in (1, 2, 3)}

**June–August 2016–2025** (n = **920** days): minimum **24.1** °C on **4 June 2024**; maximum **32.2** °C on **27 July 2023**; mean **29.23** °C; median **29.50** °C; sample SD (n−1) **1.35** °C; Pearson skew **−0.75** (mild left skew).     # ---------- Live births ----------

def extended_licence_markdown(existing_markdown: str, wave3_files: dict) -> str:
    """Replace only the file table and add an HKO / 115-01012A section; keep wave-1 wording otherwise."""
    extra = f"""
## Wave 3 files added on {RETRIEVAL}

| File | Kind | Official source |
|---|---|---|
| hk_hko_daily_rainfall_HKO_2016_2025.csv | official extract (2016–2025 subset) | HKO daily total rainfall at the Hong Kong Observatory, via DATA.GOV.HK |
| hk_hko_daily_mean_temp_HKO_2016_2025.csv | official extract (2016–2025 subset) | HKO daily mean temperature at the Hong Kong Observatory, via DATA.GOV.HK |
| hk_hko_daily_cg_lightning_2016_2025.csv | official extract (2016–2025 subset) | HKO daily total cloud-to-ground lightning count over Hong Kong territory, via DATA.GOV.HK |
| hk_hko_jja_lightning_days_2016_2025.csv | teaching table derived from the official daily lightning extract | same official daily series |
| hk_live_births_monthly_115-01012A.csv | official extract (monthly totals, 1976–2025) | C&SD table 115-01012A |

Each CSV has a matching `*_codebook.md`.

**Hong Kong Observatory attribution.** {HKO_ATTR} The rainfall, temperature and lightning datasets are listed on DATA.GOV.HK and were retrieved from the official open-data endpoints named in each codebook. Reuse follows the DATA.GOV.HK Terms of Use as read on 18 Nov 2026. A separate Intellectual Property Rights Notice applies to materials on the Observatory website; these extracts are taken from the open-data portal / API, not copied from website prose or graphics.

**Live births attribution.** {CSD_ATTR} C&SD Intellectual Property Rights Notice: {CSD_IP}

Worked numbers added in wave 3 are FlippedStat calculations on official figures, or FlippedStat derivations such as a count of days, and are labelled as such. They are not official HKO or C&SD statistics.
"""
    if "## Wave 3 files added" in existing_markdown:
        # idempotent: drop a previous wave-3 section if the generator is re-run
        head = existing_markdown.split("## Wave 3 files added")[0].rstrip() + "\n"
        return head + "\n" + extra
    return existing_markdown.rstrip() + "\n" + extra

"""FlippedStat v7.0 integration builder (final form, all v7.0 patches merged).
Assigns EVERY unit of both embedded textbooks (OpenIntro Statistics 4e edition and Learning Statistics with jamovi) to exactly
one FlippedStat home (a lesson subtopic in W1-W14/E1-E4, or a companion/depth topic chosen by the audited Phase C tracks).
Output: build/fsi_data.js (window.FSI_DATA) + logs/integration_map.csv.
Seeds: Phase C tracks (FS.track) fix the topic; TF-IDF similarity picks the lesson inside it.
Unseeded intros follow their own section/chapter; unseeded others: similarity + chapter coherence. Nothing is deleted."""
import json, re, csv, html as H
from collections import Counter
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity
import numpy as np
F=json.load(open('FSfinal.json')); O=json.load(open('OISD.json')); B=json.load(open('BOOK.json')); X=json.load(open('EXTRA.json'))
AU={c['num']:c for c in O['auth']['chapters']}
def txt(s): s=re.sub(r'<[^>]+>',' ',s or ''); return re.sub(r'\s+',' ',H.unescape(s)).strip()
def flat(o):
    if isinstance(o,str): return o
    if isinstance(o,dict): return ' '.join(flat(v) for v in o.values())
    if isinstance(o,list): return ' '.join(flat(v) for v in o)
    return ''
# ---------- course order, lessons

        for e in s['ex']:

    for pg,fld in [('orient',['goal','oneBreath','everyday','audience']),('before',['prereq']),('see',['playground','story','connect']),('lab',['lab','apps']),('wrap',['wrap'])]:
        t=txt(' '.join(flat(A.get(f,'')) for f in fld)); add(id=f'OG:{cn}:{pg}',src='O',kind='page',ch=cn,key=pg,title={'orient':'Chapter orientation','before':'Before you start: prerequisite checks','see':'See it work: playground and story','lab':'Lab and applications','wrap':'Chapter wrap-up'}[pg],text=t,words=len(t.split()),anchors=[])

========== FILE: ws/tools/m8_data.py ==========

"""Stage 5: synthetic dataset for the Module 8 three-tool comparison lab, with planted traps and the ground truth.
Traps: (1) score = -99 means 'absent from exam' (6 rows); (2) 4 rows are exact duplicates of earlier rows; (3) observational
data (tutorial format chosen by students) — any causal claim is an over-claim. Output: build/m8_data.json"""
import json, numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
rng = np.random.default_rng(8088)
n = 150
grp = rng.choice(['A', 'B'], n, p=[0.5, 0.5])
attend = np.clip(np.round(rng.normal(8.5, 2.2, n)), 0, 12).astype(int)
score = np.round(np.clip(42 + 3.1 * attend + np.where(grp == 'B', 2.0, 0) + rng.normal(0, 9, n), 0, 100)).astype(int)
df = pd.DataFrame({'student_id': [f'S{1000 + i}' for i in range(n)], 'tutorial': grp, 'attended': attend, 'score': score})
miss = rng.choice(n, 6, replace=False); df.loc[miss, 'score'] = -99
dups = df.iloc[[5, 40, 77, 120]].copy()
raw = pd.concat([df, dups]).reset_index(drop=True)
raw = raw.iloc[rng.permutation(len(raw))].reset_index(drop=True)
clean = raw.drop_duplicates().query('score != -99')
a, b = clean[clean.tutorial == 'A'].score, clean[clean.tutorial == 'B'].score
w = stats.ttest_ind(b, a, equal_var=False)
se = np.sqrt(a.var() / len(a) + b.var() / len(b))
dfw = (a.var() / len(a) + b.var() / len(b)) ** 2 / ((a.var() / len(a)) ** 2 / (len(a) - 1) + (b.var() / len(b)) ** 2 / (len(b) - 1))
ci = (b.mean() - a.mean()) + np.array([-1, 1]) * stats.t.ppf(.975, dfw) * se
r = stats.pearsonr(clean.attended, clean.score)
naive = raw  # what a careless tool does: keep duplicates and -99
na, nb = naive[naive.tutorial == 'A'].score, naive[naive.tutorial == 'B'].score
T = dict(rows_file=len(raw), rows_dup=int(raw.duplicated().sum()), rows_m99=int((raw.score == -99).sum()), n_clean=len(clean),
         n_A=len(a), n_B=len(b), mean_A=round(a.mean(), 2), mean_B=round(b.mean(), 2), diff=round(b.mean() - a.mean(), 2),
         t=round(w.statistic, 2), df=round(dfw, 1), p=round(w.pvalue, 4), ci=[round(ci[0], 2), round(ci[1], 2)],
         r_attend=round(r.statistic, 3), p_r=float(r.pvalue),
         naive_mean_A=round(na.mean(), 2), naive_mean_B=round(nb.mean(), 2), naive_n=len(raw))
csv = raw.to_csv(index=False)
json.dump(dict(T=T, csv=csv), open('build/m8_data.json', 'w'))
for k, v in T.items(): print(k, v)

========== END FILE: ws/tools/m8_data.py ==========


========== FILE: ws/tools/make_backup.py ==========

"""Make the FlippedStat workspace backups.
1) build/FlippedStat_workspace_backup_<ver>.html  — self-extracting: open in a browser and press "Download"; or run
   python restore_flippedstat.py <file>.html. Being .html, it is saved to OneDrive when delivered, so it survives sandbox wipes.

========== FILE: ws/tools/qa_ledger.py ==========

"""Stage 6 (WP3): statistical QA ledger — site-wide independent recomputation of every stated numeric calculation.

Scans every text field of every lesson card (FS.lessons), topic page (FS.content) and “Learn it in depth” stage (FSA_DATA),
finds expressions of the form  <numeric expression> = <number>[%]  and recomputes the left side.
Expressions may chain + − × ÷ / * ^, parentheses, √, e^x, and k of n (p%). Results are compared with the printed value within the
printed precision (half a unit in the last printed digit, or 0.5% relative, whichever is larger).
Output: logs/qa_ledger_<ver>.json (all rows) — consumed by tools/build_qa97.py.
Usage: python tools/qa_ledger.py build/FlippedStat_vX.html ver"""
import json, re, math, sys, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
src, ver = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
s = open(src, encoding='utf8').read()
g = lambda n: json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(s, s.index(f'window.{n}=') + len(f'window.{n}='))[0]
FS, FA = g('FS'), g('FSA_DATA')
unit_of = {t['no']: u['id'] for u in FS['units'] for t in u['topics']}
def unit(no):
    p = no.split('.'); return unit_of.get('.'.join(p[:2]), unit_of.get(p[0], '?'))
texts = []
def walk(o, where, path=''):
    if isinstance(o, str):
        t = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', o); t = (t.replace('&lt;', '<').replace('&gt;', '>').replace('&amp;', '&').replace('\u2009', ' ').replace('\xa0', ' ')
             .replace('\u2212', '−').replace('\\(', ' ').replace('\\)', ' ').replace('\\times', '×').replace('\\cdot', '×'))
        t = re.sub(r'e⁻¹\s*', 'ε^(−1)×', t); t = re.sub(r'e\^(−?[\d.]+)', r'ε^(\1)', t)
        t = re.sub(r'([\d)])([⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹]+)', lambda m: m.group(1) + '^' + m.group(2).translate(str.maketrans('⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹', '0123456789')), t)
        texts.append((where, path, t))
    elif isinstance(o, list): [walk(x, where, f'{path}[{k}]') for k, x in enumerate(o)]
    elif isinstance(o, dict): [walk(v, where, f'{path}.{k}') for k, v in o.items() if k not in ('src', 'fig', 'emb', 'viz', 'comesback', 'credit')]
for no, L in FS['lessons'].items(): walk(L, ('L', no))
for no, C in FS['content'].items(): walk(C, ('C', no))
for no, A in FA['lessons'].items(): walk(A, ('A', no))
NUMR = r'(?:\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+|\d+)(?:\.\d+)?|\.\d+'
ATOM = r'(?:(?:' + NUMR + r')\s*)?(?:√\s*|ε\^)?(?:\|?\(\s*)*\|?(?:−\s*)?(?:' + NUMR + r')\|?(?:\s*\))*\s*%?'
OP = r'(?:[+\-−×*/÷^]|x(?=\s*[\d(√]))'
RUN = r'(?:[−\-]\s*)?' + ATOM + r'(?:\s*' + OP + r'\s*' + ATOM + r')*'
CHAIN = re.compile(r'(' + RUN + r')((?:\s*[=≈]\s*' + RUN + r')+)')
def py(expr):
    e = expr.strip().replace('ε^', 'exp').replace('|', '').replace(',', '').replace('−', '-').replace('×', '*').replace('÷', '/').replace('^', '**')
    e = re.sub(r'(?<=[\d)])\s*x\s*(?=[\d(√])', '*', e)
    e = re.sub(r'(\d)\s*√', r'\1*√', e)
    e = re.sub(r'√\s*\(', 'sqrt(', e); e = re.sub(r'√\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)', r'sqrt(\1)', e)
    e = re.sub(r'(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*%', r'(\1/100)', e)
    if re.search(r'[^0-9.+\-*/() sqrtexp]', e) or e.count('(') != e.count(')'): return None
    return e
def ev(seg):
    e = py(seg)
    if e is None: return None
    try: v = eval(e, {'__builtins__': {}}, {'sqrt': math.sqrt, 'exp': math.exp})
    except Exception: return None
    return float(v) if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not math.isinf(v) else None
def lastnum(seg):
    m = re.findall(NUMR, seg); return m[-1] if m else '0'
def tol(c):
    d = len(c.split('.')[1]) if '.' in c else 0
    return 0.5 * 10 ** -d
rows, seen = [], set()
for (kind, no), path, t in texts:
    for m in CHAIN.finditer(t):
        segs = [m.group(1)] + re.split(r'\s*[=≈]\s*', m.group(2).strip())[1:]
        pre = t[max(0, m.start() - 2):m.start()]
        if re.search(r'[A-Za-z_±⁻·)\]:]\s*$', pre): continue          # symbol, ± margin, superscript, function argument
        if not any(re.search(OP, x.strip().lstrip('−-')) for x in segs): continue
        if len(segs) == 2 and re.search(r'\d\s*[–-]\s*\d', segs[0]) and not re.search(r'[×*/÷√]', segs[0]) and ' − ' not in segs[0] and ' - ' not in segs[0]: continue
        vals = [ev(x) for x in segs]
        for i in range(len(segs) - 1):
            a_, b_ = vals[i], vals[i + 1]
            if a_ is None or b_ is None: continue
            if not (re.search(OP, segs[i].strip().lstrip('−-')) or re.search(OP, segs[i + 1].strip().lstrip('−-'))): continue
            ref = segs[i + 1] if not re.search(OP, segs[i + 1].strip().lstrip('−-')) else segs[i]
            c = b_ if ref is segs[i + 1] else a_; v = a_ if ref is segs[i + 1] else b_
            digits = lastnum(ref)
            scale = 0.01 if ref.strip().endswith('%') else 1
            tl = max(tol(digits) * scale, abs(c) * 0.005) + 1e-12
            if scale == 0.01 and '%' not in (segs[i] if ref is segs[i + 1] else segs[i + 1]) and abs(v) > 1.5 * abs(c) and abs(v / 100 - c) <= tl: v = v / 100
            if abs(v - c) <= tl: st = 'verified'
            elif abs(v - c) <= 2 * tl + 0.0005 * abs(c): st = 'rounding'
            else: st = 'FLAG'
            printed = f'{segs[i].strip()} = {segs[i + 1].strip()}'
            key = (no, printed)
            if key in seen: continue
            seen.add(key)
            rows.append(dict(where=kind, no=no, unit=unit(no), path=path, printed=printed, recomputed=round(v, 6), status=st, context=t[max(0, m.start() - 90):m.end() + 60].strip()))
# k of n (p%) statements
for (kind, no), path, t in texts:
    for m in re.finditer(r'\b(\d[\d,]*) (?:of|out of) (\d[\d,]*)\b[^.;()]{0,30}?\(\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*%\)', t):
        k, n_, p = m.groups(); kk, nn = float(k.replace(',', '')), float(n_.replace(',', ''))
        if not nn or kk > nn: continue
        r = 100 * kk / nn; st = 'verified' if abs(r - float(p)) <= tol(p) + 1e-9 else ('rounding' if abs(r - float(p)) <= 2 * tol(p) + .05 else 'FLAG')
        key = (no, m.group(0))
        if key in seen: continue
        seen.add(key)
        rows.append(dict(where=kind, no=no, unit=unit(no), path=path, printed=m.group(0), recomputed=round(r, 3), status=st, context=t[max(0, m.start() - 90):m.end() + 60].strip()))
json.dump(rows, open(f'logs/qa_ledger_{ver}.json', 'w'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=0)
from collections import Counter
print(len(rows), 'calculations;', dict(Counter(r['status'] for r in rows)))
for r in rows:
    if r['status'] == 'FLAG': print(f"{r['where']}:{r['no']} | {r['printed']} | recomputed {r['recomputed']} | {r['context'][:170]}")

========== END FILE: ws/tools/qa_ledger.py ==========


========== FILE: ws/tools/rawprobe.py ==========

import sys
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b=p.chromium.launch(executable_path='/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1228/chrome-linux64/chrome',args=['--no-sandbox'])
    pg=b.new_page(); pg.goto('file:///home/claude/iso87/'+sys.argv[1]+'#t/'+sys.argv[2],timeout=120000); pg.wait_for_timeout(3000)

      await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,4000));

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 13.2  satisfaction survey: 300 rows, 289 satisfaction, 228 complete
rng = np.random.default_rng(132)
def make(nlow, nhigh, total):   # values in 1..5, nlow in {1,2,3}, nhigh in {4,5}, given integer sum
    for _ in range(200000):
        lo = rng.choice([1, 2, 3], nlow, p=[.15, .3, .55]); hi = rng.choice([4, 5], nhigh, p=[.5, .5])
        diff = total - lo.sum() - hi.sum()
        # adjust highs between 4 and 5
        hi = np.sort(hi); 
        if diff > 0:
            can = np.where(hi == 4)[0]
            if len(can) < diff: continue
            hi[can[:diff]] = 5
        elif diff < 0:
            can = np.where(hi == 5)[0]
            if len(can) < -diff: continue
            hi[can[:-diff]] = 4
        v = np.concatenate([lo, hi]); rng.shuffle(v); return v
    raise SystemExit('no solution')
comp = make(49, 179, 935)        # complete rows: mean 935/228 = 4.10, 21.5% rated <= 3

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 13.5 / 13.7  capstone wellbeing file: 300 rows, 254 complete, primary model reproduces Week 14
rng = np.random.default_rng(1314)
n = 254
yr = rng.integers(1, 5, n); facs = ['Arts', 'Business', 'Engineering', 'Science', 'Social Science']; fa = rng.integers(0, 5, n)
exh = np.round(np.clip(rng.gamma(2.0, 2.4, n), 0, 14.5), 1); exh[np.argmax(exh)] = 21.0          # the 21-hour student (14.2.2)
X = np.column_stack([np.ones(n), exh] + [(yr == k).astype(float) for k in (2, 3, 4)] + [(fa == k).astype(float) for k in (1, 2, 3, 4)])
Q, _ = np.linalg.qr(X)
def build(gamma_scale, sig):
    beta = np.array([5.2, 0.138, -0.15, -0.3, -0.42, 0.1, -0.2, 0.05, 0.12]) * np.array([1, 1] + [gamma_scale] * 7)
    z = rng_e.normal(size=n); e = z - Q @ (Q.T @ z); e = e / np.sqrt(e @ e / (n - X.shape[1])) * sig
    return X @ beta + e
rng_e = np.random.default_rng(99); z0 = None
def fit(y, Xm):
    b, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(Xm, y, rcond=None); r = y - Xm @ b; df = len(y) - Xm.shape[1]; s2 = r @ r / df
    cov = s2 * np.linalg.inv(Xm.T @ Xm); se = np.sqrt(np.diag(cov)); t = stats.t.ppf(.975, df)
    r2 = 1 - r @ r / ((y - y.mean()) @ (y - y.mean())); return b, se, t, r2
# choose sigma so that SE(b1) gives CI 0.068..0.208  (half width 0.070)
best = None
for gs in np.linspace(0.0, 3.0, 301):
    rng_e = np.random.default_rng(99)
    y = build(gs, 1.0); b, se, t, r2 = fit(y, X); sig = 0.070 / (t * se[1])
    rng_e = np.random.default_rng(99); y = build(gs, sig); b, se, t, r2 = fit(y, X)
    if best is None or abs(r2 - 0.089) < abs(best[1] - 0.089): best = (gs, r2, sig)
gs, _, sig = best; rng_e = np.random.default_rng(99); y = np.round(build(gs, sig), 6)
b, se, t, r2 = fit(y, X)
prim = dict(n=n, b=round(b[1], 3), lo=round(b[1] - t * se[1], 3), hi=round(b[1] + t * se[1], 3), r2=round(r2, 3))
assert prim['b'] == 0.138 and prim['lo'] == 0.068 and prim['hi'] == 0.208 and prim['r2'] == 0.089, prim
# sensitivity analyses recomputed on this file
keep = exh < 15; b2, se2, t2, _ = fit(y[keep], X[keep])
Xu = X[:, :2]; b3, se3, t3, _ = fit(y, Xu)
Xl = X.copy(); Xl[:, 1] = np.log(1 + exh); b4, se4, t4, _ = fit(y, Xl)
sens = dict(without_ge15=dict(n=int(keep.sum()), b=round(b2[1], 3), lo=round(b2[1] - t2 * se2[1], 3), hi=round(b2[1] + t2 * se2[1], 3)),
            unadjusted=dict(b=round(b3[1], 3), lo=round(b3[1] - t3 * se3[1], 3), hi=round(b3[1] + t3 * se3[1], 3)),
            log1p_raw=dict(b=round(b4[1], 3), lo=round(b4[1] - t4 * se4[1], 3), hi=round(b4[1] + t4 * se4[1], 3)),
            log1p_per_doubling=dict(b=round(b4[1] * np.log(2), 3), lo=round((b4[1] - t4 * se4[1]) * np.log(2), 3), hi=round((b4[1] + t4 * se4[1]) * np.log(2), 3)))
# 46 incomplete rows (missing exercise or sleep or faculty)
rows = []
for i in range(n): rows.append([int(yr[i]), facs[fa[i]], f'{exh[i]:.1f}', f'{y[i]:.3f}'])
ri = np.random.default_rng(5)
for i in range(46):
    r = [int(ri.integers(1, 5)), facs[int(ri.integers(0, 5))], f'{np.clip(ri.gamma(2, 2.4), 0, 14):.1f}', f'{np.clip(ri.normal(5.6, .9), 2, 9):.3f}']
    r[[2, 3, 1][i % 3]] = ''
    rows.append(r)
perm = np.random.default_rng(8).permutation(300); rows = [[f'W{k+1:03d}'] + rows[j] for k, j in enumerate(perm)]
OUT['wellbeing300.csv'] = tocsv(['id', 'year', 'faculty', 'exercise_h_week', 'sleep_quality'], rows)
OUT['wellbeing300_codebook.md'] = """# wellbeing300.csv — capstone codebook (synthetic, FlippedStat v9.0, seed 1314)
| Column | Meaning | Type | Missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| id | respondent | identifier | — |
| year | year of study 1–4 (reference category: 1) | ordinal, entered as a factor | — |
| faculty | faculty (reference category: Arts) | nominal | blank = not answered |
| exercise_h_week | hours of exercise last week | numeric | blank = not answered |
| sleep_quality | sleep-quality index (higher = better; scale 0–10) | numeric | blank = not answered |
Ledger: 300 file rows; 254 complete for sleep_quality ~ exercise_h_week + year + faculty; 46 rows dropped (one column blank each).
The data are synthetic. No real student is described. Primary model (pre-specified): `lm(sleep_quality ~ exercise_h_week + factor(year) + faculty)`.
"""
KEYS.append(('13.5/13.7 wellbeing300.csv primary model', prim)); KEYS.append(('14.2.2 sensitivity analyses recomputed on wellbeing300.csv', sens))
json.dump(OUT, open('build/rev90_files.json', 'w'), ensure_ascii=False)
CONV=lambda o: o.item() if hasattr(o,'item') else str(o)

========== FILE: ws/tools/split_parts.py ==========

"""Split a FlippedStat standalone HTML into parts/sNN.js (one per <script>) and hNN.html fragments; join_parts.py reverses it byte-exactly.
usage: python tools/split_parts.py <standalone.html> [outdir=parts]"""
import re,sys,os
src=open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf8').read(); out=sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv)>2 else 'parts'; os.makedirs(out,exist_ok=True)
pos=0
for k,m in enumerate(re.finditer(r'<script([^>]*)>',src)):
    b=src.find('</script>',m.end())
    open(f'{out}/h{k:02d}.html','w',encoding='utf8').write(src[pos:m.end()])
    open(f'{out}/s{k:02d}.js','w',encoding='utf8').write(src[m.end():b]); pos=b
open(f'{out}/hend.html','w',encoding='utf8').write(src[pos:]); print('parts written to',out)

========== END FILE: ws/tools/split_parts.py ==========

"""Copilot 2026-11-18: render every #t/<id> route of a standalone and record
MathJax errors, unrendered TeX left in visible text, and JS errors. Read-only."""
import sys, os, asyncio, json, re
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
src = sys.argv[1]; out = sys.argv[2]
LO = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 0; HI = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 10**6
CH = "/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1228/chrome-linux64/chrome"
RAW = re.compile(r"\\\(|\\\)|\\\[|\\\]|\\(?:frac|sqrt|hat|bar|alpha|beta|sigma|mu|times|le|ge|pm|text|mathrm|chi|pounds|%)\b|\$\$")
async def main():
    res = []
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        kw = dict(args=["--no-sandbox", "--disable-gpu"])
        if os.path.exists(CH): kw["executable_path"] = CH
        b = await p.chromium.launch(**kw)
        pg = await b.new_page(viewport={"width": 1280, "height": 900})
        pg.set_default_navigation_timeout(180000); pg.set_default_timeout(60000)
        errs = []; pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: errs.append(str(e)))
        url = "file://" + os.path.abspath(src)
        await pg.goto(url + "#home"); await pg.wait_for_timeout(3000)
        ids = await pg.evaluate("""() => { const s=new Set();
          for (const k of ['FSA_DATA']) {}
          document.querySelectorAll('a[href^="#t/"]').forEach(a=>s.add(a.getAttribute('href').slice(3)));
          return [...s]; }""")
        try:
            ids2 = await pg.evaluate("() => { const o=[]; (window.FS&&FS.units||[]).forEach(u=>(u.topics||[]).forEach(t=>o.push(String(t.no||t.id||t.n)))); return o; }")
        except Exception: ids2 = []
        if len(ids2) > len(ids): ids = ids2
        if len(ids) < 100:
            raw = open(src, encoding="utf-8").read()
            ids = sorted(set(re.findall(r'#t/([A-Za-z0-9.\-]+)', raw)))
        print("routes", len(ids), flush=True)
        ids = ids[LO:HI]
        for i, tid in enumerate(ids):
            errs.clear()
            await pg.evaluate("h => { location.hash = h; }", "#t/" + tid)
            await pg.wait_for_timeout(700)
            try:
                await pg.evaluate("() => (window.MathJax && MathJax.startup && MathJax.startup.promise) ? MathJax.startup.promise.then(()=>MathJax.typesetPromise ? MathJax.typesetPromise() : 0) : 0")
            except Exception as e:
                errs.append("typeset:" + str(e)[:120])
            r = await pg.evaluate("""() => {
              const m=document.querySelector('#main'); if(!m) return {t:'',merr:[]};
              const merr=[...m.querySelectorAll('mjx-merror, .MathJax_Error, [data-mjx-error]')].map(e=>(e.getAttribute('data-mjx-error')||e.textContent).slice(0,140));
              const c=m.cloneNode(true); c.querySelectorAll('script,style,code,pre,textarea,mjx-container,.MathJax,mjx-assistive-mml').forEach(x=>x.remove());
              return {t:c.innerText, merr, title:(m.querySelector('h1,h2')||{}).innerText||''};}""")
            raw_hits = [r["t"][max(0, m.start()-50):m.end()+50].replace("\n", " ") for m in RAW.finditer(r["t"])][:6]
            res.append(dict(id=tid, title=r.get("title", ""), merr=r["merr"], raw=raw_hits, js=list(errs), chars=len(r["t"])))
            if i % 20 == 0: print(i, tid, flush=True); json.dump(res, open(out, "w"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
        await b.close()
    json.dump(res, open(out, "w"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
    bad = [x for x in res if x["merr"] or x["raw"] or x["js"]]
    print("DONE", len(res), "routes; with issues:", len(bad), flush=True)
asyncio.run(main())

========== END FILE: ws/tools/sweep_math_v108.py ==========

========== FILE: ws/tools/ts_data.py ==========

"""E5 Time Series — synthetic datasets, every computed number, and Plotly figures.

All data are SYNTHETIC (fixed seeds) and labelled so on the site, consistent with the rest of FlippedStat.
Methods follow Think Stats 3e, Chapter 12 (Downey; code MIT): classical seasonal decomposition,
linear/quadratic trend forecasts, year-over-year differencing, autoregression by OLS, the MA step on
residuals, retrodiction by integration, and SARIMA via statsmodels.
Output: build/e5_data.json  (datasets, numbers, figures). Run: python tools/ts_data.py
"""
import json, warnings
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import statsmodels.tsa.api as tsa
from statsmodels.tsa.seasonal import seasonal_decompose
from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import acf
from statsmodels.stats.diagnostic import acorr_ljungbox
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

N = {}          # every number quoted on the site
FIG = {}        # Plotly figures (FS.figs format: data, layout, alt, cap)
C = dict(a='#1f6f8b', t='#d9822b', p='#2e8b57', m='#7a7a7a', r='#b8336a', g='#9aa5b1')
r3 = lambda x: float(round(float(x), 3))
r2 = lambda x: float(round(float(x), 2))
r1 = lambda x: float(round(float(x), 1))

def dstr(idx): return [d.strftime('%Y-%m') for d in idx]
def tr(x, y, name, col, dash=None, width=1.6, mode='lines'):
    t = dict(type='scatter', mode=mode, x=list(x), y=[None if (v is None or (isinstance(v, float) and np.isnan(v))) else r2(v) for v in y], name=name, line=dict(color=col, width=width))
    if dash: t['line']['dash'] = dash
    return t
def lay(ytitle, xtitle='', h=320, **k):
    L = dict(height=h, margin=dict(l=60, r=16, t=16, b=48), yaxis=dict(title=ytitle), xaxis=dict(title=xtitle), legend=dict(orientation='h', y=-0.22))
    L.update(k); return L
def fig(key, data, layout, alt, cap): FIG[key] = dict(data=data, layout=layout, alt=alt, cap=cap)
def mape(f, a): return float(np.mean(np.abs(f - a) / a) * 100)
def mae(f, a): return float(np.mean(np.abs(f - a)))
def rmse(f, a): return float(np.sqrt(np.mean((f - a) ** 2)))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ dataset A: Harbourside electricity demand
rng = np.random.default_rng(20261117)
idxA = pd.date_range('2006-01', periods=19 * 12, freq='ME')       # Jan 2006 – Dec 2024, 228 months
t = np.arange(len(idxA))
season_shape = np.array([-310, -360, -250, -60, 170, 330, 420, 440, 330, 140, -60, -240])  # GWh; summer air-conditioning peak
season_shape = season_shape - season_shape.mean()
trendA = 3150 + 4.2 * t - 0.004 * t ** 2
e = np.zeros(len(t)); w = rng.normal(0, 55, len(t))
for i in range(len(t)): e[i] = (0.55 * e[i - 1] if i else 0) + w[i]
breakA = np.where(idxA >= pd.Timestamp('2020-02-01'), -150.0, 0.0)          # level shift from Feb 2020 (synthetic)
breakA = np.where((idxA >= pd.Timestamp('2020-02-01')) & (idxA < pd.Timestamp('2020-07-01')), -260.0, breakA)
A = pd.Series(np.round(trendA + season_shape[idxA.month - 1] + e + breakA, 0), index=idxA, name='demand_gwh')
N['A_n'] = len(A); N['A_start'] = '2006-01'; N['A_end'] = '2024-12'
N['A_mean'] = r1(A.mean()); N['A_min'] = int(A.min()); N['A_max'] = int(A.max())
N['A_maxmonth'] = A.idxmax().strftime('%b %Y'); N['A_minmonth'] = A.idxmin().strftime('%b %Y')

# moving averages
ma12 = A.rolling(12).mean(); cma = A.rolling(12, center=True).mean()
N['A_ma_first'] = A.index[11].strftime('%b %Y'); N['A_ma_lost'] = 11
fig('e5series', [tr(dstr(A.index), A.values, 'monthly demand', C['a'], width=1.2)],
    lay('GWh', 'month'), 'Line chart of monthly electricity demand in synthetic Harbourside, 2006 to 2024: rising, with a summer peak every year and a dip in 2020.',
    f'Synthetic Harbourside demand, {N["A_n"]} months. Every year peaks in July–August; the series rises; 2020 drops below the pattern.')
fig('e5ma', [tr(dstr(A.index), A.values, 'monthly demand', C['g'], width=1), tr(dstr(A.index), ma12.values, 'trailing 12-month mean', C['t'], width=2.2),
             tr(dstr(A.index), cma.values, 'centred 12-month mean', C['p'], 'dot', 2.2)],
    lay('GWh', 'month'), 'Monthly demand with a trailing and a centred 12-month moving average; the trailing curve lags behind the centred one.',
    'The trailing mean (orange) uses the last 12 months only, so it lags; the centred mean (green) uses six months on each side — including the future.')

# additive decomposition (classical; same algorithm as R decompose())
dA = seasonal_decompose(A, model='additive', period=12)
trA, seA, reA = dA.trend, dA.seasonal, dA.resid
N['A_R2_decomp'] = r3(1 - reA.var() / A.var())
mon = seA.groupby(seA.index.month).mean()
N['A_season'] = {int(k): r1(v) for k, v in mon.items()}
N['A_season_peak'] = r1(mon.max()); N['A_season_low'] = r1(mon.min())
det = (A - ma12).dropna(); monthly_raw = det.groupby(det.index.month).mean()
N['A_detr_aug'] = r1(monthly_raw[8]); N['A_detr_feb'] = r1(monthly_raw[2])
N['A_resid_sd'] = r1(reA.std())
# hand version with the trailing mean (Think Stats' first pass) for comparison
seas_hand = monthly_raw[A.index.month].values; exp_hand = ma12.values + seas_hand
res_hand = A.values - exp_hand
N['A_R2_hand'] = r3(1 - np.nanvar(res_hand, ddof=1) / A.var())
mlab = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec']
fig('e5season', [dict(type='bar', x=mlab, y=[r1(mon[m]) for m in range(1, 13)], marker=dict(color=C['a']), name='seasonal effect')],
    lay('GWh above / below trend', 'calendar month', 300), 'Bar chart of the additive seasonal component: negative in winter months, largest positive values in July and August.',
    f'Seasonal component (additive): Aug {N["A_season"][8]:+} GWh, Feb {N["A_season"][2]:+} GWh. The twelve effects sum to zero.')
xs = dstr(A.index)
FIG['e5decomp'] = dict(data=[
    dict(type='scatter', mode='lines', x=xs, y=[r1(v) for v in A], name='observed', line=dict(color=C['a'], width=1), xaxis='x', yaxis='y'),
    dict(type='scatter', mode='lines', x=xs, y=[None if np.isnan(v) else r1(v) for v in trA], name='trend', line=dict(color=C['t'], width=1.6), xaxis='x', yaxis='y2'),
    dict(type='scatter', mode='lines', x=xs, y=[r1(v) for v in seA], name='seasonal', line=dict(color=C['p'], width=1), xaxis='x', yaxis='y3'),
    dict(type='scatter', mode='lines', x=xs, y=[None if np.isnan(v) else r1(v) for v in reA], name='residual', line=dict(color=C['r'], width=1), xaxis='x', yaxis='y4')],
    layout=dict(height=520, margin=dict(l=60, r=16, t=10, b=40), showlegend=False, grid=dict(rows=4, columns=1, pattern='coupled'),
                yaxis=dict(title='observed'), yaxis2=dict(title='trend'), yaxis3=dict(title='seasonal'), yaxis4=dict(title='residual')),
    alt='Four stacked panels: observed series, smooth rising trend with a 2020 dip, a repeating seasonal pattern, and residuals scattered around zero with larger values in 2020.',
    cap=f'Additive decomposition, period 12. Trend + seasonal explain R² = {N["A_R2_decomp"]} of the variance; the 2020 shock lands in the residual and pulls the trend down.')
rr = reA.dropna()
fig('e5resid', [dict(type='histogram', x=[r1(v) for v in rr], nbinsx=30, marker=dict(color=C['r']), name='residual')],
    lay('number of months', 'residual (GWh)', 280), 'Histogram of decomposition residuals: roughly bell-shaped around zero with a few large negative values.',
    f'Residuals: SD {N["A_resid_sd"]} GWh. The far-left months are the 2020 shock — not noise the model should "explain".')

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ forecasting by decomposition (train/test in time order)
H = 36
trn, tst = A.iloc[:-H], A.iloc[-H:]
N['H'] = H; N['test_start'] = tst.index[0].strftime('%b %Y'); N['train_end'] = trn.index[-1].strftime('%b %Y')
dT = seasonal_decompose(trn, model='additive', period=12)
months = np.arange(len(dT.trend)); df = pd.DataFrame({'trend': dT.trend.values, 'months': months}).dropna()
fitT = smf.ols('trend ~ months', data=df).fit()
N['trend_b0'] = r1(fitT.params['Intercept']); N['trend_b1'] = r3(fitT.params['months']); N['trend_R2'] = r3(fitT.rsquared)
allm = pd.DataFrame({'months': np.arange(len(A))}); pred_trend = pd.Series(fitT.predict(allm).values, index=A.index)
mavg = dT.seasonal.groupby(dT.seasonal.index.month).mean(); pred_seas = pd.Series(mavg[A.index.month].values, index=A.index)
predD = pred_trend + pred_seas
fD = predD[tst.index]
snaive = pd.Series(A.shift(12)[tst.index].values, index=tst.index)  # last year's same month (uses only past)
# multi-step seasonal naive must repeat the last observed year, not peek: use last 12 training months repeated
last = trn.iloc[-12:].values; sn = pd.Series(np.tile(last, H // 12), index=tst.index)
naive = pd.Series(np.repeat(trn.iloc[-1], H), index=tst.index)
meanf = pd.Series(np.repeat(trn.mean(), H), index=tst.index)
for k, f in [('naive', naive), ('mean', meanf), ('snaive', sn), ('decomp', fD)]:
    N[f'mape_{k}'] = r2(mape(f.values, tst.values)); N[f'mae_{k}'] = r1(mae(f.values, tst.values)); N[f'rmse_{k}'] = r1(rmse(f.values, tst.values))
# in-sample (retrodiction) error of the same decomposition model on the training data — the number the audit lab exposes
ins = predD[trn.index]
N['mape_decomp_insample'] = r2(mape(ins.values, trn.values))
# decomposition fitted on ALL data incl. test (the peeking version) and its "accuracy" on the last 36 months
dAll = seasonal_decompose(A, model='additive', period=12, extrapolate_trend='freq')
peek = dAll.trend + dAll.seasonal
N['mape_peek'] = r2(mape(peek[tst.index].values, tst.values))
fig('e5split', [tr(dstr(trn.index), trn.values, 'training', C['a'], width=1.2), tr(dstr(tst.index), tst.values, 'test (held back)', C['r'], width=1.2)],
    lay('GWh', 'month', shapes=[dict(type='line', x0=dstr(tst.index)[0], x1=dstr(tst.index)[0], y0=0, y1=1, yref='paper', line=dict(dash='dash', color='#555'))]),
    'Series split by a vertical dashed line: the earlier training part in blue and the final 36 months in red as the held-back test set.',
    f'Split in time order: train to {N["train_end"]}, test the last {H} months from {N["test_start"]}. Never shuffle months.')
fig('e5fc', [tr(dstr(tst.index), tst.values, 'actual', C['a'], width=1.6), tr(dstr(tst.index), fD.values, 'decomposition forecast', C['p'], 'dot', 2),
             tr(dstr(tst.index), sn.values, 'seasonal naive', C['t'], 'dash', 1.6)],
    lay('GWh', 'month'), 'Actual test-period demand with two forecasts: decomposition with a linear trend, and the seasonal naive repeat of the last training year.',
    f'Test MAPE: decomposition {N["mape_decomp"]}%, seasonal naive {N["mape_snaive"]}%, naive {N["mape_naive"]}%, mean {N["mape_mean"]}%.')

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ dataset B: rooftop solar (multiplicative)
rngB = np.random.default_rng(714)
idxB = pd.date_range('2014-01', periods=11 * 12, freq='ME'); tb = np.arange(len(idxB))
sunB = np.array([0.72, 0.70, 0.78, 0.86, 1.05, 1.08, 1.25, 1.22, 1.15, 1.10, 0.97, 0.80]); sunB = sunB / sunB.mean()
levelB = 18 + 0.35 * tb + 0.0105 * tb ** 2
B = pd.Series(np.round(levelB * sunB[idxB.month - 1] * np.exp(rngB.normal(0, 0.035, len(tb))), 1), index=idxB, name='solar_gwh')
N['B_n'] = len(B); N['B_first_year_mean'] = r1(B.iloc[:12].mean()); N['B_last_year_mean'] = r1(B.iloc[-12:].mean())
N['B_growth'] = r1(B.iloc[-12:].mean() / B.iloc[:12].mean())
amp_first = B.iloc[:12].max() - B.iloc[:12].min(); amp_last = B.iloc[-12:].max() - B.iloc[-12:].min()
N['B_amp_first'] = r1(amp_first); N['B_amp_last'] = r1(amp_last)
HB = 36; trB, teB = B.iloc[:-HB], B.iloc[-HB:]
dBm = seasonal_decompose(trB, model='multiplicative', period=12); dBa = seasonal_decompose(trB, model='additive', period=12)
N['B_R2_mult'] = r3(1 - (trB - dBm.trend * dBm.seasonal).var() / trB.var())
N['B_seas_max'] = r1((dBm.seasonal.max() - 1) * 100); N['B_seas_min'] = r1((dBm.seasonal.min() - 1) * 100)
N['B_resid_pct'] = r1(np.nanpercentile(np.abs(dBm.resid.dropna() - 1) * 100, 95))
mB = np.arange(len(dBm.trend)); dfB = pd.DataFrame({'trend': dBm.trend.values, 'months': mB}).dropna()
qB = smf.ols('trend ~ months + I(months**2)', data=dfB).fit(); lB = smf.ols('trend ~ months', data=dfB).fit()
N['B_quad_R2'] = r3(qB.rsquared); N['B_lin_R2'] = r3(lB.rsquared); N['B_quad_p2'] = qB.pvalues['I(months ** 2)']
N['B_quad_p2_txt'] = '< 0.001' if N['B_quad_p2'] < 0.001 else f'{N["B_quad_p2"]:.3f}'
allB = pd.DataFrame({'months': np.arange(len(B))})
sm_ = dBm.seasonal.groupby(dBm.seasonal.index.month).mean(); sa_ = dBa.seasonal.groupby(dBa.seasonal.index.month).mean()
pBm = pd.Series(qB.predict(allB).values, index=B.index) * sm_[B.index.month].values
pBl = pd.Series(lB.predict(allB).values, index=B.index) * sm_[B.index.month].values
qBa = smf.ols('trend ~ months + I(months**2)', data=pd.DataFrame({'trend': dBa.trend.values, 'months': mB}).dropna()).fit()
pBa = pd.Series(qBa.predict(allB).values, index=B.index) + sa_[B.index.month].values
N['B_mape_mult_quad'] = r2(mape(pBm[teB.index].values, teB.values)); N['B_mape_mult_lin'] = r2(mape(pBl[teB.index].values, teB.values))
N['B_mape_add_quad'] = r2(mape(pBa[teB.index].values, teB.values))
logB = np.log(trB); dlog = seasonal_decompose(logB, model='additive', period=12)
N['B_log_seas_aug'] = r3(dlog.seasonal.groupby(dlog.seasonal.index.month).mean()[7]); N['B_log_seas_aug_pct'] = r1((np.exp(N['B_log_seas_aug']) - 1) * 100)
fig('e5solar', [tr(dstr(B.index), B.values, 'rooftop solar', C['t'], width=1.3)], lay('GWh', 'month'),
    'Rooftop solar generation 2014 to 2024: strongly rising and the summer–winter swing grows as the level grows.',
    f'Synthetic rooftop solar. Seasonal swing in 2014: {N["B_amp_first"]} GWh; in 2024: {N["B_amp_last"]} GWh. A growing swing signals a multiplicative pattern.')
fig('e5solarfc', [tr(dstr(B.index), B.values, 'actual', C['a'], width=1.2), tr(dstr(B.index), pBm.values, 'multiplicative + quadratic trend', C['p'], 'dot', 2),
                  tr(dstr(B.index), pBa.values, 'additive + quadratic trend', C['r'], 'dash', 1.4)],
    lay('GWh', 'month', shapes=[dict(type='line', x0=dstr(teB.index)[0], x1=dstr(teB.index)[0], y0=0, y1=1, yref='paper', line=dict(dash='dash', color='#555'))]),
    'Rooftop solar with retrodictions and 36-month forecasts from a multiplicative model and an additive model, both with quadratic trends.',
    f'Test MAPE: multiplicative {N["B_mape_mult_quad"]}%, additive {N["B_mape_add_quad"]}% (both quadratic trend). Multiplicative with a straight-line trend: {N["B_mape_mult_lin"]}%.')

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ autocorrelation, YoY differences, AR, MA, retrodiction, SARIMA (on A)
diff = (A - A.shift(12)).dropna()
N['diff_sd'] = r1(diff.std()); N['A_sd'] = r1(A.std())
dfar = pd.DataFrame({'diff': diff})
for lag in [1, 2, 3]: dfar[f'lag{lag}'] = diff.shift(lag)
dfar = dfar.dropna()
cors = dfar.corr()['diff']
N['ac1'] = r3(cors['lag1']); N['ac2'] = r3(cors['lag2']); N['ac3'] = r3(cors['lag3'])
ar = smf.ols('diff ~ lag1 + lag2 + lag3', data=dfar).fit()
N['ar_coef'] = {k: r3(v) for k, v in ar.params.items()}; N['ar_p'] = {k: float(v) for k, v in ar.pvalues.items()}
pred_ar = ar.predict(dfar); resid_ar = (diff - pred_ar).dropna()
N['ar_R2'] = r3(1 - resid_ar.var() / diff.var())
dfma = pd.DataFrame({'resid': resid_ar})
for lag in [1, 6]: dfma[f'lag{lag}'] = resid_ar.shift(lag)
dfma = dfma.dropna(); maf = smf.ols('resid ~ lag1 + lag6', data=dfma).fit()
N['ma_R2'] = r3(maf.rsquared); N['ma_p1'] = float(maf.pvalues['lag1']); N['ma_p6'] = float(maf.pvalues['lag6'])
pred_ma = maf.predict(dfma); pred_diff = (pred_ar + pred_ma)
N['arma_R2'] = r3(1 - (diff - pred_diff).dropna().var() / diff.var())
pdiff = pd.Series(pred_diff, index=A.index); nmiss = int(pdiff.isna().sum()); N['n_missing'] = nmiss
ps = pd.Series(index=A.index, dtype=float); ps.iloc[:nmiss] = A.iloc[:nmiss]
for i in range(nmiss, len(ps)): ps.iloc[i] = ps.iloc[i - 12] + pdiff.iloc[i]
ps[:nmiss] = np.nan
N['retro_R2'] = r3(1 - (A - ps).dropna().var() / A.var())
lags = list(range(0, 37))
acf_raw = acf(A, nlags=36); acf_diff = acf(diff, nlags=36); acf_res = acf(rr, nlags=36)
N['acf_raw_12'] = r3(acf_raw[12]); N['acf_raw_6'] = r3(acf_raw[6]); N['acf_diff_1'] = r3(acf_diff[1]); N['acf_diff_12'] = r3(acf_diff[12])
N['acf_band_diff'] = r3(2 / np.sqrt(len(diff))); N['acf_band_raw'] = r3(2 / np.sqrt(len(A)))
def acfbars(v, n, col):
    b = 2 / np.sqrt(n)
    return [dict(type='bar', x=lags[1:], y=[r3(x) for x in v[1:]], marker=dict(color=col), name='autocorrelation'),
            dict(type='scatter', mode='lines', x=[0.5, 36.5], y=[b, b], line=dict(color='#555', dash='dash', width=1), name='±2/√n'),
            dict(type='scatter', mode='lines', x=[0.5, 36.5], y=[-b, -b], line=dict(color='#555', dash='dash', width=1), showlegend=False)]
fig('e5acfraw', acfbars(acf_raw, len(A), C['a']), lay('autocorrelation', 'lag (months)', 290, yaxis=dict(title='autocorrelation', range=[-1, 1])),
    'Autocorrelation bars of the raw demand series for lags 1 to 36: large and positive, with peaks at 12, 24 and 36.',
    f'Raw series: lag 12 r = {N["acf_raw_12"]}, lag 6 r = {N["acf_raw_6"]}. Trend and season dominate; the bars barely fall inside the dashed band.')
fig('e5acfdiff', acfbars(acf_diff, len(diff), C['p']), lay('autocorrelation', 'lag (months)', 290, yaxis=dict(title='autocorrelation', range=[-1, 1])),
    'Autocorrelation bars of year-over-year differences: positive and decaying over the first few lags, then a negative spike at lag 12.',
    f'Year-over-year differences: lag 1 r = {N["acf_diff_1"]}, lag 12 r = {N["acf_diff_12"]}. Short-lag memory remains — that is what the AR part models.')
fig('e5yoy', [tr(dstr(diff.index), diff.values, 'A(t) − A(t−12)', C['p'], width=1.2), tr(dstr(diff.index), pred_ar.reindex(diff.index).values, 'AR(3) retrodiction', C['t'], 'dot', 1.6)],
    lay('GWh', 'month'), 'Year-over-year differences in demand with the AR(3) model retrodictions overlaid.',
    f'Differences have SD {N["diff_sd"]} GWh versus {N["A_sd"]} for the raw series. AR(3) explains R² = {N["ar_R2"]} of their variance.')
fig('e5retro', [tr(dstr(A.index), A.values, 'actual', C['a'], width=1.1), tr(dstr(A.index), ps.values, 'retrodiction (integrated)', C['t'], 'dot', 1.8)],
    lay('GWh', 'month'), 'Actual demand with retrodictions rebuilt by adding predicted year-over-year differences to the value twelve months earlier.',
    f'Integrated retrodictions: R² = {N["retro_R2"]}; the first {nmiss} months cannot be predicted and are left blank.')

order = ([1, 2, 3], 0, [1, 6]); sorder = (0, 1, 0, 12)
fitS = tsa.ARIMA(A, order=order, seasonal_order=sorder).fit()
fv = fitS.fittedvalues[nmiss:]
N['sarima_R2'] = r3(1 - (fv - A[nmiss:]).var() / A[nmiss:].var()); N['sarima_sigma2'] = r1(fitS.params['sigma2'])
N['sarima_params'] = {k: r3(v) for k, v in fitS.params.items()}
lb = acorr_ljungbox(fitS.resid[nmiss:], lags=[12], return_df=True); N['lb_p12'] = r3(lb['lb_pvalue'].iloc[0])
fitT2 = tsa.ARIMA(trn, order=order, seasonal_order=sorder).fit()
fc = fitT2.get_forecast(steps=H); fm = fc.predicted_mean; ci = fc.conf_int(alpha=0.05); ci.columns = ['lo', 'hi']
N['mape_sarima'] = r2(mape(fm.values, tst.values)); N['mae_sarima'] = r1(mae(fm.values, tst.values)); N['rmse_sarima'] = r1(rmse(fm.values, tst.values))
N['cover95'] = int(((tst >= ci.lo) & (tst <= ci.hi)).sum()); N['cover95_pct'] = r1(100 * N['cover95'] / H)
N['ci_w1'] = r1(ci.hi.iloc[0] - ci.lo.iloc[0]); N['ci_w36'] = r1(ci.hi.iloc[-1] - ci.lo.iloc[-1])
# a simpler alternative: seasonal ARIMA(1,0,0)(0,1,1)12 and AIC comparison
alt = tsa.ARIMA(trn, order=(1, 0, 0), seasonal_order=(0, 1, 1, 12)).fit()
N['aic_main'] = r1(fitT2.aic); N['aic_alt'] = r1(alt.aic)
N['lb_p12_alt'] = r3(acorr_ljungbox(alt.resid[13:], lags=[12], return_df=True)['lb_pvalue'].iloc[0])
N['lb_p12_main_train'] = r3(acorr_ljungbox(fitT2.resid[21:], lags=[12], return_df=True)['lb_pvalue'].iloc[0])
N['alt_params'] = {k: r3(v) for k, v in alt.params.items()}
fa_ci = alt.get_forecast(steps=H).conf_int(alpha=0.05); N['cover95_alt'] = int(((tst >= fa_ci.iloc[:,0]) & (tst <= fa_ci.iloc[:,1])).sum()); N['ci_w1_alt'] = r1(fa_ci.iloc[0,1]-fa_ci.iloc[0,0]); N['ci_w36_alt'] = r1(fa_ci.iloc[-1,1]-fa_ci.iloc[-1,0])
fa = alt.get_forecast(steps=H).predicted_mean; N['mape_alt'] = r2(mape(fa.values, tst.values))
fig('e5sarimafc', [dict(type='scatter', mode='lines', x=dstr(ci.index) + dstr(ci.index)[::-1], y=[r1(v) for v in ci.hi] + [r1(v) for v in ci.lo[::-1]], fill='toself',
                        fillcolor='rgba(154,165,177,0.35)', line=dict(width=0), name='95% interval'),
                   tr(dstr(trn.index[-48:]), trn.values[-48:], 'training (last 4 years)', C['a'], width=1.2), tr(dstr(tst.index), tst.values, 'actual (test)', C['r'], width=1.4),
                   tr(dstr(fm.index), fm.values, 'SARIMA forecast', C['p'], 'dot', 2)],
    lay('GWh', 'month'), 'SARIMA forecast for the 36 test months with a grey 95 percent interval that widens with the horizon, against actual test values.',
    f'SARIMA test MAPE {N["mape_sarima"]}%; {N["cover95"]} of {H} actual months fall inside the 95% interval. Interval width grows from {N["ci_w1"]} to {N["ci_w36"]} GWh.')

# rolling origin: 1-month-ahead and 12-month-ahead errors from origins Dec 2017 … Dec 2023 (seasonal naive vs SARIMA(1,0,0)(0,1,1))
orig = [o for o in range(len(A) - 84, len(A) - 12, 6)]
roll = []
for o in orig:
    tr_ = A.iloc[:o]; te_ = A.iloc[o:o + 12]
    m = tsa.ARIMA(tr_, order=(1, 0, 0), seasonal_order=(0, 1, 1, 12)).fit()
    f = m.get_forecast(12).predicted_mean.values; s = np.tile(tr_.iloc[-12:].values, 1)
    roll.append(dict(origin=tr_.index[-1].strftime('%Y-%m'), sarima=r2(mape(f, te_.values)), snaive=r2(mape(s, te_.values))))
N['roll'] = roll; N['roll_n'] = len(roll)
N['roll_sarima_mean'] = r2(np.mean([x['sarima'] for x in roll])); N['roll_snaive_mean'] = r2(np.mean([x['snaive'] for x in roll]))
N['roll_sarima_wins'] = sum(x['sarima'] < x['snaive'] for x in roll)
fig('e5roll', [dict(type='bar', x=[x['origin'] for x in roll], y=[x['snaive'] for x in roll], name='seasonal naive', marker=dict(color=C['t'])),
               dict(type='bar', x=[x['origin'] for x in roll], y=[x['sarima'] for x in roll], name='SARIMA(1,0,0)(0,1,1)₁₂', marker=dict(color=C['p']))],
    lay('12-month MAPE (%)', 'forecast origin (last month of training data)', 300, barmode='group'),
    'Grouped bars of 12-month-ahead MAPE from several forecast origins, comparing seasonal naive with a SARIMA model.',
    f'Rolling origin: {N["roll_n"]} origins. Mean MAPE: SARIMA {N["roll_sarima_mean"]}%, seasonal naive {N["roll_snaive_mean"]}%. Origins spanning 2020 are the worst for both.')

# spurious correlation: two independent random walks
rs = np.random.default_rng(99); w1 = np.cumsum(rs.normal(0, 1, 200)); w2 = np.cumsum(rs.normal(0, 1, 200))
N['spur_r'] = r3(np.corrcoef(w1, w2)[0, 1]); N['spur_rdiff'] = r3(np.corrcoef(np.diff(w1), np.diff(w2))[0, 1])
cnt = 0; rng2 = np.random.default_rng(7)
for _ in range(1000):
    a_ = np.cumsum(rng2.normal(size=200)); b_ = np.cumsum(rng2.normal(size=200))
    cnt += abs(np.corrcoef(a_, b_)[0, 1]) > 0.5
N['spur_share05'] = r1(cnt / 10)
fig('e5spur', [tr(list(range(200)), w1, 'walk 1', C['a']), tr(list(range(200)), w2, 'walk 2', C['t'])], lay('value', 'time', 280),
    'Two independent random walks drifting over 200 steps.',
    f'Two unrelated random walks: r = {N["spur_r"]}. Their step-to-step changes: r = {N["spur_rdiff"]}. In 1,000 simulated pairs, {N["spur_share05"]}% had |r| > 0.5.')

# audit lab figure (peeking vs honest)
fig('e5audit', [dict(type='bar', x=['AI: in-sample fit<br>(training months)', 'AI: decomposition on all data<br>(test months included)', 'Honest: forecast from<br>training only', 'Seasonal naive<br>baseline'],
                     y=[N['mape_decomp_insample'], N['mape_peek'], N['mape_decomp'], N['mape_snaive']], marker=dict(color=[C['r'], C['r'], C['p'], C['t']]))],
    lay('MAPE on the evaluated months (%)', '', 320), 'Bar chart comparing error when the model sees the evaluated months with error on genuinely held-out months.',
    f'The AI\'s "{N["mape_peek"]}% error" came from a decomposition that had already seen the test months. Honest holdout: {N["mape_decomp"]}%; seasonal naive: {N["mape_snaive"]}%.')

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ dataset C: Harbourside temperature (exercise analogue of Think Stats 12.1)
rngC = np.random.default_rng(1950)
idxC = pd.date_range('1995-01', periods=30 * 12, freq='ME'); tc = np.arange(len(idxC))
seasC = np.array([16.3, 16.9, 19.0, 22.6, 25.8, 27.9, 28.8, 28.6, 27.7, 25.4, 21.8, 17.9]) - 23.24
Cser = pd.Series(np.round(23.24 + seasC[idxC.month - 1] + 0.0021 * tc + rngC.normal(0, 0.55, len(tc)), 2), index=idxC, name='temp_c')

ciC = fc_.conf_int().loc['months'] * 12; N['C_slope_ci'] = [r3(ciC[0]), r3(ciC[1])]
N['C_true_year'] = r3(0.0021 * 12); N['C_R2'] = r3(1 - dC.resid.var() / Cser.var())
# naive (autocorrelation-ignoring) SE versus the trend points' strong serial correlation

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ dataset D: harbour water consumption (exercise analogue of 12.3) — generated from a SARIMA process
rngD = np.random.default_rng(31)
idxD = pd.date_range('2008-01', periods=17 * 12, freq='ME')

res = []
for o in [(1, 0, 0), (2, 0, 0), (1, 0, 1), (2, 0, 1), ([1, 2, 3], 0, [1, 6])]:
    m = tsa.ARIMA(Dser, order=o, seasonal_order=(0, 1, 0, 12)).fit()
    fvD = m.fittedvalues[24:]; R2 = 1 - (fvD - Dser[24:]).var() / Dser[24:].var()

N['D_true_ar'] = 0.6; N['D_true_ma'] = 0.3; N['D_est'] = {k: r3(v) for k, v in mD.params.items()}

"""Stage 3g: render every registered widget (FSW.W) in isolation; report errors and empty output. Output logs/widgets_v9.4.txt"""
import sys, asyncio, pathlib
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
HTML = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'build/FlippedStat_v9.4_standalone.html'
async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        b = await p.chromium.launch(executable_path='/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1228/chrome-linux64/chrome')
        pg = await b.new_page(viewport={'width': 1100, 'height': 900}); errs = []
        pg.on('pageerror', lambda e: errs.append(str(e)))
        await pg.goto(pathlib.Path(HTML).resolve().as_uri(), timeout=180000); await pg.wait_for_timeout(3500)
        await pg.evaluate("location.hash='#t/1.2'"); await pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        res = await pg.evaluate("""async () => { const W = window.FSW.W, out = [];
          for (const k of Object.keys(W)) { const h = document.createElement('div'); h.className = 'widget'; document.querySelector('#main').appendChild(h); let err = '';
            try { const r = W[k](h, { topic: '1.2', sort: (FS.lessons['1.2.1']||{}).sort }); if (r && r.then) await r; } catch (e) { err = String(e).slice(0, 120); }
            await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 60));
            out.push([k, err, h.querySelectorAll('svg, canvas, .plotly-host, table, input, button, select').length, h.innerText.length,
              /NaN|undefined|Infinity/.test(h.innerText) ? 'BADTEXT' : '']); h.remove(); } return out; }""")
        await b.close()
    bad = [r for r in res if r[1] or (r[2] == 0 and r[3] < 20) or r[4]]
    lines = [f"{'FAIL' if r in bad else 'ok'}\t{r[0]}\tcontrols/graphics {r[2]}\ttext {r[3]}\t{r[4]}\t{r[1]}" for r in res]
    open('logs/widgets_v9.4.txt', 'w').write(f'Widget rendering check: {len(res)} widgets, {len(bad)} failing (page errors during run: {len(errs)})\n' + '\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
    print(len(res), 'widgets;', len(bad), 'failing'); [print(l) for l in lines if l.startswith('FAIL')]; print(errs[:5])
asyncio.run(main())
